# how-things-work

A collection of animated explanations. We use animation to make "invisible principles" visible — how mechanisms transmit motion, how chemical bonds break and form, how life unfolds step by step.

📖 **中文版**: [README.md](./README.md).

## Goals

- **Mechanism first**: the animations reveal principle and causal chains, not polished transitions.
- **Step-by-step**: every principle supports step playback, pause and per-step scrubbing so you can think while watching.
- **Self-contained**: each animation avoids heavy build pipelines and runs as soon as you open it.
- **中英双语 · 双主题**: every page exposes 中文/English and dark/light toggles in the top-right corner; choices persist via `localStorage` (theme follows the system by default).

## Repository layout & adding an animation

The site is published by GitHub Pages (the `/docs` directory of the `main` branch). Animation URLs are unaffected by the repo layout: `…/how-things-work/<topic>/`.

- `docs/<topic>/index.html` — one self-contained folder per animation, one URL per topic
- `docs/index.html` — the homepage, **generated by a script; do not edit by hand**
- `data/topics.json` — the single source of truth for every topic: slug, section, Chinese/English titles and blurbs
- `scripts/homepage.template.html` — homepage chrome (styles, hero, footer, shared script)
- `scripts/build-homepage.mjs` — regenerates the homepage from the manifest: cards, section counts and top quick counts stay in sync automatically
- `scripts/check-sync.mjs` — validates folders ↔ manifest ↔ homepage ↔ README registration

To add an animation: create `docs/<slug>/index.html`, append an entry to `data/topics.json`, run `node scripts/build-homepage.mjs && node scripts/check-sync.mjs`, then register it in the README (`✅ **<slug>/**`). The scripts are dependency-free (Node standard library only).

### Phase 21 deep dives

#### Ball screw: grinding rotation into translation

- **What you see**: a motor spins the threaded shaft while 40 steel balls recirculate through the nut and loop back through the return tube; the efficiency-vs-lead-angle chart shows rolling (ρ≈0.2°) against sliding (ρ≈11.3°); drag the table backwards and the ball screw back-drives instantly — vertical axes need a brake; swap to the sliding screw and, at the same lead, λ<ρ locks solid until you stretch the lead past the friction angle.
- **How to play**: drag speed/lead, switch drive/push/brake/sliding modes, follow the dot on the chart; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?rpm=` `?pitch=` `?drive=` `?push=` `?brake=` `?slide=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Bike derailleur: ten gears from a fingertip

- **What you see**: cadence drives the 48T ring and the golden chain runs its S-path ring → cog → jockey → tension pulley → back; shifting slides the parallelogram and the chain hops onto the neighboring cog; a bigger cog needs more chain, so the cage swings open; coasting, the freehub ratchet clicks while the wheel keeps spinning.
- **How to play**: shift up/down (↑/↓), drag cadence, toggle coast and slow-mo shift, compare the five cogs in the chart; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?gear=` `?cad=` `?coast=` `?slow=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Flywheel & KERS: banking your brakes

- **What you see**: a 24-second scripted loop — cruise, brake, idle, boost; the motor-turned-generator pours 313 kJ of KE into an 8 kg flywheel (steel caps at 48k rpm, overflow goes to heat); the boost hands it back; "brakes only" comparison piles up 910 kJ of heat vs ~60 kJ; overrev pushes the rim past σ=ρv² and it bursts in slow motion; the material slider moves the ceiling between steel/aluminum/carbon fiber.
- **How to play**: scrub the timeline, switch KERS/brakes and materials, press overrev; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?mode=` `?mat=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Defibrillator: not a restart, a global reset

- **What you see**: the myocardium is an excitable 1,700-vertex mesh — in sinus rhythm one wave sweeps the heart every 0.8 s; induce VF and six rogue foci shatter the waves, pump output collapsing to ~10%; charging banks E=½CV² (150 J ≈ 1732 V) and the shock depolarizes everything at once — after the flat window the sinus node leads again; under 70 J re-fibrillates, over 300 J leaves burn marks; shocking a healthy heart triggers R-on-T.
- **How to play**: induce VF → charge → shock; drag the energy slider across the three dose zones; watch the scrolling ECG; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?en=` `?mode=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Blood pressure monitor: two numbers from a squeezed artery

- **What you see**: the cuff inflates past systolic and flattens the brachial artery; bleeding 3 mmHg/s, each pulse peak cracks it open — turbulence knocks Korotkoff sounds and ripples the cuff; the amber envelope peaks at MAP (93) and its shoulders read ~117/79; drag the preset to 150/95 and the whole envelope shifts right.
- **How to play**: press start for the automatic ~30-second cycle, drag systolic/diastolic, watch the gauge and the chart; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?sys=` `?dia=` `?auto=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### 3D printing: slicing a model into sheets, stacking them back

- **What you see**: a chess pawn sliced into 60 layers, the gantry laying perimeter + zigzag infill while the slicer window draws the current section; the ball's underside widens faster than 45° — supports OFF and the strands sag red, supports ON and a yellow scaffold carries them; snap the supports off when done; layer height 0.1/0.2/0.3 mm means 90/60/40 layers.
- **How to play**: drag layer height/infill/speed, toggle supports, reprint; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?lh=` `?infill=` `?pspd=` `?support=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 22 deep dives

#### Tornado: stretching spin out of control

- **What you see**: drag shear past 30% and the whole supercell starts turning, lowering a wall cloud; the updraft stretches the vortex vertically and angular momentum does the rest — 520 debris particles wind into a funnel; past 85% it touches down and grinds up a dust curtain; the v·r≈const hyperbola shows the dot climbing as you stretch; readouts give wind speed, rpm, ΔP≈0.75v² and the EF rating, and at EF3+ the barn roof tears off until you press "fix the barn". "Auto evolve" plays the whole fair → shear → stretch → touchdown life cycle.
- **How to play**: drag shear/stretch, run auto-evolve, fix the barn; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?shear=` `?stretch=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Rain shadow: one mountain, two fates

- **What you see**: a blue parcel climbs from the sea — dry-adiabatic cooling at 9.8 °C/km until the LCL, then condensation and latent heat slow the cooling; the rain all falls windward, dyeing that slope green; past the summit the bone-dry air warms by compression into a foehn, landing +3.7 °C hotter, and the lee slope fades to desert; the T-altitude chart draws both adiabats and the parcel's current state. Raise the mountain past the LCL and rainforest and desert appear together; flip the wind and the shadow swaps sides instantly.
- **How to play**: drag height/dew point, flip the wind, try the Himalaya preset; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?hmt=` `?td=` `?flip=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Benford's law: leading digits live on a log circle

- **What you see**: 171 country populations scattered on a logarithmic cylinder — the angle is set by the mantissa, so everything starting with 1 crowds into one arc; the nine base arcs are the theory log10(1+1/d) and nine colored bars grow out of them; switching datasets (rivers, Fibonacci, powers of 2) keeps the bars on the white line; "×3.7" spins every dot around the cylinder yet the bars land unchanged; "fabricate a book" flattens the digits and χ² blows past 15.5 — rejected.
- **How to play**: six dataset buttons, ×3.7 for scale invariance, fake books for fraud detection; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?ds=` `?pause=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Turing machine: one tape computes everything computable

- **What you see**: a tape receding into the fog, a read-write head, and a highlighted rule table — each step only reads, writes, moves and changes state; three built-in programs give the same machine three identities: unary addition 111+11→11111, binary increment 1011→1100 (a carry wave moving left), and a copier 11#→11#11 (x/y marks track progress); the space-time diagram draws every tape as growth rings; HALT turns the sign green.
- **How to play**: switch the three programs, step once at a time, drag the speed 0.5–20 steps/s, reset anytime; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?p=` `?speed=` `?pause=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 23 deep dives

#### Wing lift: angle of attack is everything

- **What you see**: streamline particles sweep past a NACA airfoil — upper tubes squeeze, speed up and warm; drag the angle slider and the green lift vector stretches with C_L; pull past ~15° and the upper flow separates into chaos, the nose buffets and C_L dives; flaps shift the whole curve up and lower the minimum speed. One-click stall and one-click recovery.
- **How to play**: drag angle/speed, toggle flaps, follow the dot on the C_L-α chart; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?aoa=` `?spd=` `?flap=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Jet engine: making air push you forward

- **What you see**: particles turn blue → white → orange → red as they pass fan, compressor, burner, turbine and nozzle; the twin spools spin at N1/N2; the chart shows pressure and temperature rising through the compressor, peaking in the burner and bleeding through the turbine; switch to a turbofan for the blue bypass stream and a thrust jump; afterburner re-lights the exhaust; the start sequence replays starter → ignition → idle.
- **How to play**: drag throttle/airspeed, toggle turbofan and afterburner, run the start; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?thr=` `?v0=` `?fan=` `?ab=` `?run=` `?start=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Buoyancy & stability: why steel floats and why it capsizes

- **What you see**: a hull cross-section in a tank whose draft follows the cargo (Archimedes solved by bisection); stack containers five high, switch the ballast off, add a storm — GM goes negative, the roll passes the flood angle and she slowly heels to 90°; open the ballast and G drops, GM recovers, and the same storm only rocks her; the GZ=GM·sinθ curve tracks your working point.
- **How to play**: drag cargo/stack, hit a swell or a storm, toggle ballast, reset; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?cargo=` `?stack=` `?ballast=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Terminal velocity: gravity is constant, drag calls the shots

- **What you see**: a skydiver exits at 3,000 m and the speed curve settles onto 55 m/s in about 12 s; at the auto altitude the canopy scales CdA from 0.47 to 50, speed snaps to 5 m/s and a ≈3 g red spike marks the opening shock; the altitude ruler and ground slide up as she descends, ending in a soft touchdown.

### Phase 26 deep dives

#### The siphon: air pressure pushes water over the hill

- **What you see**: two pools, one tube over a dam — the atmosphere (101 kPa) pressing on the upper surface pushes water up and over; past the crest gravity takes over and the drop Δh is the only engine, v = C·√(2gΔh); the crest vacuum gauge reads absolute p = p₀ − ρg·h_c − ½ρv²(1+ζ), with the 10.07 m vapor line ruled on the ruler — hoist the crest past it and the column boils apart at the top, air rushes in, flow dies; pool levels drift (time-lapse) until the drop is spent and the flow stops by itself: no perpetual motion.
- **How to play**: drag crest height and pool drop; press prime, "hoist crest to 11.5 m" (watch the gauge snap), and "level the pools" for the self-stop; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?hc=` `?dh=` `?prime=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### The Magnus effect: a spinning ball bends the wind

- **What you see**: one force, three arenas — ① a spinning cylinder in a wind tunnel: 420 streamline particles tinted by Bernoulli, the side running with the flow turns red (low pressure), the side against it blue (high), the whole wake shoved aside, the red arrow is F = ρUΓ (Kutta–Joukowski); ② the banana kick: sidespin pushes sideways via F ∝ ω×v — the ball is aimed wide of the wall, lateral speed builds, and the arc bends hard back inside the post while the grey ghost, launched identically without spin, sails straight out; ③ the 1925 Buckau rotor ship: Magnus ⟂ apparent wind, decomposed into forward thrust — best on a beam wind, dead downwind it stalls (exactly like a sail).
- **How to play**: switch wind tunnel / banana kick / rotor ship; drag surface speed, sidespin, wind angle; try "perfect curl" and "spin it backwards"; space to play / pause.

#### Cavitation & supercavitation: low pressure tears water open

- **What you see**: ① a propeller in a test tank: raise the rpm and suction-side pressure falls below vapor (2.3 kPa) — bubbles are born at the tips, drift downstream, and collapse in flashes, their micro-jets hammering pits into the blades (a running counter); "dive to 40 m" squeezes the bubbles out of existence; ② the supercavitating torpedo: feed gas and the cavity grows aft from the cavitator into a full shroud — wetted area ≈ 4%, the drag curve switches from red to green, and the same thrust now balances at 85 m/s instead of 37 (the Shkval trick).
- **How to play**: drag rpm & depth (propeller) or thrust (torpedo); press max rpm, dive to 40 m, gas feed, full sprint; read the σ-vs-rpm and drag-vs-speed charts; space to play / pause.

#### Tsunami & shallow-water waves: a jump in the deep, a wall at the beach

- **What you see**: a second-order 1-D shallow-water solver (Lax-Wendroff with wet/dry isolation, time ×60) — the fault slips and lifts the whole column; in 4000 m of water the crest runs at c = √(gh) = 713 km/h while the surface shows a 1–2 m bump (live DART-buoy reading), unfelt aboard ship; onto the shelf the speed falls 713 → 36 km/h and energy-flux conservation piles the height up by Green's law A ∝ h^(-1/4) (measured 1.9 → 2.5 m across the slope); the trough arrives first — "the sea is draining" — then the crest lands and run-up (≈ 4× the shore height) drives water up the beach and over the huts; the side panel tracks η(x), the bathymetry and the Green's-law prediction live.
- **How to play**: drag fault slip and playback speed; press "trigger quake" and "slow-mo ×15"; watch the crest speed fall from 713 km/h to tens and the height climb from 1 m to 10; space to play / pause.

#### Sonic boom & the Mach cone: see first, hear later

#### Exoplanets: a thousandth of the light tells all

- **What you see**: a planet crosses its star on a Kepler ellipse while a photometer watches; the light curve dips by δ = (Rp/R★)² — the radius; Kepler III turns the period into orbital distance and equilibrium temperature against the green habitable-zone ring; the RV mode shows the star wobbling with spectral lines sliding blue-red, K ∝ Mp·sin i/√P giving the mass — with radius, density settles rock vs gas. Drag the inclination past ~89.7° and the transit vanishes: only edge-on orbits are ever detected.
- **How to play**: drag radius / period / inclination / star luminosity; press hot Jupiter / Earth twin (watch the noise) / TRAPPIST-1 / inclination-miss presets; toggle transit / RV modes; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?mode=transit|rv` `?rp=` `?per=` `?inc=` `?lum=` `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Information entropy: the compression limit

- **What you see**: a golden dome is the entropy surface H(p₁,p₂,p₃) — highest at uniform (log₂3 ≈ 1.585 bit), zero at the corners; beside the four probability bars, stacked cubes show the live-rebuilt Huffman codewords — frequent symbols short, rare ones long; a symbol stream encodes into a 0/1 bit ribbon whose counter converges to L̄, hugging H but never crossing (Shannon: L̄ ≥ H, Huffman within 1 bit). Uniform 4 symbols: H = 2 bit, nothing to squeeze; extreme 97/1/1/1: H ≈ 0.24 yet Huffman still needs 1.05.
- **How to play**: drag p(A)/p(B)/p(C) and watch codewords reshape; press uniform / skewed / extreme / English-frequency presets; the H vs L̄ vs fixed-length bars update live; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?pa=` `?pb=` `?pc=` `?preset=` `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Elevator & counterweight: the motor pushes a balance

- **What you see**: a six-floor shaft cross-section — car and concrete counterweight hang off the same grooved traction sheave: gripped by friction, not hooked. At half load with the 50% counterweight, Δm ≈ 0 and cruise power reads ≈ 0 (a green "balanced" tag) — the motor only pays for acceleration and friction; switch to no-counterweight and the same trip glows red; the overspeed test flings the governor weights open, the linkage yanks the wedge safety gear into the rails with a clang, and the oil buffer waits at the pit.
- **How to play**: call floors 1F–6F; drag load (0–1000 kg); switch counterweight 0/40/50%; the chart records the last trip's power curve with its green ≈0 cruise stretch; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?load=` `?cw=` `?floor=` `?mode=` `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 77 · Cross-Family Gap-Fill Batch 47 (16/16 complete)

- [x] Electrical Discharge Machining: Sparking Away the Hardest Steel(Hardened steel that mills and lathes cannot touch yields to EDM - because it cuts with electricity, not force. The tool electrode and workpiece soak together in a dielectric fluid (kerosene or deionized water) while a servo holds their gap at 10-50 μm; every microsecond pulse (1-2000 μs on-time, 1-100 A peak) breaks down the fluid at its thinnest point and strikes a spark channel at 8000-12000 °C, melting and vaporizing a micro-spot of metal. When the pulse ends the bubble collapses, and together with the flushing flow the molten beads are hurled into the fluid, leaving a micron-sized crater on the surface. Discharges repeat up to hundreds of thousands of times per second, and billions of micro-craters pile up into the cavity you need. Hardness means nothing here - conductivity is the only entry ticket: hardened steel and carbide are all fair game, the very edge EDM holds over cutting. The fluid wears four hats: insulator at rest, channel compressor and coolant after breakdown, chip flusher, and deionizer for recovery. Polarity matters: with short pulses (below about 50 μs) the workpiece goes positive and erodes faster; the recast layer is only a few microns thick. The servo retreats the instant it senses a short - never pushing its luck. Wire EDM is the variant: a traveling molybdenum or brass wire becomes the electrode and cuts any contour. Typical figures: surface roughness Ra 0.1-10 μm, removal rates in the mm³/min class. In the demo watch the electrode approach, sparks flash at the thinnest points and craters grow into a cavity; raise the peak current to see craters deepen and the surface roughen; press short-retract to watch the servo lunge back; switch to wire mode to see the wire slice through and drop the piece. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **edm-machining/**

- [x] Gear Undercut and Profile Shift: The Few-Teeth Problem(Why does a hobbing machine not simply carve the tooth shape? Because gears use the generating method: the cutter rack and the blank roll together like a meshing pair, and the envelope of the cutting-edge positions automatically forms an exact involute - change the tooth count and you only change the ratio, not the cutter. But generation has a life-or-death line: the working flank of the tool is tangent to the base circle at the limit point N, and a rack cutter can generate only up to N. With too few teeth (the undercut-free minimum is z_min = 2ha*/sin²α, about 17 teeth at α=20°, ha*=1), the tool tip line crosses N and the corner plows away the freshly generated involute together with root material - undercut: a weakened root and reduced contact ratio. The remedy is profile shift: move the cutter outward by x·m (positive shift), and x ≥ (17−z)/17 avoids undercut while thickening the root and raising bending strength; the price is a pointed tip and a slightly lower contact ratio. Equal shift (x1+x2=0) keeps the center distance and helps match ratios; the angle-modified center distance a′ = a·cosα/cosα′ fits non-standard spacings; shift also balances specific sliding and extends wear life - which is why nearly every gear in a gearbox carries a shift coefficient. In the demo watch the rack stroke and roll with the blank to generate the profile; draw the tip trochoid live and slide the tooth count to 10 to see it dig into the root; pull the shift slider to cure the undercut and fatten the teeth; overlay the standard gear for comparison; press angle-shift center distance to see a 25-tooth mate mesh at a′. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **gear-profile-shift/**

- [x] The pH Meter: A Glass Membrane Reads Acidity(A pH meter measures neither color nor chemical reaction - it measures an electric potential. The tip of a glass electrode is a special-glass membrane only 50-100 μm thick; after soaking, its surface hydrates into a gel layer about 10 nm deep. The gel layers on the two faces exchange Na+/H+ ions with the inner and outer solutions - H+ never actually crosses the glass, yet the interface potential on each side tracks the hydrogen-ion activity of its solution, and the whole membrane obeys the Nernst equation E = E0 - 2.303RT/F × pH: a slope of 59.16 mV/pH at 25 °C, growing with temperature. A sensitive membrane alone makes no circuit: inside sits an inner reference solution of known pH with an Ag/AgCl inner reference; an outer Ag/AgCl reference reaches the sample through a saturated-KCl salt bridge that suppresses the liquid-junction potential - modern combination electrodes merge both into a single stem. Every electrode leaves the factory with its own zero offset (the asymmetry potential), and its slope decays with age, so two-point calibration is mandatory: dip into pH 4.01 then pH 9.18 buffers to pin down slope and zero; temperature changes the slope, corrected automatically by ATC. Strong alkali hides a trap: above pH 12 the glass also responds to Na+ and the reading drifts low - the sodium error. Its trump card is universality: turbid, colored, viscous, oxidizing solutions all read fine - impossible for indicators and test strips; response in seconds, and no sample is consumed. In the demo: drag the pH slider and watch the ion clouds and the mV needle deflect together as the working point slides along the mV-pH line; run the two-point calibration first, then press uncalibrated drift and sodium error to wreck the reading; drag temperature to watch the slope climb. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **ph-glass-electrode/**

- [x] Carbon Fiber & Polymer Composites(A black fiber one-tenth the width of a human hair - why is it stiffer than steel? Carbon fiber starts as white PAN (polyacrylonitrile) precursor and transforms through three heat stages: stabilization at 200-300 °C, where oxygen crosslinks the linear chains into a heat-resistant ladder structure that freezes the stretched orientation - without it, the next furnace would melt the filaments together; carbonization at 1000-1500 °C in inert atmosphere, where non-carbon elements leave as HCN/N2/CO2 and 92-99% carbon remains in a turbostratic graphite structure; optionally graphitization at 2000-3000 °C to align the layers further and raise the modulus. Strength comes from orientation: tension is applied throughout carbonization so the graphite layers align with the fiber axis - each filament is 5-7 μm across with tensile strength 3.5-7 GPa (steel about 1.8 GPa), modulus 230-590 GPa, and a density of only 1.8 g/cm3 (aluminum 2.7, steel 7.9) - specific strength about twelve times steel. But single filaments are fine and brittle, weak in compression and shear, so they are combined with epoxy: the matrix transfers load into the fibers and protects them; the layup is anisotropic and tailored to the load - 0° plies carry tension, ±45° carry shear and torsion, 90° brace transversely; prepreg stacks cure in an autoclave. On fracture, fiber pull-out and delamination absorb large amounts of energy - no glass-like sudden cleavage. The Boeing 787 fuselage is 50% composite by weight; wind blades, bike frames and F1 bodies work the same way. In the demo: on the left a production line from precursor through the stabilization and carbonization ovens to black tow; on the right drag the layup angle 0°/±45°/90° and the load slider to see how deformation and failure differ; press fiber pull-out slow motion to see the composite break without shattering; press furnace history to replay the temperature ladder on the scope. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **carbon-fiber-composite/**

- [x] Sickle Cell & Balanced Polymorphism(Sickle cell disease begins as a single misprint: at codon 6 of the beta-globin gene, GAG becomes GTG, swapping glutamic acid for valine - one base out of three billion, yet a textbook two-sided ledger. Valine's hydrophobic side chain acts as a sticky patch: hidden while oxygen is bound, exposed once hemoglobin gives its oxygen up. Then sticky patch meets the complementary pocket on the next hemoglobin molecule, and the proteins chain into rigid 14-strand fibers that stretch the red cell from a soft disc into a sickle. Sickled cells lose the deformability needed to squeeze through gaps narrower than themselves: at a capillary stenosis they lock into a dam, causing pain crises and organ hypoxia; fragile cells are cleared early by the spleen - a lifespan of about 20 days instead of 120, the homozygote's (HbSS) hemolytic anemia. But the ledger has a second page: where malaria is endemic, heterozygotes (HbAS, sickle trait) carry a red-cell interior hostile to the parasite, and infected cells are cleared by immunity more readily - severe-malaria mortality drops about 90%. Malaria, the strongest selection pressure in human history, therefore pins HbS frequency at a balanced point of 10-20%: homozygous disease is the cost t, heterozygote protection the benefit s, and Hardy-Weinberg supplies the genotype floor p²:2pq:q² beneath an equilibrium p*=s/(s+t) - the quantitative face of balancing selection. Leave malaria behind and the benefit drops to zero while the cost remains: HbS loses its support and slides slowly under genetic drift, while SS patients still pay the full price. In the demo: watch one base build a fiber and bend a disc on the left; tune deoxygenation to jam or clear a capillary in the middle; on the right, set malaria intensity on an 800-person panel, run 50 generations, and open the Hardy-Weinberg overlay to see AS frequency settle at the midpoint or dissolve. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **sickle-cell-malaria/**

- [x] Trophic Cascades & Keystone Species(In 1926 the last wolf of Yellowstone was killed; in 1995 wolves were brought back - and in the 69 years between, the valley changed its face. Without wolves the elk lost their fear and wintered on open valley floors, slowly browsing willow and aspen seedlings bare; once wolves returned, elk no longer dared linger on exposed banks - the ecology of fear: a map of risk decides where to feed. So willow thickets recovered -> banks held, channels stabilized -> songbirds found nesting shrubs -> beavers returned, and beaver dams rebuilt wetlands that raise fish and amphibians and even reshape river form: a predator restraining plants one level removed - top-down control. The counterexamples cut just as sharp: with cougars gone in the eastern US, white-tailed deer boomed and grazed the forest understory into a mowed lawn; off Alaska, fewer sea otters meant a sea-urchin explosion that mowed kelp forests into urchin barrens - otters back, kelp reborn: a tiny share of the biomass with impact far beyond proportion, a keystone species; the intertidal starfish Pisaster holding mussels in check leaves space for a dozen-plus species, same logic. Fretwell's four-level rule: add a level, and the two below it alternate suppression and release. Trophic cascades (top-down) and nutrient driving (bottom-up) are ecology's two master axes. In the demo: drag the wolf count on the left and watch elk time-in-valley, willow cover, beaver dams and species counts respond; drag otters in the middle to swap kelp forest for urchin barren; on the right, press remove the keystone to watch mussels pave the intertidal as species fall from 15 to 3. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **trophic-cascade/**

- [x] Kirchhoff's Circuit Laws: Conservation of Current and Voltage(However tangled a lumped circuit looks, two ledgers plus one law solve it completely. Ledger one, KCL (Kirchhoff's current law): the sum of currents flowing into any node equals the sum flowing out - charge conservation; in steady state a node stockpiles no charge, one ampere in means one ampere out. Ledger two, KVL (Kirchhoff's voltage law): going around any closed loop, the algebraic sum of potential rises and drops is zero - energy conservation; the net electrostatic work on a unit charge after one full lap is zero, otherwise each lap would mint free energy and a wire loop would be a perpetual motion machine. With V=IR the circuit becomes a linear system: the node-voltage method takes node potentials as unknowns, one KCL equation per node yields every branch current - this page solves a live 2x2 system as you watch. Classic applications: series resistors divide voltage in proportion to resistance, V=12·R2/(R1+R2) from a 12 V source; parallel resistors divide current inversely, and an ammeter shunts with a small parallel resistor to extend its range; a Wheatstone bridge balances when R1/R2=R3/R4 so the diagonal galvanometer reads exactly zero - precision resistance measurement, the basis of strain-gauge and thermistor instrumentation. Limits: the lumped approximation demands a circuit much smaller than the signal wavelength; at 3 GHz the wavelength is about 10 cm, traces of that size are already transmission lines, and KVL fails segment by segment. Demo: a 12 V source drives a four-arm bridge; drag any resistor slider and the equations re-solve instantly - particle density = current magnitude, particle speed = current direction, wires colored blue to red by potential; click a node for its KCL ledger, turn on ledger x-ray for the live KVL ledger of every loop, press Wheatstone mode to watch the galvanometer null. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **kirchhoff-laws/**

- [x] The Ising Model: How Little Spins Turn Together(Why does a piece of iron magnetize itself? The Ising model is the minimal answer: put a spin on every lattice site, each taking only ±1, with energy E=−J·Σ⟨ij⟩ s_i·s_j − h·Σs_i - the sum runs over nearest neighbors, and for J>0 aligned neighbors cost less energy (ferromagnetic). Temperature and coupling play tug-of-war: large kT and entropy wins - spins point every way, net magnetization is zero (paramagnetic phase); small kT and energy wins - spins clump into domains that swallow each other into one block, and spontaneous magnetization appears (ferromagnetic phase). The 2D square lattice has an exact solution (Onsager, 1944): critical temperature Tc = 2J/(k·ln(1+√2)) ≈ 2.269 J/k, where susceptibility and specific heat diverge and the correlation length becomes infinite - a continuous phase transition; clusters of every scale, fractal boundaries. Simulation uses Metropolis Monte Carlo: pick a random spin, compute the flip cost ΔE; accept if ΔE≤0 outright, otherwise accept with probability exp(−ΔE/kT) - hotter means more willing to err. Quenching (rapid cooling) freezes the high-temperature mess into a mottled red-blue domain pattern; annealing (slow cooling) gathers it into one large domain. An external field h tips the balance, and sweeping h back and forth below Tc reveals hysteresis - the origin of hard-magnet memory. The same mathematics describes lattice gases, order-disorder in alloys, even Hopfield neural networks - universality: details do not matter, only symmetry and dimension. Demo: 24×24 = 576 two-color cubes evolving live (a flat lattice because the exact solution holds only in 2D, making the comparison rigorous); temperature, field and J sliders act instantly; the scatter plot accumulates (T,|M|) against the Onsager line; try quench, anneal and field flip in sequence. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **ising-model/**

- [x] The Fermi Paradox & Drake Equation(The Milky Way holds some 400 billion stars and 13 billion years of history - so why have we never met a single alien? In 1961 Frank Drake split the count of communicative civilizations into a product of seven terms: N = R*·fp·ne·fl·fi·fc·L - the star-formation rate R* near 1.5-3 stars per year; the planet fraction fp near 1 (Kepler and TESS proved planets outnumber stars); habitable planets per system ne about 0.1-0.4 - the first three terms are pinned down by telescopes; but the chance of life starting fl, of intelligence fi, of detectable technology fc, and the lifetime L of a technological civilization, are all extrapolated from a single sample - Earth - and nobody dares sign that statistics. Feed the optimistic numbers in and N climbs past dozens or hundreds; and even at a leisurely 0.1c with 400-year layovers between hops, a colonization wave floods the galaxy in only 1-10 million years - a thousandth of the galaxy's age. Hence Fermi's 1950 lunchtime question: where is everybody? The mainstream answer is the Great Filter: abiogenesis (chemistry to self-replication is brutally hard), eukaryotic complexity (Earth stalled 2-3 billion years), intelligence, technology, or self-destruction (war, ecology, AI) - the knife either fell behind us (we are exceedingly rare, the road ahead is clear) or waits ahead of us (we are in trouble). Other replies: the zoo hypothesis, dark forest, we-are-early (most of the cosmos' lifetime belongs to the red-dwarf era), and the fact that technosignature windows are naturally short - Earth's omnidirectional radio era lasted only about a century before fiber and directed links, so L may be small by nature. SETI hunts technosignatures (narrowband signals, megastructure transits); since 1960 its only candidate is the 72-second Wow! signal of 1977, never repeated. In the demo, drag the seven equation sliders and watch N and the lit civilization dots in the galaxy respond (with a live log-scale bar); press colonization wave to launch a ripple from one civilization and compare its clock against the galactic age; press Great Filter to move the knife along the chain; press timeline to set 13.8 Gyr beside 100 years. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **fermi-paradox-drake/**

- [x] Vertical Rocket Recovery(The first stage is 60-70% of a rocket\u2019s cost - throwing it away burns an airliner every flight; reuse has a price though: some 3-6% of the propellant must be reserved to fly home, costing 30-40% of the payload. The Falcon-9-style homecoming is a chain of linked steps: after stage separation, cold-gas nitrogen thrusters flip the 40-meter stack 180 degrees, engines forward; then the engines relight in mid-air - a boostback burn bends the trajectory back to the landing zone, or the stage saves that fuel and rides its arc a few hundred kilometers downrange onto a drone ship; the titanium 3D-printed grid fins deploy and keep generating control authority in supersonic flow, holding the center of mass near the thrust vector; next comes the entry burn - three engines retro-propulse while the base heat shield takes the peak heating; finally the landing burn: a rocket with thrust-to-weight above one cannot hover in principle, so it flies a hoverslam - the single center engine deep-throttled to 40-57% of rated thrust on a suicide curve whose deceleration brings velocity to exactly zero at touchdown, with cutoff timing set in milliseconds and the last 2-6 m/s absorbed by the landing legs, all inside a 10-meter navigation circle. Barge landings save the boostback propellant but add tugs and sea-state windows; a single Merlin has flown 20+ missions and refurbishing costs far less than building new - the economics close. In the demo, drag the reserved-propellant slider to read the Δv ledger: too little splashes into the sea, too much eats the payload; switch barge to compare trajectories; drag grid-fin deflection to see landing dispersion; press failure replay to watch an attitude-excursion topple and fireball; the scope traces altitude and speed. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **rocket-recovery/**

- [x] Microfluidics: A Lab on a Fingernail-Sized Chip(Etch a channel down to 10-500 micrometres and the rules of fluid flow are rewritten: the Reynolds number Re=ρvd/μ falls to 0.01-100, viscosity beats inertia outright - flow is always laminar, the red and blue streams advance side by side with a razor-straight interface, never swirling into each other; the price is that mixing is left to molecular diffusion alone, t≈w²/2D, about 5 s for a 100 μm channel and tens of seconds for a few hundred - far too slow. So engineers fold the channel into a serpentine and use stretch-and-fold chaotic advection to crush mixing to sub-second. Laminar predictability is also a gift: at a T-junction, oil shears the water into monodisperse droplets (coefficient of variation under 2%), and one droplet is one pL-nL reactor - droplet PCR platforms generate thousands per second. At small scale surface tension outruns body forces: capillarity pumps fluid by itself - the paper lateral-flow strip (L∝√t) is exactly how a pregnancy test works; electrowetting (EWOD) shifts the contact angle with voltage and drags droplets pad by pad, called digital microfluidics. The huge surface-to-volume ratio also buys second-scale heat exchange (PCR thermal cycling) and single-cell capture, and the inkjet printhead is its most successful industrial cousin. In the demo: sliders set flow velocity / channel width / water fraction, linked live to Re, diffusion time and droplet size & frequency; buttons switch straight-channel comparison, the T-junction droplet line and electrowetting. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **microfluidics/**

- [x] Activated Sludge: The Microbe Legion That Eats Wastewater(Municipal wastewater carries a BOD (biodegradable organic matter) of about 200-300 mg/L, which must be pressed below 10 before discharge to the river - and the workforce is not chemicals but a tankful of microbes. Screens first catch floating rags, a grit chamber settles out sand, and the primary clarifier removes 50-70% of settleable solids by gravity; the real protagonists work in the aeration tank: flocs of 0.1-1 mm bio-aggregates adsorb and oxidize organics while synthesizing new cells, and blowers push air through fine-bubble diffusers to supply oxygen (transfer efficiency only 10-30%, yet 40-60% of total plant power) and stir. The key parameters: food-to-mass ratio F/M of 0.2-0.5 kgBOD/(kgMLSS·d), hydraulic residence 4-8 h, sludge age SRT 10-20 d - SRT must exceed the nitrifiers' doubling time or these slow growers wash out. In the secondary clarifier flocs settle by gravity; return sludge at 50-100% keeps the tank concentration up, and the surplus leaves as waste sludge: grow as much as you remove. Nitrogen takes a two-leg relay: aerobic nitrification NH₄⁺→NO₂⁻→NO₃⁻, then anoxic denitrification NO₃⁻→N₂ escaping to air (carbon sourced from raw BOD); the A/O process puts the anoxic zone first plus internal recycle. Phosphorus relies on PAOs that release P anaerobically then take up luxury amounts aerobically (A²/O). And when filamentous organisms overgrow, it all breaks: sludge bulking, stringy flocs, clarifier blanket washout, effluent violations. In the demo: drag aeration to watch DO collapse and power burn, tune return ratio and sludge age, and toggle internal recycle A/O, the bulking event and the nitrogen path. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **activated-sludge/**

- [x] P vs NP: Easy to Check, Hard to Solve(Sorting and shortest paths can be solved directly in polynomial time - class P. A finished sudoku, by contrast, is verified by one sweep over its rows, columns and boxes; a big Boolean formula is checked by testing one assignment term by term - problems whose answers are cheap to verify form NP. Clearly P is contained in NP; the hard question is the reverse: does easy verification imply easy solving? That is the Clay Institute's million-dollar P vs NP problem. The bridge is reduction: translate an instance of problem A into an instance of problem B in polynomial time, and a solver for B solves A. The Cook-Levin theorem proves Boolean satisfiability (SAT) is NP-complete - among the hardest in NP - and Karp then chained 21 classic problems (3SAT, clique, vertex cover, Hamiltonian cycle, graph coloring, knapsack, decision-TSP...) onto it: all NP-complete problems stand or fall together - a polynomial algorithm for any one of them topples them all. Cryptography bets P is not NP (more precisely it relies on one-way functions): RSA and friends rest on the asymmetry of easy to verify, hard to solve. Practitioners have three workarounds: approximation algorithms (Christofides guarantees a tour within 1.5x optimal for TSP), parameterized algorithms (exponential in a small parameter k, polynomial in n), and industrial SAT solvers (worst-case exponential with a tiny constant - tens of thousands of variables solved in practice). Easter egg: random 3SAT undergoes a phase transition at clause-to-variable ratio alpha of about 4.267, where satisfiability plunges from 1 to 0 - the hardest instances cluster right at the threshold. In the demo: watch the sudoku sweep finish instantly while the backtracking tree's node count explodes; drag n to see the 2^n brute-force bars shear away from the flat n^2 verification bars; run the reduction animation turning 3SAT into a clique; and sample 3SAT instances at your chosen alpha to hit the phase transition yourself. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **p-versus-np/**

- [x] Buffer Overflow & Memory Safety(C never checks array bounds: write 100 bytes into a 64-byte stack buffer and the extra 36 bytes flood upward over the neighboring data. A stack frame lays out from low to high addresses as: local variables (including the buffer), then the saved frame pointer, then the return address; given enough input, the return address is overwritten with attacker data - when the function executes ret, the program counter is loaded with that forged value and control flow jumps wherever the attacker points: the classic bug the 1988 Morris worm exploited, toppling thousands of machines overnight. Thirty years of defense: the stack canary places a sentinel before the return address at function entry and checks it before returning, killing the process on tamper; ASLR randomizes stack/heap/library base addresses at every launch so hardcoded offsets miss; NX/DEP marks stack pages non-executable so injected code cannot run; attackers answered with ROP (return-oriented programming), chaining ready-made code gadgets already in the program to bypass NX, which in turn motivated CFI (control-flow integrity); the root cure is memory-safe languages - Rust/Go/Java with runtime bounds checks: Microsoft and Google report roughly 70% of severe security bugs are memory-safety issues, and the industry is rewriting critical components in Rust. Engineering lessons: always check lengths, use bounded APIs, and turn on compiler hardening (-fstack-protector and friends). In the demo: drag the input-length slider to pour data into the stack tower cell by cell and watch it cross the buffer edge, dyeing the canary and the return address red; press function return to see four endings - hijacked with no defenses, killed on the spot by the canary, hardcoded offsets defeated by ASLR, or the NX page refusing to execute; switch on bounds-checked writes to compare the safe version, and press re-call to draw a fresh random base under ASLR. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **buffer-overflow/**

- [x] Myoelectric Prosthetics(After an amputation, healthy residual muscles still fire normally when they contract: spinal motor neurons excite the fibers, and the action potentials reach the skin surface through volume conduction as a patch of noisy spikes, 10 uV to 1 mV in amplitude over 20-500 Hz - that is surface electromyography, EMG. The signal chain has three stages: a differential electrode (two pads + one reference) first rejects far-field common-mode interference; a 20-450 Hz bandpass removes baseline drift and high-frequency noise, with a 50/60 Hz notch for the power line; then rectification extracts the envelope (RMS, time constant 100-200 ms - too short jitters, too long feels sluggish), giving a smooth measure of effort. The simplest control is two-channel thresholding: flexor over threshold -> close, extensor over threshold -> open; proportional control maps envelope amplitude into grip force. The advanced option is pattern recognition: several electrode channels yield time-domain features (MAV, zero crossings, waveform length) and a classifier (LDA or a small network) recognizes four to eight intended gestures, above 95% accuracy in the lab. Targeted muscle reinnervation (TMR) sews the cut brachial-plexus nerves onto other residual muscles, moving the hand's signals to the skin surface - richer channels, a larger gesture set. The biggest weakness is open loop: the hand feels nothing, so users must watch it; vibrotactile and electrical feedback closed loops are the frontier. Daily challenges: electrode shift, sweat attenuation, EMG fatigue, and a battery that needs daily charging. In the demo, drag the contraction slider to watch glowing waves run along the muscle bundles and raw EMG spikes climb on the scope, then the envelope crosses threshold and the hand acts; switch to pattern recognition to watch confidence bars compete in real time; press electrode shift or sweat interference to see mis-grasps; tick TMR to double the gesture library. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **myoelectric-prosthesis/**

- [x] Diesel Particulate Filter and Regeneration(A diesel engine burns by diffusion: fuel is sprayed into the cylinder without time to mix evenly, so fuel-rich zones at high temperature run out of oxygen and naturally make soot - carbon cores coated with organics and sulfates, tens to hundreds of nanometers. The DPF (diesel particulate filter) is a wall-flow honeycomb ceramic (cordierite or silicon carbide, 200-300 cpsi cells, 0.3-0.5 mm walls, pores around ten microns): adjacent channels are plugged at opposite ends, alternating - exhaust has no straight path and is forced through the porous walls, where particles are caught, giving over 95% filtration efficiency by mass; the gas walks through the wall, the soot stays. As carbon accumulates, backpressure rises, fuel consumption climbs and power drops, so the filter must regenerate periodically: passive regeneration - the upstream DOC oxidizes NO into NO2, and C+2NO2->CO2+2NO slow-burns the soot continuously at 250-450 C; active regeneration - when exhaust temperature is too low, fuel is injected late or post-injected to push the substrate to 550-650 C, where C+O2 -> CO2 releases heat that drives the burn front forward, taking 10-30 minutes, typically every few hundred kilometers. Temperature is double-edged: below 550 nothing burns, above 800 the substrate sinters or even melts. Ash (Ca/Zn/P from oil additives plus wear metals) is incombustible and slowly fills the volume - after tens of thousands of kilometers the filter must be removed and ash-washed; failed regens and long-term short trips clog it solid, triggering torque limits and limp mode. Together with the gasoline three-way catalyst (TWC) and diesel SCR urea system it forms the aftertreatment trio; full soot capacity is 5-8 g/L of substrate and regeneration costs 2-4% extra fuel. In the demo, drag the exhaust temperature to switch passive/active regeneration and watch channels darken and the pressure gauge climb; ignite to see the burning front sweep through, soot leave as CO2 and backpressure fall; press ash accumulation or regen failure for the long-term story; tick the trio panorama for the DOC -> DPF -> SCR pipeline. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **dpf-regeneration/**

### Phase 78 · Cross-Family Gap-Fill Batch 48 (8/8 complete)

- [x] Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch: A Linear Motor Replaces the Steam Piston(A steam catapult uses high-pressure steam from an accumulator to slam a piston down its cylinder: the release valve is mechanical and the force arrives as one big wave - fiercest at the start, fading toward the end. Energy efficiency is only 4-6%, the cylinder and steam train occupy over 1100 cubic meters and needs freshwater boiled into steam; it barely suffices for a 30-ton fighter, but for a light drone of a few tons the opening jolt can overload and snap the airframe. EMALS replaces the piston with a linear motor: hundreds of stator coil segments are buried along the launch groove, and the roughly 30 m shuttle is the rotor - power electronics energize only the segments under the shuttle, so a traveling wave of magnetism carries it forward while empty segments draw no current and make no heat, wasting almost no energy. The energy comes from flywheel accumulators that spin slowly to bank kinetic energy - a single unit outputs on the order of 120 MJ - then dumps it through inverters within 3 seconds, hurling the aircraft to 70-100 m/s with about 45 s between launches. The key dividend is closed-loop programmability: shuttle position and speed are measured in real time and the thrust curve is tailored to the aircraft mass - a 5-ton drone and a 30-ton fighter each get their own acceleration spectrum with smooth peaks and controlled overload; cut the power and the force vanishes; a faulty segment is simply skipped. In the demo, drag the mass and exit-speed sliders to watch thrust and acceleration recompute live; press steam compare to pit sawtooth against smooth acceleration on one scope; press flywheel charge to see the store-and-dump cycle; press segment x-ray to watch lit stator segments chase the shuttle. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **em-catapult/**

- [x] Rare-Earth Separation: Solvent Extraction Cascades for 17 Near-Twins(The 17 rare-earth elements (scandium, yttrium plus 15 lanthanides) are a nest of chemical near-twins: all stable at +3, ionic radii shrinking smoothly with atomic number (the lanthanide contraction) so adjacent pairs differ by only about 1 pm, and always co-occurring as one family in bastnasite and monazite - precipitation grading and distillation are helpless. Industry answers with solvent-extraction cascades: the organic phase (acidic phosphorus extractants such as P507) takes up each rare earth at a slightly different distribution ratio; the single-stage separation factor between neighbors is only about 1.5-2.5, so one stage is never clean - instead hundreds of mixer-settlers are chained together: aqueous flows toward one end, organic toward the other, each stage mixing, contacting and settling, and the tiny difference is amplified exponentially (separation D_A/D_B = beta^N, N the stage count). A cascade of a hundred-plus stages splits praseodymium from neodymium at 99.99-99.999% (5N). Xu Guangxian's cascade extraction theory turned stage counts and scrub reflux into computable formulas, letting China lead the world on an integrated concentrate-to-oxide flowsheet. What comes out props up half of high tech: NdPr into NdFeB permanent magnets for wind turbines and EV motors, DyTb into heat-resistant magnets, EuY into phosphors. A single flowsheet runs 50-100+ stages; at beta of about 2, 100 stages amplify by 2^100, about 10^30. In the demo, drag the beta, stage-count and feed-ratio sliders and watch the blue (Pr/aqueous) and yellow (Nd/organic) concentration curves pull apart stage by stage while purity jumps by orders of magnitude; press single vs cascade to see what one stage manages alone; press lanthanide contraction to see 15 radius columns separated by a hair. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **rare-earth-separation/**

- [x] Mitochondria & Maternal Inheritance: The Line That Only Runs Through Mothers(Mitochondria are the power plants of the cell, yet they keep a small genome of their own: human mtDNA is 16,569 bp long with only 37 genes - 13 respiratory-chain subunits, 22 tRNAs and 2 rRNAs. This genome passes to the next generation almost exclusively through the egg's cytoplasm: the few dozen mitochondria a sperm brings in are tagged with ubiquitin and then destroyed, leaving only the egg's 100,000+ copies in the zygote - so the family tree runs only along the maternal line, which is exactly how mitochondrial Eve (a common maternal ancestor 150,000-200,000 years ago) was traced. Each cell holds hundreds to thousands of mitochondria with 2-10 mtDNA copies each, and mutant and wild-type genomes can coexist - a mixture called heteroplasmy. Passing to the next generation crosses a genetic bottleneck: early in egg development mtDNA is first cut from about 100,000 copies down to a few dozen-hundred, then re-amplified; sampling noise gives children of the same mother wildly different mutation loads - a mother at 20% can have a child at 5% or 80%. There is also a threshold effect: symptoms appear only above roughly 60-90% mutant fraction (depending on the variant), and the biggest energy consumers - nerve, muscle, heart - fail first: MELAS, MERRF and Leber optic neuropathy all sit on this chain. Three-parent babies / mitochondrial replacement - moving nuclear DNA into a donor's healthy egg cytoplasm - exists precisely to cut this transmission chain. In the demo, watch sperm mitochondria get ubiquitinated and cleared; set maternal load (5-80%) and bottleneck width (20-500 copies), then press breed one generation for binomial sampling - the histogram and four-generation pedigree drift, and individuals above threshold light up red. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **mitochondrial-inheritance/**

- [x] Magnetocaloric Cooling: Let the Magnetic Field Do the Compressing(Magnetic refrigeration never compresses a gas - it plays the entropy card: put a magnetic field on a magnetocaloric material and the spin moments align with the field, so magnetic entropy plunges; under adiabatic conditions total entropy cannot simply vanish, so lattice entropy fills in and the material heats itself up. Remove the field, the spins re-randomize, heat is absorbed from the surroundings and the material cools back down. The catch: a single stage only shifts a few kelvin - gadolinium happens to have its Curie point right near room temperature (about 293 K), and 1 T buys an adiabetic rise of just 2.5-3 K. Household machines amplify it with an active magnetic regenerator (AMR) cycle: magnetize (heat rejected to the regenerator) - hot-end exchange - demagnetize (heat absorbed from the regenerator) - cold-end exchange; the belt of working material shuttles between the cold and hot ends while the regenerator works like a ladder, stacking the small steps into a 20-30 K span at 0.5-4 Hz. The field comes from a Halbach permanent-magnet array (1-1.5 T): spinning the inner cylinder switches the bed between strong and weak field - no superconductors, no compressor, no HFC refrigerants, quiet, with efficiency up to 30-60% of Carnot. Working materials are picked per temperature range: Gd5Si2Ge2 giant magnetocaloric, La(Fe,Si)13, Mn-based alloys. Beverage coolers have been in commercial pilot since 2016 and household fridges are in development. In the demo, watch chain links enter the strong field - spins line up, the link glows red and dumps heat - then leave, disorder, glow blue and soak heat up; drag field strength (0.5-1.5 T), cycle frequency (0.5-4 Hz) and cold-side load and watch the cold/hot temperature curves climb into steady state; open the Halbach x-ray, spin slow-motion and T-S diagram for the three inner views. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **magnetocaloric/**

- [x] Lunar Water Ice: Treasure in Perpetual Shadow(The Moon spins almost perfectly upright - an axial tilt of only about 1.5 degrees (Earth: 23.5), so the sun forever circles low along its horizon. The floors of the deep south-polar craters (Shackleton, Haworth, Shoemaker) have seen no direct sunlight for billions of years: these permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) sit at roughly 25-110 K, among the coldest natural surfaces in the solar system. Water delivered over 4 billion years by comets, carbon-rich asteroids and solar-wind protons falls into these cold traps and never leaves - sublimation depends on thermal motion, and at 110 K ice escapes on astronomical timescales, so ice grains have been accumulating in the regolith (polar reserves estimated in the hundreds of millions of tonnes, with large uncertainty). The evidence is a relay race: in 1998 Lunar Prospector's neutron spectrometer measured excess hydrogen at both poles; in 2009 LCROSS slammed the Centaur upper stage into crater Cabeus and the plume spectrum read out about 5.6 percent water by mass; in 2018 Chandrayaan-1's M3 infrared imager directly identified exposed ice. Why care? Water is drinkable and electrolyzes into hydrogen-oxygen propellant, and shipping it from the lunar surface to lunar orbit costs only about 1.9 km/s of delta-v versus 9.4 km/s from Earth - the Moon may become a deep-space gas station. The challenges are real: at -230 C batteries and mechanisms fail and photovoltaics are useless inside a PSR - power must come from always-lit crater rims via long cables or from nuclear sources, and radio needs relay masts on sunlit peaks. In the demo, drag the axial-tilt slider to compare crater-floor fates under lunar versus terrestrial tilt, run the year time-lapse to watch 1.5 degrees keep the floor dark all year; press the LCROSS impact to replay the 2009 strike and its plume spectrum; press mining base to watch rim photovoltaics, a power cable, drill sublimation, electrolysis and rocket fuelling. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **lunar-water-ice/**

- [x] Piston Wind: The Train Makes Its Own Breeze(A train in a tunnel is a close-fitting piston: the nose shoves the air ahead into a compression zone, the tail drags a negative-pressure wake, and the real work happens in the 10-25 cm annular gap between car body and tunnel wall - squeezed air jets out of this ring at high speed, handing momentum to the tunnel air layer by layer like an annular jet. At 80 km/h the tunnel wind can hit 5-10 m/s; one passing train exchanges half the air of kilometers of tunnel, and a whole line moves millions of cubic meters a day on piston action alone. The wind is both nuisance and benefactor: a nuisance on platforms - before a train arrives the piston wind slams in and can gust to 10 m/s across the waiting crowd, so piston relief shafts at both station ends vent the pressure early; a benefactor in the tunnel - the train is the biggest ventilation fan of the whole system, hauling brake-resistor, traction and air-conditioning heat out trainload by trainload, and many lines run their daily ventilation on piston effect alone, saving serious electricity. Modern metros added two switches: platform screen doors (PSD) seal the platform from the tunnel - safer waiting and 30-40 percent less cooling energy, though tunnel heat then needs dedicated fans; and streamlined noses (high fineness ratio) tame the micro-pressure wave released when the compression wave exits the tunnel - the low boom that made Japanese engineers stretch bullet-train noses to ten meters. In the demo, drag speed and blocking ratio to watch tunnel wind and platform pressure climb; toggle screen doors and relief shafts to compare the platform fates; press micro-pressure wave for the boom at the portal. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **piston-wind/**

- [x] Quantum Teleportation: Destroyed Here, Reborn There(Getting an unknown quantum state psi = alpha|0> + beta|1> from Alice to Bob faces three obstacles: the no-cloning theorem (no copying), collapse on measurement (looking destroys), and light speed (no carrying at a distance). The 1993 Bennett protocol is elegant stage magic: Alice and Bob first share an entangled Bell pair; Alice measures her two qubits (the psi qubit plus her half of the pair) together in the Bell basis - four equiprobable outcomes Phi+, Phi-, Psi+, Psi-; the measurement destroys psi on Alices side while Bobs half instantly collapses into some Pauli variant of psi (acted on by I, X, Z or XZ, one quarter each); Alice sends the 2-bit result over a classical channel, Bob applies the matching Pauli correction, and his qubit becomes exactly |psi>. Note the ledger: one entangled pair plus two classical bits buys one teleported qubit; the original is destroyed in the measurement - no clone, quantum information conserved; and no matter how strong the entanglement, without those two classical bits Bob can do nothing - so teleportation never beats light speed, and relativity is unharmed. Entanglement here is not transport but a resource: a pre-laid quantum line, one pair consumed per transmission. In 2017 the Micius satellite teleported photon states 1400 km up to a ground station, and quantum networks now treat teleportation as a standard part. In the demo, set any initial state on the two Bloch spheres with the sliders and press teleport once to run the full protocol: watch the Bell measurement roll one of four outcomes, the classical packet fly across, Bobs arrow rotate through X/Z corrections onto the original state while Alices side goes dark; press no-classical-channel to watch Bob stuck with a variant (mean fidelity only 1/2); press no-cloning to meet the forbidden copy. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **quantum-teleportation/**

- [x] The Endoscope: An Eye That Bends(Seeing an ulcer inside the stomach without opening the patient - an endoscope packs an eye, a flashlight and a robotic hand into a 9 mm flexible tube. Four things live in the tip: an objective lens (140-170 degree field), a light guide (an external cold-light source sends bright light down, so nothing hot burns tissue), an air/water channel (to rinse the lens and inflate the cavity), and a 2.8-3.7 mm working channel for biopsy forceps, snares and needles. The bending section is the soul: four steel wires in two opposing pairs - two handwheels pull one side and slacken the other, letting a few centimeters of scope bend past 210 degrees with a 5-10 mm radius, turning corners among gastric folds. Images travel two ways: older fiberscopes use a fused image bundle - tens of thousands of fibers ordered identically at both ends, each carrying one pixel by total internal reflection; break one fiber and that pixel dies forever. Modern video endoscopes just put a CMOS/CCD in the tip, photographing in vivo with 0.1-1 megapixels, and NBI narrow-band imaging brings out mucosal vessel texture. The capsule endoscope is the minimal version: 26 x 11 mm, LED plus camera plus battery, 2-6 frames a second, riding peristalsis for 8-14 hours through the small intestine. The numbers: gastroscopes are 9-10 mm across, reach about a meter in, and can biopsy, snare polyps, clip bleeds and place stents - see it, treat it. In the demo, drag insertion depth to slide down the esophagus into the stomach, steer L/R and U/D to aim the bending section and watch the monitor view (scope window) respond; aim at a red lesion and press biopsy forceps to sample it; switch to fiberscope for the bundle cross-section and dead pixels; press capsule endoscope to drift through the small bowel. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause) ✅ **endoscope/**

### Phase 75 · Cross-Family Gap-Fill Batch 45 (24/24 complete)



- [x] Cycloidal Reducer: One Tooth Short, i = Zr-1 (Inside industrial robot joints, satellite solar-array drives and machining-center tool changers, the reducer that shrugs off shock yet stops within an arcminute is usually a cycloidal pinwheel reducer. Its entire secret is one sentence: the cycloid disc has exactly one tooth fewer than the pins in the housing. A motor spins an eccentric sleeve on the input shaft, dragging the disc around a circle of radius a; the one-tooth difference forces the disc to creep tooth by tooth along the pin ring - each input revolution rolls the disc backwards by exactly one tooth pitch, giving ratio i = Zr-1. Eighteen pins mean 17:1; a single stage reaches 6-87. The disc turns too slowly and its axis wobbles, so the W mechanism takes over: eight pins on the output disc pass through eight holes in the cycloid disc, each hole cut larger than its pin by exactly the eccentricity a. The orbital component is absorbed by the crescent gap; only the slow reverse self-rotation reaches the output shaft. Because more than a third of the pins share the load at all times (about half in theory), the drive survives overloads that would strip ordinary gears, with backlash under 1 arcminute and 75-92% single-stage efficiency. Two identical discs mounted 180 degrees apart cancel the eccentric vibration. German Loewe and Swiss Cyclo industrialized it in the 1930s; todays RV reducers stack an involute planetary stage in front and dominate robot joints. Press the overload preset to watch loaded pins light up with stress bars, drag the pin-count slider from 9 to 21 and watch the ratio jump from 8:1 to 20:1; on the scope, the slope ratio of the green input and red output saws is the ratio itself.)


- [x] Peaucellier: Drawing a Perfect Line with Bars (The steam age faced an awkward geometry problem: a piston must move in a perfect straight line or the cylinder packing wears unevenly and leaks steam, yet machining a long truly straight guideway was ruinously expensive. So engineers tried to draw lines with hinged bars. Watts 1784 linkage was only approximate - its trace point rides the middle of a figure eight and still sags visibly. In 1864 the French naval officer Charles-Nicolas Peaucellier found the exact answer: a rhombus of four short bars (length r) hung between two equal long bars (length R), arranged so that the pivot O and the ends P and Q stay collinear while the product OP x OQ stays equal to the constant R2-r2. Point Q is therefore the inversion of P in the circle of radius sqrt(R2-r2), and inversion maps any circle through O onto a straight line. Add a crank that pins P to such a circle and Q must draw a true line - the first exact straight-line mechanism, verified by the French Academy of Sciences in 1873. Drag the short-bar slider and watch the line position k/(2p) move; press the singularity preset and drive the crank to the dead point OP = R-r: five bars flatten into one line, the bar-force factor spikes and Q reverses on the spot. In 1876 Kempe proved that linkages can trace any algebraic curve, and planar bar chains entered textbooks as geometric computers. Rolling guides do the job today, but the inverter still turns in precision instruments and classrooms.)


- [x] Elliptic Gears: The Ratio That Breathes (A circular gear has a pitch circle of constant radius, so its ratio never changes; swap the pitch curve for an ellipse and the ratio starts to breathe. Mount two identical ellipses, each pivoted about one focus, with center distance 2a: the contact point always lies on the line of centers and the instantaneous ratio is the inverse ratio of the two pitch radii, i = r2/r1. The polar radius of an ellipse is r = a(1-e2)/(1+e cos), swinging between a(1-e) and a(1+e), so the ratio oscillates once per revolution between (1+e)/(1-e) and (1-e)/(1+e) - that is 2.33 and 0.43 at e = 0.4, and the output shaft visibly speeds up and slows down. Packaging and printing machines exploit exactly this slow-fast-slow cadence: cutting and registration during the slow phase, material advance during the fast one. Run the idea backwards and you get the oval-gear flow meter: two lobed rotors displace a fixed crescent volume per passage, so the revolution count is the delivered volume, good to 0.2-0.5% and nearly independent of viscosity - still standard for fuel and chemical dosing. All of it obeys the same fundamental law of gearing: the common normal at contact passes through the pitch point, which simply slides along the line of centers. Drag the eccentricity slider from 0.02 to 0.6 and watch the ratio needle swing and the parcels pulse; press the metering preset for crescents filling and draining with a running total, or the round-gear preset to return to the constant-ratio world of e = 0.)


- [x] Phase Diagrams & the Triple Point (Which phase wins - solid, liquid or gas - is decided by just two dials, temperature and pressure, and the phase diagram is the map of that verdict. Every line on it is a coexistence curve whose slope obeys the Clausius-Clapeyron equation dP/dT = dH/(T dV). Water is the famous rebel: ice occupies about 8.3% more volume per mole than liquid water, so dV is negative, the solid-liquid line leans backwards (about -13.5 MPa/K) and squeezing actually melts ice - a 90 kg skater pressing on a few square centimeters of blade squeezes out a micron-thin water film, and glacier beds slide on the same pressure-melting trick. CO2 has a normal, positive melt slope, but its triple point sits at -56.6 C and 5.18 bar, five times atmospheric pressure, so at 1 atm liquid CO2 has no home at all: dry ice simply sublimes at -78.5 C. The three lines meet at the triple point - water coexists as ice, liquid and vapor at 0.01 C and 611.657 Pa, the state that once defined the kelvin. The boiling line ends at the critical point (water 374 C / 22.06 MPa, CO2 31.1 C / 7.38 MPa); beyond it gas and liquid merge into one supercritical fluid. Pressure also rewrites boiling points: on Everest at 0.33 atm water boils near 71 C, while a pressure cooker at 2 atm pushes it to 120 C. Drag the temperature and pressure sliders to move the state point and watch the particles switch between lattice, flow and dispersion, or press the dry-ice, triple-point, supercritical-CO2 and Everest presets for four signature routes.)


- [x] Gibbs Free Energy: Temperature Decides Spontaneity (Which way a reaction runs is voted on by energy and entropy, and the referee is the Gibbs free energy: dG = dH - T dS, and only dG < 0 goes. Four combinations, four fates: exothermic with rising entropy - glucose oxidation, dH = -2803 kJ/mol, dS = +259 J/(mol K) - is spontaneous at every temperature; exothermic with falling entropy (water freezing) only below 273 K; endothermic with rising entropy (ice melting) only above 273 K; endothermic with falling entropy - building glucose out of CO2 and water - never, which is why photosynthesis needs photons to pay the bill. Temperature is the hand on the switch: for CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2, dH = +178.3 kJ/mol and dS = +160.5 J/(mol K), so the crossover temperature dH/dS lands near 1111 K (838 C) - exactly why lime kilns must burn above 900 C. dG is also the ceiling on useful work: a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell with dG = -237 kJ/mol tops out at 237000/(2F) = 1.23 V, while an internal combustion engine burns most of that dividend away as waste heat. dG = 0 is equilibrium, and dG = -RT lnK ties thermodynamics to the equilibrium constant. Watch the two bars: red is dH, fixed; blue is T dS, growing with temperature - the moment blue overtakes red, dG flips sign. Drag the temperature slider past 1111 K and watch the G-xi valley flip sides as the ball rolls to the new spontaneous direction, or tour the four presets for four fates.)


- [x] Dust Explosions: Surface Area Turns a Pile into a Bomb (A lump of iron will not burn, but iron dust explodes - combustion happens only at the surface, so the rate scales with contact area: one cubic centimeter of iron carries about 0.08 m2/kg of specific surface, 75-micron powder about 10 m2/kg, and 50-nanometer powder beyond 1.5x10^4 m2/kg - five orders of magnitude. A suspended dust cloud is a premixed charge of solid fuel and air with a concentration window: lower limit roughly 20-60 g/m3, upper limit 2-6 kg/m3, and particles under 75 microns are the most dangerous. Ignition gives deflagration: a flame front near 10 m/s and, in a closed workshop, pressures of 6-9 bar, while fine dust needs only 10-50 mJ to light - a static spark will do. The truly lethal part is the relay: the pressure wave of the primary blast runs ahead of the flame and lifts the settled piles wholesale into a far larger secondary cloud, which the flame ignites on arrival - often at several points at once and several times more powerful. The 1987 Harbin flax mill blast killed 58 people, the 2014 Kunshan polishing workshop took 146 - settled dust relays were the killer in both. The engineering answer is a quartet: vent panels that clamp overpressure to 0.1-0.2 bar, millisecond chemical suppression, inerting with nitrogen below the limiting oxygen concentration of 10-12%, and housekeeping - remove layers over 0.8 mm, vacuum rather than blow. Set the concentration and particle-size sliders, then press pile ignition, cloud ignition, relay blast and vented contrast to watch four outcomes; pull the speed slider to 0.2x for slow motion.)


- [x] The Growth Plate: Where Height Is Manufactured (Growing from one metre to 1.8 m, long bones do not stretch along the shaft - they lengthen at each end, inside a 1-3 mm band of translucent cartilage called the growth plate. It is a one-way assembly line: the resting zone banks reserve cells; in the proliferative zone chondrocytes stack in coin-like columns and divide every 12-24 h, pushing the whole queue toward the shaft; in the hypertrophic zone cells swell 5-10 times in volume - about 60% of all longitudinal growth - and secrete type X collagen and VEGF to guide blood vessels in; the calcified scaffold is then invaded from the shaft side by vessels and osteoblasts, which cast it into new bone. Cartilage queues first, bone is poured second, day and night. Hormones set the tempo: the GH-IGF-1 axis holds childhood at a steady 5-7 cm/yr; at puberty sex hormones first drive the peak (girls 8-9, boys 9-10 cm/yr), then act as the fuse - estrogen, which both sexes rely on, fuses the plates at 13-15 in girls and 15-17 in boys, and height is capped for life. The line is fragile too: 15-30% of children s fractures cross the plate (Salter-Harris), and crushing its germinal layer can leave one side permanently stopped, shortening or angling the limb; uncontrolled GH before closure means gigantism. Drag the age slider to watch bone extrude, push GH above 2.5x to jam the gate open, or press plate closure to see the bony bridge sweep across and growth stop on the spot.)


- [x] Vernalization: How a Plant Counts the Weeks of Winter (Winter wheat sown in autumn will head in spring only if it first lived through weeks of 0-7 C cold; otherwise it makes leaves and no ears. That ability to count winter is vernalization, and the counter sits on the FLC gene. FLC is expressed all year and holds flowering off; after 2-3 weeks of cold, VIN3 recruits the Polycomb complex PRC2 to the FLC chromatin, and from then on every extra cold week deposits one more layer of H3K27me3 methylation, stepping FLC expression down by roughly a fifth per layer - the plant is tallying the winter. Warming does not erase the count: once laid down, the cold marks persist for the plant s lifetime (epigenetic memory), so a brief warm spell in late autumn cannot fool it; only after about 6 cold weeks is the brake permanently off. Long days then take over: the phytochrome-CO module switches on FT protein in the leaf, FT rides the phloem to the shoot apex, and flowering starts - which is why winter wheat heads in early summer. Drag the cold-weeks slider and watch flags plant one by one on the chromatin while the FLC bar collapses; then push day length past 12 h and the left plant bolts and flowers while the un-vernalized control stays a rosette of leaves; after 8 cold weeks, warming will not reset the count - press warm memory to see it. Agriculture runs on it: winter vs spring wheat, cabbage and carrots bolting after winter, seed stratification at 4 C for weeks. Lysenko politicized vernalization from 1928; the real mechanism was only uncovered in the 2000s by Henderson, Dean and colleagues.)


- [x] Snake Venom: Molecular Tools That Hijack Nerve and Blood (Snake venom is not one poison but a cocktail of over a hundred proteins, in two schools. Neurotoxic (elapid) venom: three-finger toxins like alpha-bungarotoxin occupy the nicotinic receptors of the neuromuscular junction before acetylcholine can - binding about ten thousand times stronger, and essentially irreversibly. Endplate potentials fail, skeletal muscles drop out one by one, and respiratory arrest is the most direct cause of death; presynaptic beta-bungarotoxin (a phospholipase A2) wrecks the terminal s transmitter-release machinery outright. Hemotoxic (viper) venom works on logistics: metalloproteases and serine proteases first switch clotting on all over the body - microthrombi spread while clotting factors are consumed (disseminated intravascular coagulation) - then turn around and digest fibrin and the vascular basement membrane, so blood that cannot clot leaks through vessels that cannot hold; PLA2 also hydrolyzes muscle membranes into local necrosis and swelling. Treatment is antivenom: polyclonal IgG raised in horses or sheep can only hunt toxin still floating free - a golden window of about 1-4 h. Receptors already occupied cannot be rescued; you wait for new ones to be built. First aid buys the window: pressure immobilization keeps toxin in place, while cutting, sucking or icing only deepens the damage. Drag the venom-dose slider to thicken the molecular rain, switch stages with neurotoxin strike and hemotoxin strike, then compare early antivenom (0.5 h) against delayed (4 h): many-banded krait venom has an LD50 near 0.1 mg/kg while a single bite can deliver 4-43 mg - time is survival.)


- [x] Photoelasticity: Making Stress Visible in Polarized Light (A loaded transparent material reports its own stress: in 1816 Brewster noticed that squeezed glass shows colored bands between crossed polarizers - stress makes the refractive index anisotropic, and the index difference between the two polarization modes along the principal stress directions is proportional to the principal stress difference: n1 - n2 = C(s1 - s2), with C near 1e-11 m2/N for epoxy.
