### Phase 43 deep dives (condensed)

- **belt-drive/** — A tensioned belt drive with tension gradient painted along the strap (orange tight side, blue slack side). Push load torque upward and watch T1/T2 climb until it hits the e^(μθ) red line — at that instant the driven pulley stalls inside the still-running belt and starts glowing red.
- **bolt-preload/** — A half-section bolted joint sits on a Junker vibration rig: hit the shaker and the eccentric cam walks the plates sideways, the preload bar drains cell by cell, and the marked nut visibly rotates back toward disaster. Switch to the wedge washers and the same shake leaves it rock solid.
- **cycloid-gears/** — A generating circle rolls around a pitch circle while a pen traces the exact tooth flank, then two clock wheels (7:14 teeth) mesh with the contact point glowing along the describing-circle arcs. Drag the center-distance slider: the cycloid pair seizes dead while the involute pair beside it just keeps on turning.
- **magnetic-coupling/** — Two magnet rings mesh through a translucent seal wall with live field lines arching across the gap. Hit the stall button: the lines stretch and skew to the limit, the trapped rotor slips back one pole pitch at a time with a flash, and on release it hunts briefly before locking back into sync.
- **scotch-yoke/** — Two machines turn at the same speed: the Scotch yoke traces a mathematically perfect sine while the slider-crank's finite rod drags in a second harmonic. The deviation between the two curves fills in red on a live oscilloscope; pull the rod-length slider toward infinity and watch it collapse.
- **stewart-platform/** — Six telescoping legs carry a hexagonal platform; every slider change is answered instantly by six exact leg-length readouts, because parallel kinematics is a closed-form solution. Run the swell preset and the platform center paints a Lissajous figure, while a wobbly serial arm beside it stacks tolerance cone upon tolerance cone.
- **diels-alder/** — Two π chains rotate toward each other like a zipper, three orange arrows spin one synchronized turn, and in a white flash the six-membered ring snaps shut (ΔH≈−167 kJ/mol). Drag the temperature slider to cross the 105 kJ/mol barrier or flip endo/exo to see the dashed secondary-overlap lines appear.
- **glass-vitrification/** — One box of 120 atoms, two fates: drag the cooling-rate slider slow and they click into a gold-shimmering lattice with a kink on the live V-T plot; drag it fast and they freeze mid-scramble, stained red with residual stress until you hit Anneal.
- **grignard-reaction/** — Watch the reacting carbon turn from red (δ+) to blue (δ−) the instant magnesium donates its electron, then pounce on a carbonyl so a glowing orange C–C bond snaps into existence. Switch substrate to grow 1°/2°/3° alcohols, or drop in water and watch the reagent die on the spot.
- **ksp-precipitation/** — A single drop of concentrated Ba²⁺ into the near-saturated beaker and the whole bottle flashes white with turbidity while the Q marker leaps past the red Ksp tick, then slides back as the ion counters settle onto the equilibrium line; flip between CaCO₃, BaSO₄, CaF₂ and AgI to move the line by eight orders of magnitude.
- **lithium-dendrite/** — Push the C-rate slider toward 3C and watch one bump on the anode grow cell by cell into a needle; the instant it kisses the separator the cell flashes white and the temperature gauge rockets into red thermal runaway. Switch to the graphite anode and the same ions slot quietly between layers instead.
- **photocatalysis/** — A photon strikes the TiO₂ slab, the blue electron and red hole tear apart to opposite shores, and white and teal bubbles rise in an exact 2:1 rhythm; switch the cocatalyst off and the two colors sprint toward each other, flash, and vanish — the bubbles stop dead.
- **cancer-p53/** — A living cell with a visible DNA double helix: damage particles rain down, p53 tetramers light up and swarm to the breaks while the cycle ring slams to a halt at the glowing G1/S checkpoint. Flip p53 off and mutant cells sail through the red light, blossoming into a runaway clone sphere; the radio/chemo button then shows why p53-intact tumors self-destruct while p53-null ones shrug it off.
- **hox-embryogenesis/** — A wave of light sweeps the Hox cluster bead by bead along the chromosome, and the same colors spread head-to-tail across a segmented embryo wired by collinearity lines. Drag the Antp boundary forward and the head segment instantly swaps antennae for legs — the classic Antennapedia — while gradient strength, knockouts (Ubx off = an extra wing pair) and the fly/vertebrate switch rewrite the whole body map.
- **microtubule-dynamics/** — A fluorescence-view centrosome shoots out six microtubules, each flipping between growth (bright GTP caps) and banana-peel collapse, while live counters track catastrophe frequency. Drag the tubulin concentration and the whole population changes character; press Taxol to freeze the dynamics and stall mitosis, or Colchicine to dissolve everything — and watch a lucky tip catch a chromosome to complete search-and-capture.
- **pain-gate-control/** — Signal particles race from a burning skin spot to the dorsal horn: fat yellow myelinated Aδ arrives in a blink while skinny bare C fibers crawl in late. Then rub the neighboring skin — blue Aβ fibers light up the green interneuron, the gate doors swing half-shut and the ascending stream visibly thins; press endorphin and descending fibers from the PAG slam the gate all the way closed.
- **sleep-brainwaves/** — One whole night compressed to 30 seconds: an oscilloscope morphs between spindles, giant δ waves and awake-like REM while a red EMG line flatlines in REM, and a 48-cell sleep tower fills stage by stage. During N3, glowing memory particles stream from the hippocampus up fibers into the cortex — hit the coffee button to sink the adenosine curve, or switch on slow-wave deprivation and watch tomorrow's memory test score slide.
- **vesicle-transport/** — A vesicle buds off the Golgi, sheds its coat, and rides a kinesin down a striped microtubule; then in slow motion four SNARE helices twist together like a zipper, dragging the two membranes to ~1 nm until a fusion pore blossoms and fluorescent cargo floods out. Press the Ca²⁺ button mid-tether to skip straight to the burst, or flip the switch to watch dynein haul the empty vesicle home retrograde.
- **elastic-rebound/** — Fast-forward the timeline and the fence posts across the locked fault twist into an S while the stress bar creeps red; at rupture the bend snaps into a bare offset step, the road breaks, wave rings race out and a "≈1906 San Francisco M7.9, ~6 m" flag pops when the slip is that big.
- **friction-stick-slip/** — A block rides a moving belt while the spring stress bar climbs to its red peak, then everything jumps at once: force collapses, the energy bar dumps, ripples spread and the sawtooth trace draws itself live. Slow the pull speed and Dieterich-style static-friction healing makes every stress drop more violent; switch to fault mode and the same sawtooth becomes an earthquake.
- **heat-conduction/** — The hot-end lattice jitters violently while bright phonon pulses dart for the cold side, scattering off course as the material gets messier; flip to copper and the blue electron gas outraces them all. In composite-wall mode the temperature profile bends steeply through the foam layer — insulation you can read off the slope.
- **heisenberg-uncertainty/** — Drag the slit slider from wide to narrow and the wavefronts fan out on the screen in real time while the Δx·Δp meter stays pinned above the red ħ/2 line. In atomic-scale mode, squeezing the electron cloud toward the nucleus sends the kinetic-energy bar from 0.4 eV to tens of keV — the pressure that keeps atoms from collapsing.
- **pauli-periodic-table/** — A proton slider adds electrons one by one: each one hops from the nucleus into its shell slot while the element name, flame color and chemical mood cycle past, and the "full shell · inert" badge flashes exactly at Z=2, 10, 18. Beside it the ionization-energy sawtooth draws itself — periodicity made visible.
- **stress-strain/** — The test bar stretches elastically, yields, then pinches into a visible waist before snapping with a glowing fracture face and sparks — while the live dot walks the σ-ε diagram through hardening and the post-necking drop. Hit "unload" past yield and the bar returns along the E-slope but stays permanently longer.
- **cosmic-dawn/** — The orange afterglow of recombination fades to black, the first zero-metal star flares inside a dark halo, and fresnel-lit ionization bubbles swell, kiss and merge while the ionized-fraction bar climbs toward a transparent cosmos; a spectrum window sets Pop III's clean blue continuum against the Sun's metal-lined curve.
- **cosmic-web/** — 32,768 particles start as a near-uniform lattice and, under a precomputed Zel'dovich displacement field, pour themselves into walls, filaments and knots while a live density map recolors the web and lights the richest nodes into galaxies; the 2D slice view and the gain-to-zero switch turn "gravity did this" into something you can watch fail.
- **dark-energy/** — A comoving galaxy grid recolors by recession speed while the Hubble diagram beside it reveals distant SNe Ia sagging off the decelerating curve; flip to the a(t) timeline and drag w past −1 to watch the curve bend from concave-down to concave-up on the spot — and the fate verdict flip from heat death to big rip with it.
- **galaxy-merger/** — Two thousand-star disks swing past twice, throwing mirror tidal tails, then spiral in and relax into one golden elliptical while the star-collision counter sits frozen at 0 with a live cross-section expectation of ~10⁻²⁴ — the emptiness of galaxies made quantitative.
- **orbital-resonance/** — Drag the period-ratio slider across 2:1 and Jupiter's repeated tug plows the highlighted asteroid's trail into a wobbling rosette until it is ejected, while the live belt histogram carves gaps at 3:1, 5:2 and 2:1; the Pluto case plots every 3:2 conjunction safely at ~49 AU, never near Neptune's orbit.
- **rendezvous-docking/** — A scripted retro burn at t+1.2 s sends the chaser dipping below and creeping forward while three readouts tell one story: Δa goes negative, closing rate goes positive, range melts away — braking really is the accelerator; arrive at the corridor faster than 0.5 m/s and the panel calls it a crash.
- **aeroelastic-flutter/** — Slide the wind speed past U_f and the wing's gentle sway turns into a bending-torsion spiral as the amplitude bar goes exponential, the phase meter settling near 90°, until the structure tears and slow-motion shows the wreckage fly. Flip to Tacoma mode: 17 m/s is enough for pure torsion to self-destruct.
- **gliding-soaring/** — The altimeter ticks slowly down until the glider banks into a thermal column, particles streaming up under the wing, and after two circles the vario flips from −0.8 to +2.5 m/s. Drag the airspeed slider and watch the dot ride the live polar curve while the MacCready marker re-solves for headwind.
- **sea-breeze/** — Drag the time slider from 09:00 to 15:00: the isotherms bow up over the warming land, the wind vanes swing onshore one by one, and the sea-breeze front lands with a chain of cumulus — push ΔT high enough and lightning bolts off the front. Slide past sunset and the whole circulation quietly reverses.
- **turbidity-current/** — The gate lifts and muddy water dives beneath clear, its curling mushroom head devouring bed grains down the slope while transatlantic cables snap one by one, each stamped with its cut time — 600 km in about 14 hours, just as 1929's broken cables revealed. At the toe the current chokes on its own sediment and the fan visibly grows.
- **vortex-ring/** — A slow-motion ink puff is curled into a ring right before your eyes, then cruises the whole tank and threads a crossing current unharmed. Switch to jellyfish mode to swim on ring pulses, or to the helicopter: pull the descent-rate slider into the VRS band and watch the tip vortices loop back up through the rotor disc as the lift readout collapses.
- **wing-icing/** — Flying through cloud, droplets stick and the leading-edge horn grows drop by drop while the same angle of attack slides down two lift curves at once — the iced one collapsing toward stall at 8°. Hit the de-icer boots and the horn shatters off in falling chunks as the curves snap back together.
- **binary-heap/** — A complete tree lives inside a plain array, parent i over children 2i and 2i+1, parent-child edges following the spheres as they swap. Insert a 77 and watch the bubble sift up level by level; hit extract-max and the tail element parachutes to the top, sinks in slow motion through the swaps, while every max rolls onto a green sorted shelf.
- **dynamic-programming/** — The exponential fib call tree detonates across the screen, then memoization detonates it back down: gray subtrees hang pruned in mid-air while the call counter collapses from 29,860,703 to 69. Switch to bottom-up and the recursion vanishes into a 36-cell table filling left to right; knapsack mode fills its dp grid cell by glowing cell and backlights the winning items.
- **fft-butterfly/** — A real radix-2 engine up to N=1024 draws its own butterfly circuit: signal nodes pour through bit-reversed entry gates and merge stage by stage while two multiply counters race overhead. Slide N to 1024 and the scoreboard freezes at 1,048,576 vs 10,240 as the last of 5,120 butterflies snaps shut.
- **q-learning/** — A tabular Q-agent trains live in an 8×6 grid with walls and traps you can paint in by clicking, the first flailing episode pinned in red while the greedy path snaps straight. The heatmap brightens into signposts and the arrow field bends toward the goal; set ε=0 and the demo agent spins in place, ε=1 and the heatmap never sharpens.
- **regression-correlation/** — Grab any point and the least-squares line yields in real time, red residual squares breathing with the RSS counter; one added outlier yanks the whole fit across the panel. The Anscombe quartet stands in a row wearing identical r=0.816 lines, and pulling the hidden "temperature" axis out of the ice-cream–drowning cloud shatters the spurious correlation into three flat within-band lines.
- **zipf-power-law/** — Six thousand word-drops fall live with probability ∝ count^α, growing a Matthew-effect skyline while the log-log inset stretches from a bent knee to a clean slope −1 line. Drag α from 0 to 1 and a flat multinomial plateau pulls itself straight in about a second; Brown-corpus words, UN metro areas and Chinese surnames re-fit on the same plot.
- **cpu-cache/** — A real direct-mapped L1/L2/L3 engine (4/12/42/200-cycle latencies) streams a request dot across a DRAM matrix: row-major scan leaves a green sea of L1 hits, flip to column-major and the pass drowns in red misses while the col/row cycle ratio counter climbs past 5x. Toggle hardware prefetch and watch the next line ride ahead of a sequential stream.
- **gpu-rasterizer/** — A 26x16 pixel screen rasterizes two draggable triangles with real edge functions: watch the bounding box sweep pixel by pixel, colors arriving as barycentric blends, rejects bouncing off the z-buffer. Hit the z-fight demo and the overlap shimmers white until the depths separate and the buffer settles it; crank the cores slider and the whole frame fills in a blink.
- **grid-frequency/** — One flywheel stands for every synchronous machine on the grid: click a load step and the wheel audibly slows as frequency tumbles past the 49.9 limit line, plant bars rise in sequence, and AGC walks the trace back to 50.00. Drop the sync share and replay the identical event — the ghost curve shows the low-inertia dip digging twice as deep, twice as fast.
- **optical-mouse/** — The correlation is computed for real: two 18x18 frames stream in a floating panel, a 13x13 SAD heat map blooms with a white peak, and the displacement arrow and mini-screen cursor move in lockstep. Drag the roughness slider to zero and the heat map goes flat, the tracker flags failure in red, and the cursor freezes — exactly why mice die on glass.
- **pacemaker/** — A real timing engine drives ECG and a contracting 3D heart: sinus beats march, the SA node dies for 3 seconds, the strip goes flat, and an orange spike nails the ventricle into an instant wide QRS. Switch to DDD in complete heart block and every blocked P gets a tracked ventricular spike; kill demand sensing and the fixed-rate spikes start landing on T waves with red R-on-T warnings.
- **ventilator/** — Real respiratory mechanics drive every breath: watch the pressure ramp fill a row of alveolar bubbles, then drag PEEP upward and collapsed units pop open one by one, exchange area climbing. Push tidal volume into a stiff ARDS lung and the gauge needle slams past 30 cmH2O into the red barotrauma zone while the waveforms grow spiky.

### Phase 41 deep dives (condensed)

- **screw-jack/** — A cutaway jack lifts a car corner while its helix unrolls into an incline of the same lead angle: the moment ledger T=W·(d₂/2)·tan(λ+ρ′) prices every turn, the self-lock test lets go of the handle and nothing back-drives, and the ball-screw comparison trades 44% efficiency for 90% — along with the lock.
- **cable-stayed-bridge/** — A truck crosses and the load path lights up stay by stay: straight tensioned cables carry the deck to the pylon, vertical components stack into ~800 MN of tower compression, the girder takes the axial squeeze — and cutting the back stays lets the midspan drag the tower top inward in real time.
- **esterification/** — Molecules in a cutaway flask: sulfuric acid protonates the carbonyl, ethanol attacks, water leaves ("acid loses OH, alcohol loses H"), and the ester floats to the top layer; a Dean–Stark trap drains the water and the concentration curves swing toward ester while Q tracks its way to K≈4.
- **copper-refining/** — A crude anode thins itself into Cu²⁺ ions that cross the bath and grow a 99.99% cathode; gold and silver sink into the slime bag, zinc/iron/nickel dissolve but never plate, and the Faraday ledger m=ItM/(zF) draws the cathode-mass line at ~0.3 V.
- **trophic-pyramid/** — Sunlight pours into the base of a glass pyramid and golden energy particles climb, leaking dark-red at every level — respiration, feces, the never-eaten; slide transfer efficiency from 5% to 20% and the top-layer glow, the leak density and the hectares of grass under one hawk all jump together.
- **mycorrhiza/** — A soil cutaway: sugar particles flow root→fungus while phosphorus flows hypha→root across a glowing network; drag the phosphate rock away and the hyphae grow to reach it; cut the network and the seedling's P-intake curve sags as its leaves yellow.
- **diffraction-grating/** — Plane wavefronts meet N slits and the screen combs light into sharp maxima: pull N from 2 to 200 and fat fringes pinch into needles, switch to white light and the rainbow unfolds with overlapping orders, while the live I(θ)=(sinNα/sinα)² trace breathes with the screen.
- **joule-thomson/** — Molecules squeeze through a porous plug with enthalpy unchanged: intermolecular "springs" stretch and brighten as potential energy bills the kinetic, the speed colors darken on the cold side — and switching to helium flips both ends warm, with the T–P working point skating along the isenthalp across the inversion curve.
- **radial-velocity/** — A star wobbles around the barycenter while its absorption lines breathe red and blue in the zoom inset; the RV curve fills with error-barred samples, and tipping the inclination to 0° flattens it into noise — the m·sin i limit made visible.
- **diffie-hellman/** — Three paint stations under the eavesdropper's hood: yellow g is public, secret tints go in private, mixed colors travel the wire, and Alice's and Bob's pots land on the same brown K while Eve's stays one step short; small-number mode runs the real mod-23 arithmetic, and Eve's brute-force counter rolls.
- **cpu-pipeline/** — Instruction blocks ride a conveyor through five arch stations; at full flow one finishes every beat (CPI=1), a RAW hazard lights the forwarding shortcut, a load-use pair injects a bubble, and a mispredicted branch flushes the pipe — watch the CPI trace against the ideal line.
- **water-treatment/** — A cutaway plant train: paddle mixing neutralizes zeta potential, flocs snowball and settle, sand catches stragglers, chlorine guards the clearwell; the turbidity trace steps below the 1-NTU line — and the skip-coagulation control clogs the filter black.

### Phase 40 deep dives (condensed)

- **bldc-motor/** — A cutaway motor with its three-phase bridge exposed: the green resultant-field arrow jumps 60° per commutation while the two-pole-pair rotor chases it, the glowing current path re-routes every step, and a live trapezoidal phase-current trace marks each switch; single-step the sequence, or let Hall sensors and back-EMF zero crossings call the timing while PWM holds the speed.
- **torque-converter/** — A toroidal cutaway slings oil particles from impeller to turbine; stall the turbine and the stator's re-aimed return flow multiplies torque 2.1×, ease off and K slides to 1 as the one-way clutch freewheels, then snap the lockup clutch for a no-slip ~99% drive.
- **tower-crane/** — A trolley drags the load along the jib while the moment ledger compares load arm, counterweight and the 1000 kN·m envelope — the allowable-load hyperbola shrinks toward the tip; cross the line and the tower flushes red and tilts as the compressed chords buckle, with the stress view finding the first strut to go.
- **suspension-bridge/** — A truck crosses and the load-path animation hands the weight from deck to hangers to main cable to towers and anchorages; the parabolic cable and H=wL²/8f update with sag, and a resonance excitation replays Tacoma's lesson.
- **dishwasher/** — A cutaway tub runs fill → heat → wash → rinse → dry: 60–70 °C jets fire from arms that spin on recoil torque alone, enzymes and surfactants drop in on cue, and the rinse-aid meter drags surface tension from 72 to ~25 mN/m so water sheets away instead of spotting.
- **circuit-breaker/** — One series loop, two judges: the bimetal's I²t clock for overloads, the magnetic coil's 10 ms snap for shorts; open the contacts and the arc climbs an 11-plate chute until its voltage overshoots the 230 V supply and strangles the current at a forced zero — thermal, magnetic and reset all replayable.
- **hall-heroult/** — A cutaway cell of 960 °C cryolite with ion traffic in both directions: Al³⁺ plating onto the cathode as molten metal, O²⁻ burning the carbon anode away at 0.42 kg C/kg Al; trigger an anode effect for the spark rain, tap the sump with a vacuum ladle, and read the 13–15 MWh/tonne ledger.
- **seafloor-spreading/** — A mid-ocean ridge extrudes basalt that records polarity below the 580 °C Curie point; flip the field and fresh crust records the opposite, striping both flanks mirror-symmetrically; the age ruler and spreading rates reproduce the 1963 Vine–Matthews–Morley magnetic-anomaly profile.
- **hydrothermal-vent/** — Seawater dives into cracks, exits as 350–400 °C black-smoker fluid, and feeds a chemosynthetic food chain; kill the flow and the ecosystem goes dark; particle loops trace the percolate–heat–vent cycle while the lamp sweep finds the tube worms.
- **honeycomb/** — Wax cylinders settle into hexagons in front of you; switch triangle/square/hex tilings to compare wall length for equal area (4.56 / 4.00 / 3.72), flip to the double-layer comb with its shared 109.47° rhombic bottoms, and watch fanning dry the honey from 80% to 18% water.
- **metamorphosis/** — A caterpillar with its hormone panel exposed: inject a 20E peak to molt, and the JH slider decides whether the next instar is larva or pupa; inside the chrysalis, imaginal discs dismantle ~45% of the dry mass while the titer curves narrate every switch.
- **cyclotron/** — Particles spiral outward between the dees as a fixed-frequency RF gap kicks twice per lap; the radius-energy ledger tracks r=mv/(qB) until the deflector plate ejects them — run the −6% detune demo and relativistic lag walks the beam into the wall.
- **dns/** — A query climbs a glowing domain tree — root, TLD, authoritative — with the answer stamped by a TTL; re-ask and the lit caches answer in ~1 ms, clear them and the full climb replays; hit and miss sit two orders of magnitude apart on the latency chart.
- **genetic-algorithm/** — Sixty balls hill-climb a fitness terrain by roulette selection, crossover and mutation, one steppable generation at a time; the μ=0 experiment strands them on the 0.66 local peak, and re-enabled mutation flings a resampled ball across the valley toward 1.00.
- **tsp/** — Glowing cities wait for a tour; random, greedy and 2-opt runs share the length chart as the red X lifts a crossing pair, reverses the segment and re-seats it shorter — step by step or straight to within 5% of the reference optimum.
- **pumped-storage/** — One shaft, two jobs: daytime generation lights the city's grid band, night pumping hauls the water back uphill; the round-trip ledger books 76 of every 100 units while the emergency stop shows the minutes-scale response the grid is buying.

### Phase 39 deep dives (condensed)

- **blast-furnace/** — A cutaway shaft with burden descending and gas climbing: tuyere flames, CO made from CO₂ + hot coke, ore pellets changing hue stepwise to silver, slag floating over iron in the hearth, and taphole pours on demand; the height–temperature chart slides its three reduction zones with blast temperature.
- **premixed-flame/** — One burner port in cutaway: the jet entrains air through the venturi throat, a pale inner cone sits inside a bright blue mantle; close the shutter and yellow soot beads glow and deposit; drive flow below flame speed for lightback, above blow-off for lift-off — the v–S_L map tracks it all.
- **gas-discharge/** — A glass tube between electrodes: at 760 torr nothing; drag pressure to a few torr and the Paschen-curve working point crosses the line — snap, the avalanche ignites; cathode layers, Faraday dark space, striations in the positive column; swap neon/argon/mercury+phosphor for three identities.
- **fluorescence-phosphorescence/** — A 3D Jablonski sculpture with photon beads riding the transitions: S₁ falls fast (fluoresce), T₁ leaks slowly (phosphor); kill the lamp and the green dies while cyan lingers on an exponential tail; a glow stick pumps itself chemically in the dark room.
- **predator-prey/** — Populations orbit a closed loop in the V–P plane while a time tower stacks the history; Hudson Bay lynx–hare records 1845–1935 plot alongside; toggle logistic damping to spiral into coexistence, cull predators to hop loops.
- **lake-turnover/** — A cutaway lake with a glowing thermocline lid; drag the season and watch the surface densify until one gust flips the whole column — tracers surge up, oxygen sinks; keep going into winter and the 0→4 °C stack re-sorts itself under the ice.
- **galaxy-rotation/** — A spiral galaxy of 2000 stars on true v(r) orbits; dark matter to zero and the outer disks trail behind a collapsing Keplerian curve; back to 85% and the curve pins flat; overlay M33's measured points for the real thing.
- **sunspot-cycle/** — A rotating Sun with latitude markers slipping apart; field lines wind from polar loops into toroidal ropes, buoyant tubes punch through as spot pairs marching equatorward; the butterfly diagram and sunspot number build up cycle after cycle.
- **holography/** — A laser, a beam splitter, object and reference beams meeting at a plate that grows live fringes; hit Expose then Replay: the object's ghost floats behind the plate with parallax while an inverted conjugate hangs on the far side; slide the occluder across and the image narrows but never amputates.
- **hash-table/** — Keys fly through a real FNV-1a hopper into glowing buckets; chains grow, or switch to linear probing and watch clusters metastasize; rehash at the 0.75 line and everything re-flies shorter; a 64-bit Bloom array votes "definitely absent" in green.
- **inverted-pendulum/** — A two-wheel rover balancing on a knife edge; shove it and it dashes toward the fall, brakes, and settles — slow motion to 0.1× to watch the counterintuitive order; switch the controller off and it topples on the exponential.
- **freezing-depression/** — An ice surface at molecular zoom: freeze-on and melt-off arrows tied until salt lands and the tie breaks — a melt pit opens into brine; three basins race as the cold room drops, NaCl dying at its eutectic while CaCl₂ keeps working.

### Phase 38 deep dives (condensed)

- **involute-gears/** — A taut string unwrapped from a base circle sweeps the involute flank; contact glides along the line of action at a constant 20° while the live ratio meter stays pinned to the tooth counts. Drag the center distance ±2%: the pressure angle shifts, the ratio doesn't.
- **gear-pump/** — Two gears meshing in a snug housing carry oil tooth-space by tooth-space from suction (blue) to pressure (red); flow = displacement × rpm (16 mL/rev) and the instantaneous-flow trace pulses once per engagement — the un-machined pump's signature.
- **newtons-cradle/** — Pull one ball, exactly one leaves: momentum and energy conservation leave only two outcomes. The rejected 'half speed each' fails the energy ledger; slow to 0.06× and the impact crosses the row as a compression wave.
- **windshield-wiper/** — One crank drives a parallel rocker pair sweeping both blades across a 43° arc in phase; the intermittent timer is pure RC — watch the capacitor climb, the relay fire one wipe, the park switch drain it, with t=R·C·ln(V/(V−Vth)) updating live.
- **toilet-flush/** — A cut-away toilet runs the whole chain: fast tank dump crests the trap weir, the siphon ignites and gulps the bowl empty, air breaks the film, and the float valve refills while the trickle tube rebuilds the seal — three events marked on the level chart.
- **washing-machine/** — Drag the load off-center and spin up: amplitude spikes past the 12 mm guard near resonance, the machine tumbles the load even and spins again; the damping slider separates bounce-forever (0.2) from one-sway-settle (0.35).
- **fire-extinguisher/** — Squeeze, pierce, and nitrogen drives powder to the flame base; the fire triangle dims edge by edge, radical scavenging snaps the chain reaction, CO₂ floods low and smothers, and the gauge sinking into red is the re-ignition countdown.
- **relay/** — A 5 V coil snaps the armature over and lights a 220 V load; the rolling scope catches the −237 V flyback spike until the diode clamps −0.8 V, contact bounce draws saw-teeth, and the latch mode parallels an auxiliary contact across the start button.
- **reverse-osmosis/** — Membrane pores pass water and bounce hydrated ions; drag the piston past seawater's 27 bar and the flow reverses on the spot, the flux-pressure plot crosses zero at J=A(ΔP−π)=0, and the plant hands 95% of the brine pressure back — 2.4 kWh per tonne, computed live.
- **vulcanization/** — Stretch raw rubber and chains slide, leaving permanent set; crosslink with sulfur and the same pull becomes stretched springs that rebound with overshoot; the density slider sweeps tacky → elastic → brittle along G=3νkT.
- **thermite/** — Ignite the magnesium ribbon and a front eats through 240 powder grains, iron sinking under oxide slag; on the energy-hill chart the spark rides the barrier top then rolls down −851.5 kJ/mol; open the tap and 2500 °C iron pours into a rail-weld mold.
- **photochemical-smog/** — Drag a city day from dawn to dark: NO turns to brown NO₂, UV photolyzes it, ozone accumulates through the VOC-peroxy chain, and the inversion lid rises and falls — all four curves computed from a six-species ODE box model.
- **stomata-guard-cells/** — Two kidney cells bow open as K⁺ and malate pull water in; flip the drought switch and ABA reverses the pumps within minutes; aperture, turgor and transpiration share one model, and the CO₂ slider steals aperture while WUE updates.
- **neuromuscular-junction/** — The AP lights Ca²⁺ channels, vesicles fuse, ACh ferries the 50 nm cleft, the endplate potential crosses −55 mV, and the T-tubule ignites the SR calcium spark; curare and botox break the chain at different links, and the [Ca²⁺]⁴ slider can silence the synapse.
- **gravitropism/** — Lay the seedling sideways: amyloplasts sink, PIN proteins reshuffle, auxin pools on the low flank — shoots bend up, roots bend down, and the signal fades once vertical; a 0–2 g slider and a statolith mutant that never straightens complete the story.
- **turing-patterns/** — Seed noise into a uniform dish and activator-inhibitor dynamics crack it into spots, stripes or mazes; four presets and live F/k/ratio sliders — drop the diffusivity ratio below one and the pattern dissolves on the spot.
- **coriolis-effect/** — Roll a ball across a spinning disk: straight in the inertial frame, an arc in the rotating one, a=2Ω×v arrow attached; the sphere mode flips the sign at the equator, the cyclone mode curls 36 inflow streams into a vortex, and the bathtub ledger computes 0.04 mm — myth busted.
- **bimetallic-strip/** — Brass (α=19) welded to steel (α=12) can't lie flat when heated; drag 20→150 °C and watch the curvature grow, the 3 m spiral sweep 1.8°/K, the snap-disc open at 80 °C and reset at 60 °C, and a 30 A breaker trip in a measured 5.3 s.
- **impact-crater/** — Pick diameter and velocity, watch energy ∝v² hit the ledger: contact compression, a 45° ejecta curtain with secondary chains, terraced walls and a rebounding central peak; the log-log plot carries Barringer and Chicxulub as data points.
- **airship/** — An 8400 m³ helium envelope nets a few hundred kilograms of lift; pump the fore/aft ballonets to pitch, drop 800 kg of ballast to climb, flip to hydrogen for 7% more lift and a Hindenburg-red warning, and vector the thrust for landing.
- **hovercraft/** — The fan climbs the cushion to 2.5 kPa, the hull lifts clear, and the drag trace falls off a cliff; the skirt flexes frame by frame with the waves, three terrains swap the drag table, and over-revving triggers surge and pogo.
- **sand-dunes/** — Saltating grains hop, land and knock loose more; the windward face erodes, sand crosses the crest, the lee avalanches at 34°; scrub time forward and the whole dune migrates downwind, turning barchan or longitudinal as the wind regime demands.
- **river-delta/** — The river brakes at the coast and sorts its load: sand into topsets, silt draping cross-bedded foresets, clay to far bottomsets; distributaries avulse, the delta progrades, and river/wave/tide dominance morphs bird's-foot, arc and trumpet.
- **markov-chain/** — Three weather states, one matrix, three hundred walkers; the heatmap's current row glows, and two cohorts started from different states converge onto the same stationary π, verified live as ‖πP−π‖<10⁻¹⁶.
- **a-star-search/** — On one walled, swampy grid: Dijkstra floods 790 cells, greedy dashes in 38 but pays double through the swamp, and A* finds the identical optimum in 304 — with an ε slider sweeping Dijkstra → greedy.
- **boids-flocking/** — 260 boids in a 3D volume run separation/alignment/cohesion and nothing else; focus one bird for its neighbor shell and three force arrows, tune the weights from flock to school to locust band, drop obstacles, and let the predator send shockwaves through — the order parameter φ is measured live and collapses when the rules are switched off.

### Phase 14 deep dives

#### Microwave oven — standing waves and the turntable

- **What you see**: a 2.45 GHz field flips water dipoles to make heat; the metal cavity reflects to build standing waves, hot and cold spots separated by nodes and antinodes, and the turntable sweeps those spots evenly across the food.
- **How to play**: drag the power, toggle the turntable, and watch the cavity field, dipole arrows and butter-temperature difference evolve; press space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Capacitive touchscreen — from a fingertip to coordinates

- **What you see**: transparent row and column electrodes form a mutual-capacitance grid; a fingertip draws charge away, and the scan chip resolves the touched location from row and column responses. Ordinary gloves fail; conductive gloves work.
- **How to play**: adjust the fingertip position and height, add a second finger, switch glove types, and watch the electric-field lines, capacitance heat map and reported coordinates update.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### GPS — four spheres and one fast clock

- **What you see**: pseudorange spheres meet at the receiver from three satellites; the fourth sphere locks the receiver's clock bias. Special and general relativity together require a ~38 µs/day correction — without it the fix drifts by ~10 km/day.
- **How to play**: drag the receiver around, fast-forward time, and toggle the relativity correction to see the error accumulate; press space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Transistors to adders — gates build calculation

- **What you see**: MOSFET channels open and close to make logic gates; gates assemble XOR, the half-adder, and an 8-bit ripple-carry adder, with carries rippling level by level.
- **How to play**: toggle the A and B inputs, run beat-by-beat or auto, and watch the camera fly from the nanoscale transistor to the gate-level circuit and the 5 + 3 = 8 carry chain.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Fiber optics — light bends around corners

- **What you see**: a core-cladding index gap keeps light bouncing inside the fiber; multi-mode paths smear the pulse, while single-mode fibers (and repeaters) keep the signal crisp.
- **How to play**: drag the bend radius, switch between single- and multi-mode, and watch the light pulse ricochet, leak at tight bends, and emerge at the oscilloscope.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Camera sensor — photons become pixels

- **What you see**: photons pass microlenses and Bayer filters, free electrons inside silicon photodiodes that accumulate in wells, then are read out, quantized and demosaicked into color pixels.
- **How to play**: adjust the incoming light and the ISO, and observe the photon rain, electron water level, row-by-row readout, color rebuild and dark-light noise; press space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Anti-lock brakes — keeping the tires on the grip peak

- **What you see**: wheel-speed sensors compute the slip; ordinary braking drives into the lock region where friction drops and steering is lost. ABS modulates pressure at ~15 Hz to keep the dot near the 10–20 % slip peak.
- **How to play**: switch between dry and wet surfaces, tune brake force and steering, and toggle ABS to compare slip, stopping distance and steering retention.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Wind turbine — the way the wind "lifts" the blades

- **What you see**: lift around the airfoil produces a tangential torque; the rotor delivers wind energy to a generator. Past the rated wind speed, pitch is feathered to cap power; the nacelle yaws to face the wind.
- **How to play**: drag wind speed, pitch and yaw, and enable automatic control to watch the power curve plateau past the rated wind speed.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Nuclear reactor — pinning the chain reaction near criticality

- **What you see**: fission releases neutrons, the moderator slows them so they trigger more fission, and control rods absorb the excess to keep the multiplication factor k near 1. Power falls after shutdown, but decay heat keeps coming.
- **How to play**: drag the control rods, toggle the moderator, hit the SCRAM and cooling switches, and watch k, fission power and decay-heat curves on their different timescales.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### MRI — how spin writes down position

- **What you see**: hydrogen nuclei precess at the Larmor frequency in B₀; an RF pulse tips the net magnetization by 90°, the resulting FID decays with T₂*, and gradients encode position into frequency and phase.
- **How to play**: tune B₀, RF pulse, T₂* and gradients; watch the 3D spins tip, relax and rebuild a one-dimensional profile.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Thermostat — thermal feedback without a chip

- **What you see**: a bimetal strip bends because its two metals expand at different rates, breaking the heating circuit at the threshold and resuming once it cools; switch to the Curie-magnet mode to see the rice-cooker style demagnetization trip.
- **How to play**: adjust setpoint, power and hysteresis, then toggle between bimetal and Curie mode to watch the heat / disconnect / cool / reset cycle.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?p=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Hard drive & flash — two ways to keep a bit

- **What you see**: a write head flips nanoscale magnetic domains to store a hard-drive bit, while flash memory tunnels electrons into a floating gate held by an insulator; both turn physical state into 0/1.
- **How to play**: switch between magnetic and floating-gate modes, trigger writes and erases, and watch the domain flip, electron tunneling and retention.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 15 deep dives

#### Fission chain reaction — a snowball rolled to just-critical

- **What you see**: a neutron is captured by U-235 into wobbling U-236*, which splits into Ba/Kr fragments with a ~200 MeV flash and 2.43 fresh neutrons on average — generations light up 1→3→9→27, one hue per wave. The moderator brakes fast (orange) neutrons into thermal (cyan) ones, lifting the capture cross-section from ~1 to ~585 barns. Rods in: k<1 and the chain dies within generations; rods out: k>1 with a red runaway alert; just right: k=1, a flat self-sustaining rate.
- **How to play**: drag control-rod depth to find criticality, switch the moderator off to see k cap at 0.84, hit ignite to inject neutrons; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?rods=`.

#### Rainbow & secondary bow — why exactly 42°

- **What you see**: white light enters a raindrop and fans into six colors by real water dispersion (n = 1.331→1.343), reflects internally once or twice, then exits; sweeping the impact parameter b shows the exit directions piling up at the deviation extremum — the scattering angles 42° (primary) and 51° (secondary) are why the bows are bright. In sky mode the 42° bow is red-outside/violet-inside, the 51° secondary is reversed, with Alexander's dark band between.
- **How to play**: drag the b/R slider to watch rays bunch at the extremum, toggle one/two reflections and drop/sky views, tap a wavelength swatch to isolate a color; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?mode=` `?k=` `?b=` `?spin=`.

#### Mitosis — an exact halving of one genome

- **What you see**: in a 2n=4 cell, chromatin is replicated into X shapes (two sister chromatids sharing a centromere), the nuclear envelope dissolves, centrosomes move to the poles and grow spindle fibers; fibers search and capture kinetochores, dragging chromosomes onto the metaphase plate (one laggard is pulled in last — the spindle checkpoint); sisters then split synchronously, envelopes re-form, and the cleavage furrow pinches the cell into two genetically identical daughters.
- **How to play**: scrub the phase slider or jump via the six steps; open the contrast note to compare with meiosis (pairing + crossing-over + two divisions → 4 different cells); space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?note=` `?spin=`.

#### The birthday paradox — why 23 people suffice

- **What you see**: every newcomer must dodge all occupied birthday slots — dodge probabilities multiply while pairs explode as n(n−1)/2; at 23 people the collision chance is 50.7 %, at 57 it is 99 %. Roll random birthdays and collisions flash red, arc-linked on the 365-slot year strip; a 2000-trial Monte-Carlo point converges onto the theory curve.
- **How to play**: drag N (1–80), roll again to hunt collisions, run Monte Carlo ×2000 to watch the law of large numbers; step 5 auto-demos the repeated collisions at N=23; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?n=` `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=`.

#### Thermoregulation — the body tunes itself

- **What you see**: the hypothalamus is a comparator — the mismatch between core temperature and set-point drives everything. Cool the environment: skin vessels constrict and blue, muscles shiver for heat. Warm it: vessels dilate red, sweat evaporates away heat. Toggle fever: the set-point steps 37→39 °C while the core is still 37, so you shiver chasing it; on recovery the set-point drops and sweating chases down. A mismatch meter and the core-vs-set-point chart track it all; push the extremes to saturate the loop — hypothermia / heat stroke.
- **How to play**: drag ambient temperature (−10…45 °C), toggle fever and exercise; step 5 replays the set-point chase live; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?env=` `?spin=`.

#### Sonar & B-mode ultrasound — assembling echoes into an image

- **What you see**: a piezo element turns a voltage pulse into sound; the packet travels down at constant speed and every acoustic-impedance interface reflects part of it back; echo time × c/2 is depth — the A-scan peaks align exactly with the 3D scene. As the transducer sweeps, each ping paints one brightness strip into the B-mode image, assembling the fish/organ cross-section line by line; toggle Doppler and flowing red blood cells shift the echo frequency, color-coded red/blue with a live flow-velocity readout.
- **How to play**: switch sonar ⇄ B-mode, fire single pings or run auto, drag target depth; step 5 fast-forwards a full B image; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?mode=` `?dop=` `?dep=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 16 deep dives

#### Cosmic expansion & redshift — it is space that stretches

- **What you see**: galaxies pinned to a comoving grid do not move through space; expansion multiplies every distance by a(t) — switch observer galaxies and everything still recedes (no center); v = H·d is measured live from the sim, not assumed; a photon flying to the observer has its wave train physically stretched by a(t), hue sliding blue→red with live z; a Doppler-contrast mode separates the two mechanisms; run it backwards and everything converges to the starting point.
- **How to play**: scrub the scale-factor slider or let it auto-expand, toggle observer A/B, fire a photon, drag the H constant; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Black hole & spaghettification — shredded first, or through first

- **What you see**: gravity falls as 1/r², so the gradient across a body grows as 1/r³ — far away head and foot feel the same pull, but near the hole the foot wins and the star stretches into a radial noodle, squeezed sideways; the horizon is where even photons fail to climb out (watch photon packets stall and turn back); toggle mass: a stellar-mass hole shreds the star outside the horizon, a supermassive one is 10¹⁰× gentler at the horizon and the star crosses intact; the outside view freezes/redshifts/fades the star at the horizon while the infaller sails through.
- **How to play**: toggle stellar ⇄ supermassive, outside ⇄ infaller view, drag the release distance; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?mass=` `?view=` `?body=` `?spin=`.

#### Gravitational waves — how do you see 10⁻²¹

- **What you see**: two compact objects inspiral on a sagging mesh, stirring compression/stretch quadrupole ripples that travel at c; as a ripple crosses a Michelson interferometer one arm lengthens while the other shortens (ΔL = h·L/2, h ~ 10⁻²¹ — smaller than a proton), the recombined fringe shifts, and the photodetector draws h(t): the inspiral chirp sweeping up in frequency and amplitude, a merger flash, then ringdown.
- **How to play**: drag chirp mass (sweep speed) and source distance (amplitude), toggle +/× polarization, jump steps to the merger; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Superconductivity & the Meissner effect — the field is shown the door

- **What you see**: at room temperature electrons scatter off the lattice (resistance) and field lines pierce the disc; cooling lets the lattice play matchmaker and electrons pair into Cooper pairs (amber→cyan, spring-linked); below Tc = 92 K they condense coherently and resistance drops to exactly zero (cliff in the R(T) inset); the Meissner moment: surface currents expel the field — lines bend around the disc, the key difference from a mere perfect conductor; the expelled field's gradient pops the magnet into levitation; toggle flux pinning to see type-II vortices lock the magnet mid-air, even upside down.
- **How to play**: drag the temperature slider (Tc is ticked) or let it auto-sweep, toggle pinning to compare wobble; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?pin=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 17 deep dives

#### Lead-acid battery — the battery where both plates snow

- **What you see**: on discharge the Pb plate releases electrons and the PbO₂ plate accepts them, and BOTH plates grow white PbSO₄ crystals while the acid is consumed — the electrolyte thins, and the hydrometer float sinks from 1.28 to 1.15 (a mechanic's charge meter); cell voltage follows acid concentration, 2.1 → 1.9 V; switch to charge and the current reverses, the "snow" melts back into Pb / PbO₂ and the acid returns — one of the few chemistries that fully reverses for thousands of cycles; thin grid plates give the huge area behind a car's few-hundred-amp crank; overcharge bubbles are the water-electrolysis side reaction.
- **How to play**: toggle discharge/charge, drag the load to 300 A to see voltage sag and cranking current, scrub the state of charge; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?load=` `?mode=` `?spin=`.

#### Oxyhydrogen & the fire triangle — the math of one-becomes-two

- **What you see**: H₂ and O₂ sit quietly even when mixed (the activation-barrier inset); one spark crosses the barrier locally — H·+O₂→OH·+O·, O·+H₂→OH·+H· — one radical becomes two, the branching tree goes 1→2→4→8, and past the threshold the whole volume reacts at once: 2H₂+O₂→2H₂O, the balloon pops into water mist with a shockwave; at exactly 2:1 nothing is left over and the bang is loudest; the pure-hydrogen jet burns calmly by contrast; the interactive fire triangle — lid off oxygen, water spray off heat, valve off fuel — shows every extinguisher's playbook.
- **How to play**: drag the mixture ratio to find the loudest point, ignite, switch to the pure-jet contrast, try all three ways to kill a flame; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?ratio=` `?mode=`.

#### Acid rain — the distance from pH 5.6 to 4.3

- **What you see**: natural rain is already pH 5.6 from CO₂; SO₂/NOx plumes ride the wind into cloud droplets and oxidize to sulfuric and nitric acid (molecule-level callouts), strong acids dissociate fully and the pH meter slides to 4.3 flashing red (with the ×10-per-unit H⁺ counter); the rain bubbles on a marble statue (CaCO₃+2H⁺→Ca²⁺+H₂O+CO₂↑), the lake fades past pH 5, the forest browns; toggle mitigation — scrubber plus catalytic converter — and the plume dims while cloud pH recovers.

#### Maillard reaction — why seared food smells

- **What you see**: below 100 °C molecules only jiggle (boiling caps at 100 °C, so boiled meat stays grey); past 140 °C a reducing sugar's carbonyl meets an amino group — condensation (a water molecule visibly leaves), Amadori rearrangement into a ketosamine, then hundreds of cracking pathways erupt into flavor particles labeled by family (pyrazines = nutty, furans = caramel, thiophenes = meaty); larger products polymerize into conjugated melanoidin chains and the surface turns golden then brown; a wet surface stalls while it dries; contrast with boiling and with caramelization (no amino group, a different chemistry starting ~160 °C).
- **How to play**: drag the pan past 140 °C for the flavor burst, drag water to see the dry-first stall, switch grill/boil/caramel scenes, try alkaline pH for speed; space to play / pause.

### Phase 18 deep dives

#### Stirling engine — the external-combustion engine that banks its heat

- **What you see**: a transparent cylinder glows red at the burner end and blue at the finned cold end while the displacer shuttles the working gas: isothermal expansion pushes the power piston, the trip through the regenerator deposits the gas's heat in wire mesh (the gradient bar charges), isothermal compression at the cold end costs less work — that difference is the output — and on the way back the mesh hands the heat back (discharge); heat is banked, not dumped, so efficiency approaches the Carnot limit between the same two temperatures; the pV loop traces in sync; external combustion means any heat source works — flame, sun, waste heat; two pistons at 90° phase on one crank self-sustain the cycle.
- **How to play**: drag source temperature (ΔT drives power) and rpm, open the pV chart, tap step 5 to cycle heat sources; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Wankel rotary — three cylinders hiding in one rotor

- **What you see**: inside the figure-8 epitrochoid housing, the three flanks of the triangular rotor form three chambers: each grows past the intake port, gets carried away and compressed, fires at minimum volume, then shrinks past the exhaust port; the chambers are staggered by exactly one shaft turn — three sparks per rotor revolution (eccentric shaft : rotor = 3:1, live counter); no valves and no reciprocating mass make it smooth and high-revving; the highlighted apex seals sweep long paths along the housing — wear, oil thirst and emissions.
- **How to play**: drag rpm, use slow motion to watch the three chambers trade strokes, switch cutaway / see-through views; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Turbocharger — power recovered from exhaust

- **What you see**: red-hot exhaust that would otherwise be dumped spins the turbine past 100,000 rpm (tachometer plus speed-blur rings); the shared shaft drives the blue compressor, packing extra air through the intercooler into the cylinders — more air with more fuel lets a small engine do a big engine's work (contrasted with the crank-hungry supercharger); hit "floor it" and the rpm curve jumps while the boost curve trails — the lag draws itself as the two curves separate; past the boost target the wastegate flap lifts and pressure plateaus.
- **How to play**: drag the throttle, stomp "floor it" to measure the lag in seconds, jam the wastegate to see the overboost warning; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### Pin-tumbler lock — attack and defense on one shear line

- **What you see**: with no key the springs push every driver pin across the shear line and the plug jams (the try-turn jiggle fails); slide a key in and its peaks lift the stacks one by one — the right key lands all five pin gaps exactly on the glowing shear line and the plug turns, throwing the bolt; a wrong key leaves even one stack straddling the line and everything jams (the culprit glows red); the picking demo applies slight tension and lifts each pin until it "sets" — the plug creeps a hair and traps the driver above the line, five sets and it opens; spool security pins fake a set.
- **How to play**: compare right/wrong keys, try-turn to feel the jam, run the picking demo, drag the pin count 3–6; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?pins=` `?spin=`.

### Phase 19 deep dives

#### Altitude & EPO — content = saturation × capacity

- **What you see**: climbing drops inspired PO₂ and arterial saturation sags past the 88% warning; the kidney senses hypoxia (HIF) and pumps EPO into the blood, EPO reaches the marrow (the femur cutaway ejects new cells), and hematocrit ramps along a days-long axis; the key insight: saturation stays low but more hemoglobin means oxygen CONTENT catches up to sea level; on descent the surplus red cells persist for weeks (altitude training); a doping note shows injected EPO bypassing the sensor toward dangerous blood thickening.
- **How to play**: drag altitude (Lhasa 3650 m / Everest base camp marks), scrub acute (hours) ⇄ chronic (weeks) timelines, toggle injected EPO to push hematocrit toward 68%; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?alt=` `?mode=` `?spin=`.

#### Olfactory receptors — one molecule detonates an amplification cascade

- **What you see**: odorants drift over the epithelium and the right shape docks into a GPCR pocket (one receptor accepts several molecules with different affinities); the receptor flexes, the G protein swaps GDP for GTP and splits; the freed subunit lights adenylyl cyclase and cAMP bursts ~100-fold; cAMP opens the cyclic-nucleotide-gated channel, Na⁺ influx depolarizes to threshold and spikes race to the glomerulus; a 3-odorant × 4-receptor matrix lights cell by cell — coffee, lemon and mint each own a pattern code, because the brain reads patterns.
- **How to play**: switch the three odors, drag concentration and airflow to move the spike rate, let step 6 auto-cycle the patterns; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?conc=` `?flow=` `?spin=`.

#### Circadian rhythm — the clock that winds itself

- **What you see**: at subjective morning CLOCK-BMAL1 docks on the per/cry promoters and transcription waves leave the nucleus; by day ribosomes build PER/CRY proteins up a slope; when enough accumulate they dimerize back into the nucleus and pry the activators off their own promoters (the feedback arrow lights); at night phosphorylation and degradation drain the concentration; below threshold the repression lifts and the loop restarts by itself — a 72-hour trace draws the ≈24 h free-running oscillation; time a light pulse: early night delays, late night advances (the phase-response curve — why morning sun beats jet lag), and constant darkness drifts to a 24.3 h period.
- **How to play**: pick a phase and fire a light pulse to watch the curve shift, toggle free-run to watch the drift, speed through three days; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?spin=`.

#### C4 & CAM — plants that give CO₂ an express lane

- **What you see**: a C3 rice leaf in dry heat closes its stomata to save water, internal CO₂ runs out, Rubisco grabs oxygen instead and the photorespiration waste counter spins; C4 corn packs CO₂ into malate with PEP carboxylase (which ignores O₂) in the mesophyll, relays it through plasmodesmata into the bundle sheath and releases it there — the sheath CO₂ gauge jumps ×10, photorespiration freezes at zero, at a cost of 2 extra ATP per CO₂; CAM cacti shift the same chemistry in time: stomata open at night to stock malic acid (the vacuole tank fills) and stay sealed by day while the store feeds the Calvin cycle; a closing strip lines up the three plants' water-vs-ATP ledgers.
- **How to play**: switch the three modes, drag heat/drought to move the stomata, scrub day/night in CAM to fill and drain the tank; space to play / pause.
- **URL parameters**: `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=` `?mode=` `?hour=` `?heat=` `?spin=`.

- **blackbody-radiation/** — An anvil in a dark forge holds an iron ingot whose glow colour is integrated from Planck's curve across the visible band; below 798 K it shines only in infrared. Red light at full intensity moves the ammeter zero; a faint UV beam jets electrons instantly; drag the retarding voltage to V_s and the fastest electron turns back mid-flight. The 12 m column holds the bottom at 2.17 bar where boiling means 121 °C — so the superheated water quietly shimmers until one bubble lifts the column, pressure collapses and the whole core flashes to steam. Heat flux sets the period, throat radius acts as the valve, and dropping a pebble triggers early nucleation when superheat allows. URL: `?Q=` `?r=` `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=`
- **gravity-assist/** — The spacecraft falls past Jupiter on a true integrated hyperbola. In the planet frame, in-speed equals out-speed and the trajectory just bends by δ; flip to the heliocentric frame mid-flyby and watch the speed jump from 13.0 to 23.7 km/s — stolen orbital momentum, with the planet recoiling ~10⁻²¹ m/s. Push the wheel to its red limit and the bus drifts — alarm — then magnetorquers dump the momentum into Earth's field and the ledger drains green. Kp/Kd sliders tune sluggish, oscillatory or critically damped responses. URL: `?ang=` `?kp=` `?kd=` `?t=` `?pause=` `?speed=` `?labels=`

Scanning B walks each mass across the slit and the spectrum grows peak by peak (methanol 31/29/15…). Act two: one pollen grain simultaneously binds two IgE — cross-link, ripple, and hundreds of magenta granules erupt; the vessel wall leaks and the monitor wobbles. ### Phase 34 deep dives (condensed)

- **steam-engine/** — A cutaway horizontal engine: the boiler holds water below and saturated steam above while the fire charges pressure; the eccentric-driven slide valve steams each cylinder end in turn; piston, connecting rod and crank turn reciprocation into rotation and the flywheel smooths the pulses. Watt's governor flies outward with speed and throttles the steam automatically — detach it, shed the load and the rim glows overspeed red. ### Phase 79 · Cross-Family Gap-Fill Batch 49 (24/24 complete)



- [x] The Alkaline Cell (The 1.5 V cylinder in your remote is an internal materials relay: the anode is a zinc-powder gel - not zinc sheet but powder with hundreds of times the surface area, built for high current; the cathode is a compacted ring of electrolytic manganese dioxide that takes electrons by proton insertion into its lattice; between them a nonwoven separator soaked in potassium hydroxide. On discharge zinc oxidizes in the alkali, Zn + 2OH- -> ZnO + H2O + 2e-, while the cathode's MnO2 absorbs one electron plus one proton per step to become MnOOH, and OH- migrates through the separator to keep the books balanced - the electrons themselves refuse the electrolyte and burst out through the top cap, through your remote, and back: that external loop is the whole meaning of 1.5 V. Against the old carbon-zinc cell the alkaline recipe stores 5-10 times the capacity: highly conductive KOH replaces the ammonium-chloride paste, and powder surface replaces the can wall; the price is sealing - overdischarge evolves hydrogen at the anode, pressure builds, and the crimp vents caustic electrolyte onto your contacts. The 1.5 V discharge curve is flat and confident right up to a sudden cliff - which is why devices die without warning. Recharging it is genuinely dangerous: the manganese lattice change is irreversible, the zinc powder grows dendrites that pierce the separator, and internal pressure plus short circuits follow. Drag discharge current to watch voltage sag and capacity shrink, drag temperature to see the electrolyte stiffen; press cutaway to peel the four layers, heavy-current comparison to race a carbon-zinc cell, overdischarge leak to watch the hydrogen bulge. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 剖开 1/4 的圆柱电池:钢壳、MnO₂ 正极环(深棕)、隔膜、锌膏(银灰颗粒感)、中心集电针、顶盖正极帽;离子小球在隔膜内迁移、电子流沿外电路灯泡跑;MnO₂ 晶格嵌入质子的动画。) ✅ **alkaline-cell/**


- [x] Bile: Emulsifying Fat (When fatty food lands in the duodenum, the first thing oil meets is not an enzyme but an emulsifier: lipase only works at the water-oil interface, and a 1 cm globule offers under half a square centimetre of it - the enzyme waits helplessly outside. Bile squeezed from the gallbladder carries bile salts synthesized from cholesterol by the liver - amphipathic molecules whose acid head dips into water while the steroid rings face the oil core; scores of them ring the globule and tear it into 1-10 micron droplets, multiplying the interface about a thousandfold. Pancreatic lipase finally gets to work, anchored by colipase, snipping triglycerides into fatty acids and monoglycerides. The products are still too oily to travel: bile salts and the sheared products assemble into 4-8 nm mixed micelles that ferry fat fragments across the unstirred layer to the enterocyte's brush border. Meanwhile the salts themselves are reclaimed at the ileum's end by the ASBT transporter and ride the portal vein home - about 95 percent recycled, 4-12 loops a day, with only 5 percent freshly made. After gallbladder removal the liver's steady drip still manages, just with post-feast diarrhea; when cholesterol or calcium oversaturates the bile, crystals grow into gallstones - blocking the cystic duct brings fatty-pain attacks, blocking the common bile duct brings jaundice and pancreatitis together. Drag bile-salt concentration to watch droplet size, drag fat load to see enzymes queue; press with/without bile for steatorrhea, gallstone blockage for a stalled pipeline, micelle commute to follow one fat fragment into a villus. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] Bone Conduction (Hum with your ears plugged and the song stays clear - that route is always working: sound reaches the cochlea by two paths, air conduction (the main one: canal, eardrum, three ossicles, cochlea) and bone conduction (vibration straight through the skull). Bone-conduction headsets promote the backup to the main road: transducers on your temples set the whole skull micro-vibrating, cochlear fluid takes up the wave directly, hair cells fire as usual - ear canals stay open, ambient sound fully audible, traffic behind you included on a run; Beethoven composed with a rod clenched in his teeth after going deaf, on this very path. Clinically, bone conduction is a diagnostic key: in the Weber test a vibrating tuning fork on mid-skull sounds louder in the affected ear for conductive loss - with the canal's ambient masking gone, the bone signal stands out - while sensorineural loss hears it in the healthy ear. The Rinne test compares the two paths in one ear: normal hearing gives longer air conduction, conductive loss reverses it - together the two localize the lesion on the spot. The weakness is high frequencies: the skull is a low-pass filter, rolling off above 4 kHz, so bone conduction suits calls, navigation and sport, not the studio. Drag volume/frequency to split the two paths' response, drag air-conduction loss to simulate conductive deafness; press two-path comparison, Weber test for the fork's lean, Beethoven mode to bite the rod. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Camera Flash (A flash tube dumps fifty kilowatts for a millisecond - twenty times an electric kettle - fed by a single 3.7 V lithium cell. The magic is three steps: a boost circuit (flyback transformer plus rectifier) lifts 3.7 V to 300-340 V and stores it in the main capacitor - the "recycle" that takes 1-5 seconds, its hum and click the sound of charging; at the shutter, a trigger coil stacks on a few-thousand-volt pulse that ionizes the xenon gas into a plasma channel; the main capacitor then dumps tens to two hundred joules through that channel in a millisecond, exciting xenon into a continuous spectrum across all visible wavelengths - about 5500 K, nearly identical to noon daylight, which is why flash fill-light looks like no light at all. Guide number = distance x aperture: GN 36 at ISO 100 means f/10 exposes correctly at 3.6 m. Modern TTL systems fire a 1/1000-power preflash before the real exposure, meter through the lens, compute the output, and let the main flash finish - the two pulses tens of milliseconds apart read as one. Recycle time is the burst-shooting constraint: press early and you get half brightness; LED continuous lights handle video but trail xenon by two orders of magnitude in peak output - millisecond-scale power is still the capacitor-and-gas monopoly. Drag battery voltage for boost output, drag stored energy for recycle time; press discharge slow-motion for the 1 ms curve, GN calculator to solve an exposure live, TTL preflash to see the double blink. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] CRC Cyclic Redundancy Check (On network cables, inside zip archives, between SSD and memory, trillions of CRCs stand guard daily, and their entire mathematics is one sentence: read the bit string as a polynomial over GF(2) - coefficients are 0 or 1, addition is carry-free XOR - divide by an agreed generator, append the remainder; the receiver divides again, and a nonzero remainder means corruption. Without carries, division shrinks to shifts and XORs, and hardware is a row of flip-flops with a few XOR gates (an LFSR): division happens in flight, one gate per bit, a billion divisions a second on gigabit wire. Error detection is precisely controllable: any generator with two or more nonzero terms catches every single-bit error; an r-th order CRC detects all bursts of length up to r - CRC-32's 32-bit remainder catches any burst within 5 bytes and guarantees double-error detection for messages shorter than 2^31 bits. But be clear: CRC is not a cryptographic hash - it defends against errors, not adversaries, who can compute a valid CRC for a malicious message; TLS adds HMAC on top. Ethernet's 4-byte FCS, ZIP's CRC-32, Bluetooth and USB CRC-16/32 are all this 1961 mathematics still on active duty. Drag the generator to swap CRC-8/16/32 and watch detection ranges, drag error injection to flip bits; press long division to step through shift-and-XOR, single-bit error to see the remainder alarm, burst error to flip five bits at once. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Deep Space Network (Voyager 1's transmitter is 23 watts - a refrigerator bulb - yet from 24 billion kilometres away its sentence takes a 70-metre dish hours to catch, arriving at about 10^-18 watts: an attowatt, hundreds of quadrillions of times fainter than a snowflake landing. The engineering behind that call is NASA's Deep Space Network: three stations at Goldstone, Madrid and Canberra, spaced 120 degrees in longitude, handing the antenna aim to each other as the Earth turns - a spacecraft is never out of touch for more than one sunrise. The inverse-square law is the enemy of the whole design: four times the distance costs sixteen times the power, so the answer attacks on three fronts - a bigger dish (70-m reflector, Ka-band 32 GHz), a colder receiver (cryogenic preamps at a few kelvin), and smarter coding (from early 1200-bps convolutional codes to Turbo/LDPC, more than ten times the data rate at the same power). Light-time is a second kind of loneliness: press "burn" and the command flies 22 hours to Voyager, then 22 more to hear "received" - one handshake consumes a day, fault tolerance must be pre-computed, and onboard autonomy becomes the only option. Antenna arraying squeezes out the last margin: phase-align and sum several dishes to synthesize one bigger ear; China, India and Europe run their own deep-space stations doing the same - deep-space communication is humanity negotiating with the inverse-square law. Drag target distance to watch the signal cone spread and the power fall, drag data rate for coding gain; press light-time round trip for a 44-hour handshake, power budget for the dB ledger, antenna arraying to fuse three dishes into one. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Difference Engine: Mechanical Carry (A hundred years before Bletchley Park, the computer was a brass dream: Babbage designed the Difference Engine in 1822 for one dull job - tabulating nautical tables. Polynomials can be tabulated without any multiplication: the n-th finite difference of an n-th-degree polynomial is a constant, so each column of registers just adds its own value to its left neighbour, the constant differences cascade upward, and the leftmost column rolls out successive polynomial values - for the "prime factory" x^2+x+41 it churns out 41, 43, 47, 53, 61, 71... all by pure addition. The real difficulty is carrying: adding 1 to a wheel showing 9 must nudge the tens wheel, and if that one also shows 9 the carry erupts into a chain. Babbage solved it with skewed "anticipating carriage" gears - carry requests queue up on the ramps first, then fire in one unified stroke after each wheel finishes, compressing the worst case from digit-by-digit serial propagation into two beats. The full machine was 6th order, 31 digits, 25,000 parts; a seventh-scale section built in 1832 dazzled, and in 1991 the Science Museum built the 15-ton engine from his drawings alone - it runs with zero error, proving the design was sound all along. The Scheutz father-and-son team built the first working machine in 1853 and printed decades of tables for Britain and America. In the demo six columns of figure wheels add column by column with each crank, carry ripples flashing down the digit chain as the output rolls out primes. Drag the steps slider to crank continuously, drag the order slider to switch x^2/x^3 or higher; press prime run for 30 steps, carry closeup to slow-motion 999+1, anticipating carriage to watch the ramp gears queue and fire. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] Fish Osmoregulation (The same fish is a leaky net in freshwater and a drying sponge in the sea - osmosis always pulls water from dilute to concentrated, and freshwater versus saltwater fish face opposite versions of the problem. Teleost blood sits near 300 mOsm: freshwater is 5-50, so water floods in and salts leak out - freshwater fish simply don't drink; the kidney makes copious dilute urine (about a third of body weight per day) and gill chloride cells pump Na+/Cl- back in. Seawater is ~1000: water leaves, salts invade - saltwater fish gulp seawater (7-35 percent of body weight daily), the gut absorbs water plus monovalent salts, and the excess NaCl is actively pumped out by gill chloride cells, where NKCC cotransporters ride the gradient their basolateral Na/K-ATPase builds, while divalent magnesium and calcium trickle out via kidney and gut. Sharks take a third road: they retain urea and TMAO to match seawater osmolality, skip the drinking, and let gills deal with NaCl alone. Migrating salmon shift gears between the two systems: before entering the sea their chloride cells remodel from salt-absorbing to salt-secreting, prolactin and cortisol handing over the keys; drop a freshwater fry straight into the ocean and the gills "burn" while the remodel takes days. Adult fish skin barely passes water - the gills, a fraction of the body surface, run over ninety percent of the ion traffic. Drag salinity to flip the water flux on the spot, drag pump activity for gill salt rates; press chloride cell closeup to watch the enzyme pumps ride their gradient, salmon shift for the two-system changeover, shark plan for the urea strategy. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Guitar Pickup (An unplugged electric guitar is dull; everything on the amp comes from magnets plus a coil: the pickup's pole pieces partially magnetize the steel string - the string itself becomes a magnet. As it vibrates over the poles, the flux threading the coil rises and falls, and Faraday's law pays out: millivolts to hundreds of millivolts of alternating voltage, its frequency the string's, its harmonics the string's - the pickup is not a microphone; it reads the string's mechanical motion directly, air not involved. The single coil's curse is hum: thousands of turns make a fine antenna, and 50/60 Hz mains hum arrives as-is. In 1955 Gibson's Seth Lover doubled up: two coils wound in opposite directions with reversed pole polarity (the humbucker) - mains hum induces identical currents in both and cancels, while the string, seen through reversed poles, induces opposite currents that subtract into addition: noise cancels, signal reinforces, two birds one stone. Pickup position is a second tone knob: the bridge sits near the string's fixed end where high harmonics have nodes - bright and biting; the neck sits near antinodes, fundamentals strong - warm; one switch flicks half the timbre. Drag string amplitude to watch flux swing, drag pickup position to slide the tone; press single/double comparison to watch hum cancel, field slow-motion for the string squeezing field lines, harmonic nodes for why position changes tone. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Gyrocompass: Finding True North Inertially (A magnetic compass is useless on a steel ship: the hull's magnetism can drag the needle tens of degrees off. In 1908 Anschuetz and Sperry each offered the fix - no magnetism, inertia instead: a fast gyro's axis holds its direction in the inertial frame while the Earth turns beneath it at 15 degrees per hour, so standing on the ship you see the axis drift relative to the ground at a horizontal rate of 15 deg x sin(latitude) per hour. The trick is a pendulous weight: once the axis leaves the east-west horizontal, Earth's rotation makes its tip rise or dip, gravity on the weight then produces a precession torque that pushes the axis toward the meridian - Earth as the engine, gravity as the rudder - and the axis spirals onto true north, settling within minutes once damping is added. It reads true north, not magnetic, needs no declination correction, and ignores electromagnetic interference; submarines, warships and ocean liners still use it as the attitude reference. Its costs: power-up time, and effectiveness fading above roughly 75 degrees latitude. On the phase plane it is obvious: undamped, the axis tip draws an ellipse around equilibrium; damped, a spiral converging on north. In the demo the Earth rotates beneath while the tip trace lights up on the gimbal. Drag latitude to watch the drift rate follow sin(phi), drag initial offset to change the start; press undamped oscillation for the ellipse, damped convergence for the spiral, iron-ship comparison to watch a magnetic compass fail below decks. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
