- [x] The Halting Problem (In 1936, 24-year-old Turing proved computing's first cornerstone and drew its first ceiling in the same stroke: no program H can decide, for every program P and input I, whether P run on I halts. The proof takes five steps: assume H exists; build the adversary D - read P, ask H whether "P fed itself" halts, and if the answer is yes, loop forever, if no, halt immediately; now feed D to itself. If H says D(D) halts, D loops; if H says it doesn't, D halts - both contradict the verdict, and the only exit is that H never existed. This self-referencing trick is isomorphic to Godel's incompleteness three years later - Godel built "this statement is unprovable," Turing built "this program negates its own verdict on itself," the same diagonal. The fallout is bigger than it looks: Rice's theorem proves any nontrivial semantic property of programs - "is this bug-free," "is this code malware" - undecidable, not hard but mathematically nonexistent. Engineering retreats by narrowing, not surrendering: type systems rule out whole error classes, bounded model checking looks N steps deep, tests and static analysis cover common patterns - but "will this loop terminate" forever admits only per-program answers, never a universal bullet. Drag the program sample to switch the suspect, drag the step limit to stall the simulator; press paradox live to watch D eat D with both lamps dying, diagonal grid for Godel's twin proof, Rice's theorem for the property-decision frontier. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Ionosphere & Skywave (A shortwave transmitter of a few hundred watts talks from Beijing to Argentina - not by crawling around the globe but by bouncing off a mirror in the sky. Solar UV and X-rays ionize the upper atmosphere between 60 and 500 km into plasma: electrons stripped from atoms form the D layer (60-90 km, daytime only), E (90-150 km), and F (150-500 km, splitting into F1/F2 by day). The key plasma number is the plasma frequency, f_p = 9 x sqrt(N_e) Hz with N_e in electrons per cubic metre; waves below it get pushed back as a whole - frequency picks your door: longwave reflects off D, shortwave 3-30 MHz punches through D and folds back at F, and anything higher escapes to space. Ground waves hug the earth for a hundred kilometres while skywaves skip between ground and F layer, 2000-4000 km per hop - three hops cross an ocean; launch elevation sets the hop distance. Day-night is shortwave's breathing: D is an absorber that eats medium wave by day and evaporates at sunset, which is why AM radio blooms at night. A solar flare thickens D within minutes and the whole HF band goes silent - the 1859 Carrington event arced telegraph keys, and a 1989 storm collapsed Quebec's grid in ninety seconds. GPS pays the ionosphere too: signals are delayed in transit, and dual-frequency correction uses the differential to back out total electron content. Drag frequency to see which layer takes you, drag local time for the layer heights, drag launch angle for hop distance; press skip zone to watch the skywave fly overhead and land far away while the near field hears nothing, solar storm for F-layer disruption, day-night switch for medium wave's midnight run. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Knuckleball (What batters fear is not the 160 km/h fastball but the 100-120 km/h barely-spinning knuckleball: the seams perturb the boundary layer, separation points go asymmetric, a side force appears - but not a constant one. As the ball rolls a quarter turn, the force slowly swaps sides and the flight turns serpentine, drifting 30-40 cm late in its path; even catchers drop it. Volleyball's float serve is the same physics: a no-spin serve hits the Reynolds range where the boundary layer flips from laminar to turbulent, separation hops back and forth, the wake swings, and the ball wobbles as if breathing - receivers everywhere commit the wrong way. Football's knuckle free kick is its cousin: Cristiano Ronaldo's near-spinless shots dive and drift at the goal like the power was cut. The principle is a sensitive Reynolds band around 1-2x10^5, where transition is mid-flight and a seam decides which side separates first; a spinning ball's Magnus force is steady and predictable, while a non-spinning ball's asymmetry wanders with attitude - pure chaos from seam orientation alone. Wind-tunnel data put the lateral acceleration at 3-5 g: a ball that changes lanes mid-flight. Drag ball speed across the sensitive band, drag spin to feel the gulf between 0 and 1 rev/s; press spin comparison for a predictable Magnus arc, wake flip to slow-motion the separation swap, volleyball float for another sport's version. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Miller-Urey Experiment (In a University of Chicago basement in 1952, 25-year-old Stanley Miller moved "where did life come from" into glassware: the upper flask held methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour - Urey's proposed reducing early-Earth atmosphere, with not a whisper of oxygen. A lower flask boiled water to make rain; between them a pair of electrodes spat continuous 60 kV sparks, playing lightning for eons. Vapour carried the gases through the arc, the condenser rained the products back into the water phase, and the boil recirculated them - a closed water loop letting products hide from further bombardment. After a week the water turned amber: glycine, alanine and eleven amino acids were in there, and in 2008 a modern liquid-chromatography re-run of samples archived for 54 years counted 22. The chemistry is clear too: the spark splits CH4/NH3/H2O into HCN and aldehydes, and the three-step Strecker synthesis stitches cyanide, aldehyde and ammonia into amino acids - life's basic bricks self-assemble given a reducing atmosphere and some energy. The experiment did not replay biogenesis; it executed "organics require life" as a doctrine. The real early Earth may have run more of this chemistry at hydrothermal vents and via meteorite delivery, but the verdict stands - and Cassini's mass spectrometer found the same chemistry brewing in Titan's haze on the way down. Drag discharge power for product rate, drag time acceleration to fast-forward a week; press oxygen control to swap in a modern atmosphere and watch yield vanish, product list to flip the amino-acid name cards, one-week run to see the amber deepen. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Millikan Oil-Drop Experiment (How much charge does an electron carry? Millikan's 1909 answer: challenge it with a drop of oil. An atomizer mists oil droplets into a parallel-plate capacitor, where they pick up charge from friction or X-ray-ionized air. First let a droplet fall at terminal velocity - Stokes drag scales with radius, so the fall speed nails the droplet's mass. Then switch on the field and tune the voltage until the droplet hangs motionless: electric force has flattened gravity, qE = mg, and one substitution yields the droplet's total charge. Millikan repeated this thousands of times, logging voltage, fall speed and hover voltage, and found every charge an integer multiple of 1.59e-19 C; his 58-drop dataset published 1909-1913 fixed both e and, with the charge-to-mass ratio, the electron's mass - Nobel Prize, 1923. The beauty is that quantization becomes visible: multiples line up on a log plot as evenly spaced stairs. The controversy came later: historians found he published only selected runs while claiming "all the data" - one of the most-cited cases in data ethics. The oil drop still runs in undergraduate labs, now as the classic way to calibrate airborne dust particles. Drag plate voltage to lift and lower drops, drag droplet select to change one; press hover calibration to solve q = mgd/V live, X-ray pulse to watch charge jump stairs, data-table replay to leaf through the 1909 notebook. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 两块平行板电容器(可剖视),喷雾器喷出油滴;油滴上下运动受重力/阻力/电场力;悬停时金色光环;电荷整数倍阶梯图 HUD;X 射线管侧照。) ✅ **millikan-oil-drop/**


- [x] The Parker Solar Probe (The corona's temperature paradox stood for eighty years: the photosphere is 5500 C, yet the corona above it burns at a million degrees - thermodynamics forbids heat flowing from cold to hot, and the answer, buried in magnetic reconnection and wave dissipation, can only be tested up close. That is the Parker Solar Probe's job: its December 2024 perihelion passed within 9.86 solar radii of the sun's center, about 6.1 million kilometres, at 192 km/s the fastest human-made object ever. But you cannot simply dive sunward - Earth's 30 km/s of orbital angular momentum will not let go, and the orbit just keeps circling; Parker brakes with Venus: seven flybys siphon off angular momentum, walking the perihelion down step by step. The price is the sun-facing bake: the 11.4 cm carbon-foam shield glows 1377 C on its front while the instrument deck behind it stays room temperature - insulation comes not from bulk but from a reflective coating and radiative cooling throwing heat back into space. The two solar arrays mostly hide in the shield's shadow, and the exposed tips run on circulating water cooling; the whole thermal system fits inside a sub-kilowatt budget while facing 500 times Earth's solar intensity. And it came back with a clue: flying through the corona it found magnetic "switchbacks" - swarms of S-shaped field kinks, possibly key evidence for coronal heating and solar-wind acceleration. Drag perihelion distance to shrink the orbit and watch the temperature curve, drag time acceleration for the seven-year mission; press Venus assist to replay a braking flyby, shield cross-section for the temperature gradient, corona traverse for the switchback kinks. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] Room Acoustics & Reverberation (In a concert hall the last note doesn't stop - it decays exponentially, a tail called reverberation, built in three layers: the direct sound arrives first and sets localization and clarity; early reflections within 50 ms bounce off walls and ceiling and fuse perceptually with the direct sound, supplying spaciousness and a sense of the room's size; then thousands of later reflections crisscross, energy decaying exponentially with the room's absorption. The time to decay to one millionth (-60 dB) is RT60. Sabine's 1898 classic says RT60 = 0.161 V/A: concrete absorbs just 0.02, heavy curtains 0.5, anechoic wedges 0.99 - double the absorption in the same volume and the reverb time halves. Targets differ completely: churches and symphony halls want 1.8-2.2 s tails that smear sound into one; theaters and classrooms squeeze to 0.8-1.2 s for speech; studios go below 0.3 s - an over-reverberant classroom is a hidden tax on learning. Two parallel walls bounce a flutter echo back and forth; the echo/reverberation boundary sits at 50 ms, where a single strong reflection becomes audible as "two sounds" - which is why theater rear walls are treated with absorption or diffusion. Drag room volume and absorption materials to recompute RT60 live, drag listener position for the direct/early/late split; press classroom vs concert hall to switch presets, parallel-wall flutter for the doubled sound, impulse decay for the -60 dB curve. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 剖开的厅堂:舞台声源发出声线束(直达绿/早期黄/晚期红),墙面材质色块(吸声系数标注);能量-时间衰减曲线 canvas;听音位置小人。) ✅ **room-acoustics/**


- [x] The SOFAR Channel (Sound travels through seawater far and strangely: near the surface, warm water gives about 1500 m/s; as temperature drops with depth the speed falls to a floor near 1480 m/s at roughly 1000 m; below that temperature stops changing, pressure takes over, and speed climbs back at about +1.7 m/s per 100 m. This U-shaped profile makes a natural waveguide: sound rays always bend toward slower water - heading up into fast water folds them back down, heading down into fast water folds them back up - so a source near the axis stays trapped in the Deep Sound Channel (SOFAR, Sound Fixing And Ranging) around 1000 m, oscillating between surface and floor, spreading only cylindrically. Low frequencies barely attenuate - a few decibels per 2000 km - so a blue whale's moan crosses 3000 km to a distant herd; during the Cold War the Navy planted SOSUS hydrophone arrays on the axis and picked up Soviet submarines leaving port thousands of kilometres away; in WWII, downed pilots dropped a "SOFAR bomb" that sank to the axis and detonated, and shore stations triangulated the rescue - the same physics that puts 37.5 kHz pingers on black boxes. Climatologists now run it in reverse: sound speed is exquisitely sensitive to temperature, so timing pulses along the channel takes the ocean's temperature (the ATOC experiment). Drag source depth to release or trap the rays, drag frequency for attenuation; press ray tracing to watch the rays swing in the channel, convergence zone for sound surfacing every 50-60 km, whale call to follow one voice across an ocean. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 大洋剖面(海面/1000 m 谷底/海底);侧面声速-深度曲线联动;声源与射线束(困在声道内来回弯折);鲸与水听器;会聚区亮带。) ✅ **sofar-channel/**


- [x] The Steam Turbine (More than half of the world's electricity takes its final step through the same machine: superheated steam at 540-600 C and 16-28 MPa blasts into a steam turbine, and bladed wheels convert heat into shaft torque. The job is one sentence - let steam relieve its pressure step by step, each stage converting a small slice of pressure energy into velocity, then into mechanical work: stationary nozzles accelerate steam to hundreds of metres per second, moving blades turn that kinetic energy into rotation; impulse blades only redirect, reaction blades act as half-nozzles themselves, expanding the steam further as it passes. The hard part is volume: as pressure falls stage by stage, specific volume swells a thousandfold, last-stage blades grow to 1-1.5 m, and tip speed approaches 600 m/s - past the speed of sound, with materials racing both centrifugal load and wet-steam droplet erosion. After the last stage, steam lands in the condenser at 5 kPa of deep vacuum, squeezing out more available enthalpy: the condensate is not waste but permission - without a low-pressure endpoint, the upstream expansion cannot be completed. Reheat and regeneration push efficiency to 45 percent: HP exhaust returns to the boiler for a second superheat, extraction steam preheats feedwater, and every gram of coal saved is money. Drag main-steam pressure/temperature to reshuffle stage drops, drag condenser backpressure to resize the last blades; press velocity triangle to slow-motion the momentum swap inside a blade row, last-stage erosion to watch droplets chew the tips, vacuum comparison for the efficiency ledger. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 剖开的汽轮机轴系:高压/中压/低压缸一串,叶片列由小到大;蒸汽路径按温度/压力着色;喷嘴+动叶速度三角形动画;末级长叶片与水滴;冷凝器端。) ✅ **steam-turbine/**


- [x] The Thyroid & Iodine (The butterfly-shaped gland at the front of your throat holds the throttle for your whole metabolism, and its fuel is an element you eat by the milligram: iodine. The NIS sodium-iodide symporter on follicular cells pulls iodide against its gradient, powered by the sodium gradient the Na/K pump maintains - thyroid iodine concentrates to 20-40 times plasma. Thyroperoxidase oxidizes iodide with hydrogen peroxide and hangs it on tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin; two iodinated tyrosines couple to yield T4 and the more potent T3, all stored in the follicle's colloid - one of the body's few strategic reserves, weeks deep. Each pulse of TSH from the pituitary makes follicle cells swallow colloid, digest it, and release hormone into blood; T3/T4 land on nuclear receptors and upregulate Na/K-ATPase and thermogenic uncoupling, lifting basal metabolic rate, heart rate and temperature. And when T3 rises in blood it squeezes the pituitary's TSH back down - a textbook negative-feedback thermostat. Starve it of iodine and TSH is stuck high, follicle cells multiply in compensation, and the neck swells into endemic goiter; with iodized salt now global, that map has largely faded, yet about two billion people still fall short. Drag iodine intake to watch NIS uptake and colloid stores, drag TSH level for release rhythm; press iodine deficiency & goiter to see compensatory swelling, hyperthyroid mode for a jammed throttle, feedback loop to trace pituitary to target cell and back. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 半个甲状腺滤泡剖面:胶体球腔、单层滤泡细胞、基底侧毛细血管;NIS 泵闪蓝光抓碘;TPO 在顶端膜氧化;T₄/T₃ 四环分子模型进入血管;远处垂体小人发射 TSH;靶细胞线粒体加速;反馈弧线。) ✅ **thyroid-iodine/**


- [x] Tries & Autocomplete (Type "apr" into a search box and candidates appear in 0.1 seconds - not fuzzy matching across a hundred thousand entries, but a trie: each node is one character, each root-to-node path a prefix. Three characters land you three steps down, and query cost depends only on word length, not dictionary size - a hundred thousand words or a hundred million, still three steps. A hash table answers a single word just as fast, but it shreds prefix information: words starting with "ap" scatter across buckets, and finding all of them means a full scan. A trie gathers shared prefixes onto one path; walk to the node and take its whole subtree - prefix queries come free with the descent. Candidates then rank by frequency: every node keeps a counter, and past queries push hot words to the top of the suggestions - that is where the top three come from. The cost is memory: character-level branching creates sparse nodes, so production systems compress single-child chains (radix trees) or pack the trie into double arrays; routers invented an isomorphic use - IP forwarding tables are tries over binary bits, and 200.100.5.x resolves by longest-prefix match, a /24 specialized route beating a /8 default, a tree forwarding quintillions of packets a day. Drag the query to light up the descent, drag dictionary size to watch the step count refuse to move; press linear scan to see naive search crawl, IP routing for longest-prefix match, compression for the node count collapsing. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 3D 节点树(球+连线,字符标签);查询字符逐个下行点亮;命中子树整体高亮;候选词气泡按频率弹出;对照面板:线性扫描进度条 vs 树 3 步完成。) ✅ **trie-autocomplete/**


- [x] The Vending Machine (A vending machine must answer three questions in three seconds: is this money, is it enough money, and did the product drop. A coin sliding in first passes the size gate - wrong diameter or thickness diverts it straight to the return slot; then the material test: a bank of electromagnetic sensors measures eddy-current response and conductivity, and a steel-core counterfeit betrays itself by its signature. Only then is the balance credited. With enough credit a button selects a helix rack: the motor turns the coil exactly one revolution, pushing the front item off the shelf; as it falls into the bay it breaks an infrared beam - drop confirmation. Only a broken beam allows the sale to settle and change to be paid; a beam left unbroken means a hang-up, and the machine returns the credit automatically. The expensive part of the loop is trust: Japanese machines alone churn through hundreds of billions of coins a year, and scams from string-tied coins to slugged tokens forced the combination of optical confirmation, weight checks and one-way return slots. In the demo, follow one coin through validation, then watch a helix turn one full revolution to vend. Drag coin cadence to keep feeding coins, drag helix turns to study the dispensing kinematics; press counterfeit attack to watch a steel-core coin bounce back, jam detection to see an unbroken beam trigger a refund, change-making for a rain of coins. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 玻璃柜+三层螺旋货道(弹簧螺线+商品圆柱);投币口→斜坡滚道→尺寸门(两道缝)→传感器线圈(发光环)→储币箱;出货口红外光束(红色光带);退币槽;硬币小球沿轨道滚动的物理。) ✅ **vending-machine/**


- [x] X-Ray Grazing Optics (X-rays are famous penetrators, and that very penetration makes them impossible to image with ordinary telescopes: hitting a surface near normal incidence, they neither reflect nor refract - they tunnel in and are swallowed. Until the 1970s every orbiting X-ray "telescope" was just a counter with no sense of direction. The fix is grazing incidence: below a critical angle - about one degree at a few keV - X-rays skip off a surface like a stone on water, totally externally reflected. Wolter's 1952 scheme became the standard: a paraboloid funnels parallel light toward focus, then a hyperboloid adds a second reflection that cancels on-axis aberration - Cassegrain in X-ray form, each mirror stretched into a nearly parallel shallow cone. One shell collects too little light, so dozens of polished thin shells nest at a common focus: XMM-Newton stacks 58 gold-coated shells for 4300 cm2 of collecting area, while Chandra's four shells reach a record 0.5 arcsec resolution - able to read a coin on the Moon. The cost is a 10-metre focal length; Chandra had to fly on a highly elliptical orbit - 16,000 km perigee, 133,000 km apogee, beyond the Moon - staying clear of Earth's radiation belts and blockages. Drag photon energy to watch the critical angle narrow, drag grazing angle to collapse reflectivity; press normal-incidence failure to see photons pass through, Wolter path to follow one double reflection, nested shells to watch the collecting area stack. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 平行入射 X 射线束(品红);普通镜面(光线穿过并标红「穿透」);沃尔特嵌套壳层(多层浅锥)光线两次掠射汇聚;焦平面 CCD 亮斑成像;角度标注。) ✅ **xray-grazing-optics/**


- [x] Zeolites & Molecular Sieves (Grind pore size into a ruler accurate to 0.1 nm and you can sieve molecules by size and shape - that is what zeolites do: silicon and aluminum tetrahedra share oxygen atoms into a cage-within-cage framework; aluminum carries one charge less than silicon, so every Al site leaves a negative charge balanced by sodium, potassium or calcium cations - and those cations are the exchange players. Pore size is the door: 3A (0.3 nm) admits only water (deep ethanol drying), 4A (0.4 nm) water plus oxygen and nitrogen (air dried to a -100 C dew point), 5A (0.5 nm) even separates n-hexane from branched alkanes (octane boosting), and 13X (1.0 nm) grabs CO2. In a two-bed PSA oxygen concentrator, 13X favors nitrogen slightly - pressurized, nitrogen is held while oxygen streams through; depressurized, nitrogen leaves - home oxygen concentrators, aircraft fuel-tank inerting and hydrogen purification are all this duet. The phosphate-free agent in detergent is 4A zeolite: calcium and magnesium swap out for sodium and the water softens; in refineries ZSM-5's 0.55 nm ten-member-ring is the classic shape-selective catalyst - only straight chains fit the mouth and crack-isomerize, branched alkanes and aromatics are too big, and octane numbers rise on a molecular ruler. Water uptake is physical adsorption; bake at 200-350 C to regenerate, thousands of cycles. Drag pore size to see which molecules enter, drag temperature along the loading curve; press PSA oxygen for the two-bed duet, ion exchange for the calcium-sodium swap, shape-selective catalysis to watch straight chains enter. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 铝硅酸盐骨架(球棍模型:Si/Al 两种球 + 氧桥),中央大笼与可调孔窗(氧环);各类分子(水/乙醇/氮气/氧气/正己烷/异辛烷/CO₂)飞向孔窗,进门或弹开;骨架中阳离子(金色)可被交换;右侧双塔 PSA(压力表交替);底部洗涤剂场景小图。) ✅ **zeolite-molecular-sieve/**

### Phase 80 · Cross-Family Gap-Fill Batch 50 (24/24 complete)



- [x] Leaf Springs (Stack a few curved steel plates and you have a load carrier and a damper in one: the main leaf rolls into eyes at both ends, bushed on pins to the frame; shorter leaves stack beneath, all clamped by a center bolt and strapped to the axle with U-bolts. When the wheel kicks up, force flows in through the eyes and the pack flattens - arc height shrinks, stiffness rises, storing the bump as elastic energy. The magic is between the leaves: as the pack bends, the layers must slip past each other, and dry steel-on-steel friction burns a large share of the vibration into heat on the spot - the spring is its own shock absorber, which is why old trucks squeak through potholes. Leaf count is a built-in variable-stiffness switch: empty, only the main and first short leaves work, so the ride stays soft; fully loaded, the shorter leaves join the bending game and stiffness climbs with payload - one spring serves both the empty run and the overloaded one. The price is stiction: small jolts get locked by friction and passed straight to the body, which is why modern cars moved to coil springs plus hydraulic dampers, leaving leaf packs to trucks and off-roaders - simple, overload-tolerant, and field-repairable one leaf at a time. Drag the load to watch arc height and stiffness change, drag the leaf count to see who takes the bending; press bump strike for the energy ledger, spring eye closeup for how the ends leave room to slip, interleaf friction to watch vibration burn into heat. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 一叠渐短钢板(主片卷耳+中心螺栓+骑马螺栓)压在车桥上;过坎时整叠压扁、片端滑移闪红发热;弧高-刚度标尺;与螺旋弹簧+减振器方案并排对比。) ✅ **leaf-spring/**


- [x] The Self-Centering Chuck (A chuck must answer a tricky question: how do three jaws all arrive at the exact center at once? The answer is the scroll hidden under them: a disc machined with an Archimedean spiral groove on its face, each jaw carrying a row of teeth engaged with that same groove, spaced 120 degrees apart. Turn the key, a bevel gear spins the scroll, and because the spiral's radius grows linearly with angle, all three jaws slide radially in the same instant - one groove, one tooth pitch, concentric by construction: gripping a raw bar leaves only 0.05-0.15 mm of runout, which is why the three-jaw self-centering chuck is the lathe's default workholder. Its errors come from the same groove: uneven tooth wear, a chip caught between jaw and scroll, or indexing error in the scroll itself all amplify runout - precision work switches to a four-jaw independent chuck tuned against a dial indicator to 0.01 mm, or cuts soft jaws in place so the bore grows truly concentric with its own spindle. Grip force has its own ledger: the key multiplies hand force about fortyfold, but centrifugal force flings the jaws outward as speed rises - at high rpm the grip thins, and heavy cuts demand a speed ceiling. Drag the key angle to open and close all three jaws in sync, drag the workpiece diameter to travel the jaws; press scroll closeup to watch teeth ride the spiral groove, chucking error to see a chip manufacture runout. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 卡盘剖视:盘丝(阿基米德螺旋槽发光)、三只带齿卡爪错开 120°、锥齿轮与扳手孔;中心夹持旋转棒料,跳动表盘实时显示;嵌入铁屑时爪行程异常、跳动变大。) ✅ **lathe-chuck/**


- [x] Hydraulic Accumulators (A hydraulic system fears two things: a pump whose flow surges and stalls, and a blackout that freezes every actuator mid-stroke. The accumulator is the circuit's power bank: a pressure-rated steel shell holds a nitrogen-filled bladder, oil port at the bottom - oil will not compress, gas will, so the nitrogen cushion banks the pump's high-pressure oil while the gas squeezes down and its pressure climbs the gas law; the instant an actuator wants a gulp - mold clamping, braking, boom lift - the valve opens and the nitrogen spring shoves the oil out in a flood, letting a small pump feed a monster's appetite. It is also the circuit's stabilizer: piston pumps pulse with every revolution, and the accumulator catches the peaks to fill the troughs, shaving the sawteeth off the line pressure; water hammer from a slammed valve or a dead pump is absorbed by the same compressible cushion. Emergency hold is its sternest duty: mains fail, pump stops, and the accumulator alone keeps the clamp pressurized - the mold stays shut, the workpiece stays put; circuit-breaker mechanisms and wind-turbine pitch systems all count on this bottle of nitrogen for their last act. The design ledger is one line: precharge sits near ninety percent of minimum working pressure, and the ratio of working to precharge pressure decides how much oil it can give back - what the bladder stores is energy, billed by the gas equation. Drag precharge pressure to see deliverable oil change, drag pump flow to pace the charge; press charge for the gas squeezing, fast dump for the beast unleashed, pulsation damping to watch sawteeth flatten, blackout hold to see who keeps the pressure when the lights die. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 立式钢瓶剖视:上部黄色氮气皮囊、下部油腔(蓝色)与油口阀;充压时皮囊压缩、压力表爬升;释放时油涌向执行油缸;管路压力示波显示锯齿被削平;断电瞬间泵停、皮囊续压。) ✅ **hydraulic-accumulator/**


- [x] Olefin Metathesis (Two alkenes dance a partner swap: the two halves of their C=C bonds exchange - A=B plus C=D becomes A=C plus B=D, carbon pairs reshuffled with the electron books exactly balanced. This is olefin metathesis, and for twenty years chemists could not see how a bond that strong could just swap partners. In 1971 Chauvin supplied the answer: the catalyst does not crack the double bond - it arrives carrying its own metal-carbon double bond (a metal carbene), performs a [2+2] cycloaddition with the alkene into a four-membered metallacyclobutane, and when that ring breaks apart, it breaks at the other seam: the carbene leaves with one half of the alkene and hands the other half to the leftover fragment - one exchange done, the catalyst restored, ready for the next round. Grubbs swapped in a ruthenium carbene - stable in air, tolerant of water and alcohols - and from the 1990s the dance moved into total synthesis and drug plants; Schrock's molybdenum versions trade stability for raw activity. The 2005 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to the three of them. Metathesis has a party trick, ring-closing: a chain wearing an alkene at each end swaps partners within itself and bites its own tail into a five-, six- or seven-membered ring; refineries run self-metathesis to reshuffle propylene into ethylene and 2-butene, moving carbon skeletons to where the market wants them. Drag reaction progress to walk one exchange end to end, drag catalyst loading to count turnovers; press partner swap for the ring opening and closing, ring-closing metathesis to watch a chain bite its tail, self-metathesis for the propylene reshuffle. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 两条彩色烯烃(双键发光)与钌卡宾催化剂(橙色 Ru=);[2+2] 环加成生成四元金属环丁烷(高亮),再开环换伴;产物飞离、催化剂复原循环;侧栏显示周转计数与产物比例。) ✅ **olefin-metathesis/**


- [x] Electrodialysis Desalination (Stack alternating sheets of plastic film - one passable only to cations, one only to anions - apply DC across the pile, and salt water splits itself into fresh and brine in the gaps between membranes. That is electrodialysis: anion-exchange membranes admit only anions, cation-exchange membranes only cations, and the electric field does the hauling. Sodium ions run toward the cathode, pass a cation membrane into a chamber, then hit an anion membrane they cannot cross - stuck; chloride ions run the other way and are stopped by a cation membrane - so alternate chambers leak ions only outward and turn fresh, while their neighbors admit only and turn brine. Where reverse osmosis pushes water through under pressure, electrodialysis hauls salt, not water - which makes it the tool for mid- and low-salinity feeds like brackish water and hard groundwater: the leaner the brine, the cheaper the kilowatt-hours, roughly linear in salt removed; seawater stays reverse osmosis's home turf. The weakness is concentration polarization: push the current too hard and ions arrive at the membrane faster than the bulk can supply them, water splits into hydrogen and hydroxide, and the alkaline boundary layer precipitates calcium and magnesium scale right on the membrane - recovery collapses. The fixes are running below the limiting current, or reversing the polarity every few tens of minutes (EDR): freshly nucleated scale redissolves in the new regime and the stack cleans itself. The membranes are also promiscuous: whey demineralization, amino-acid separation, acid and base recovery from waste streams - change the feed, keep the stack. Drag working voltage to watch ion traffic and recovery, drag feed salinity for the energy ledger; press desalting run to see fresh and brine part ways, polarization to watch scale nucleate, polarity reversal to watch it dissolve away. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 膜堆立体剖视:交替排列的阳膜(蓝)/阴膜(橙)、隔网水流通道;Na⁺(蓝球)与 Cl⁻(绿球)在电场箭头下分道;淡水流与浓水流颜色渐变;极化时膜面闪白结垢,倒极后垢层溶解。) ✅ **electrodialysis/**


- [x] Hot-Dip Galvanizing (The cheapest anti-rust recipe is a pool of zinc at 450 degrees Celsius: degreased, pickled and fluxed steel goes in whole, iron and zinc react at the interface and grow a stack of iron-zinc alloy layers (the Gamma, Delta and Zeta phases locked together), and a coat of nearly pure zinc comes out on the surface - not paint laid on top but metallurgy grown in, hard to scratch through. Zinc's cleverness is that it does not protect by blocking but by sacrificing itself: zinc is the more active metal, so at a scratch or cut edge the surrounding zinc becomes the anode, oxidizing first and feeding electrons to the exposed iron until its rusting has no current left - a few millimetres of bare edge can be guarded for a decade or more by a coating only tens of microns thick: sacrificial anode protection, plated. The ledger is equally plain: hot-dip coatings run 50-150 microns, last 20-50 years outdoors, and cost a fraction of stainless; but keep the kettle below 480 degrees - above that the iron-zinc reaction runs away, the alloy layer turns thick and brittle, and the coating flakes at a knock (high-silicon steels are the worst offenders, tamed by temperature control and a little aluminum in the bath). The biggest tonnage is continuous: strip dipped on the fly becomes the galvanized sheet under car bodies and appliance panels, while fabrications - guardrails, transmission towers, lampposts - take the batch route and keep the frozen drip patterns of the zinc as it cooled. Drag dip time to watch the alloy layers thicken, drag bath temperature for reaction speed and brittleness risk; press kettle dip for the full run, coating cross-section for the five-layer stack, cut-edge protection to watch zinc die guarding a scratch, rust comparison for the fork in the road. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 锌池(银灰色液面冒烟)上钢构件吊入浸没;剖面特写:钢基体→Γ/δ/ζ 合金层→η 纯锌层逐层生长;切口处锌层发亮牺牲、电子流动画;对照未镀钢材红锈蔓延。) ✅ **hot-dip-galvanizing/**


- [x] The Golgi Apparatus (Proteins leaving the ER are rough stock; the Golgi is the finishing shop: four or five flattened sacs (cisternae) stacked into a platform, its convex cis face toward the ER, its concave trans face toward the membrane. Cargo arrives at cis in COPII vesicles and crosses the stack like a workpiece on a line: each cisterna hosts a different cast of glycosyltransferases that add, trim and edit the sugar chains - high-mannose trimmed to hybrid then matured to complex, galactose and sialic acid bolted on in order. At trans, finished proteins are packed and sorted: lysosomal enzymes get a mannose-6-phosphate address tag and ship in clathrin-coated vesicles, default cargo rides to the plasma membrane, and regulated secretors are warehoused in granules until the signal to fire. The organelle itself moves: vesicles merge at cis while buds leave at trans, and the membrane streams cis-to-trans like a belt - whether the cisternae are stationary stations or a maturing conveyor was argued for forty years, and the evidence now favors the conveyor: each cisterna matures in place while retrograde vesicles ferry the enzymes backward round after round to keep every station's job description intact. The Golgi is also quality control: misfolded proteins are held here and sent back, and wrongly glycosylated ones never leave the secretory path at all. Drag transport speed to set the line's pace, drag enzyme activity for glycan precision; press full cargo route to walk entry to shipping, glycan processing to watch sugars edited station by station, lysosome sorting to see the address tag decide, vesicle budding to watch membrane curl into a sphere. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 4-5 层扁平囊摞成的平台(cis 凸面/trans 凹面),ER 来的 COPII 小泡在 cis 并入;糖链(彩色串珠)逐层被修剪延长;trans 面三种囊泡分道:网格蛋白小泡(M6P 签)去溶酶体、默认小泡去细胞膜、分泌颗粒待命;酶逆行回送箭头。) ✅ **golgi-apparatus/**


- [x] Angiogenesis (When tissue runs short of oxygen it raises a chemical alarm: HIF-1 stabilizes, switches on the VEGF gene, and vascular endothelial growth factor spreads through the tissue as a trail of increasing concentration - the nearest capillary reads the gradient and grows toward it. This is angiogenesis. The point of the spear is the tip cell, waving a thicket of filopodia like noses, sniffing the VEGF gradient and digesting matrix to clear the way; stalk cells behind it proliferate, hollow out a lumen between them, and a new vessel takes shape; sprouts from different directions finally fuse with existing vessels (anastomosis), blood flows in, oxygen returns, HIF switches off, VEGF is withdrawn, and growth stops - a precision negative feedback loop. Tumors hijack it: the tumor core is chronically hypoxic, VEGF runs at full blast, and vessels grow wildly but badly - twisted, leaky, stagnant - supplying the tumor rather than the tissue; anti-VEGF antibodies and small-molecule kinase inhibitors cut the alarm wire to starve the tumor, now part of standard therapy in colorectal and lung cancer. Wound healing, rebuilding the uterine lining each cycle, and crowding muscle with new capillaries in training all run the same program; in diabetic retinas the same program runs away, and lasers seal the ischemic zones to stop it. Drag hypoxia level to shape the VEGF field and sprout speed, drag drug dose to watch sprouting suppressed; press sprouting for the tip-and-stalk division of labor, anastomosis for the two-front connection and first flow, tumor vasculature for the chaotic overgrowth, anti-angiogenic therapy for vessels retreating. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 组织块中既有血管(红管)+缺氧核心(紫雾 VEGF 浓度场);尖细胞(发光)伸出丝状伪足探路、柄细胞列队增殖拉出管腔;吻合瞬间血流(红粒子)涌入;肿瘤模式下血管扭曲杂乱;加药后新芽回缩。) ✅ **angiogenesis/**


- [x] Alcohol Metabolism (Alcohol does not take fat's storage route in the body - it must be destroyed on the spot in the liver: ethanol to acetaldehyde to acetate, two oxidations with no detour. Alcohol dehydrogenase runs the first step, oxidizing ethanol into acetaldehyde - the true villain: it dilates vessels (the flush), damages DNA and sits on carcinogen lists; aldehyde dehydrogenase ALDH2 then oxidizes acetaldehyde to acetate within moments, and acetate enters energy metabolism or becomes fat. The bottleneck is the second step: roughly a third of East Asians carry an ALDH2 variant (rs671) with only a few percent of normal activity - even a small drink piles up acetaldehyde, bringing flushing, palpitations and headache: the body saying outright that this machine cannot process the load. The whole system's speedometer is tiny: ADH works at a nearly fixed rate of 7-10 grams of alcohol per hour no matter how much you pour - zero-order kinetics, blood concentration just has to wait; a glass of wine (about 14 grams) takes over an hour, a serious binge takes a night. The accumulated NADH also derails metabolism: fat synthesis accelerates, fatty-acid oxidation stalls, and the liver of a heavy drinker goes fatty, then inflamed, then fibrotic; the induced CYP2E1 bypass generates extra acetaldehyde and free radicals. No pill speeds these enzymes - caffeine only leaves you awake while drunk; what works is time and dose. Drag drink size to watch BAC climb and creep back down, drag ALDH2 activity to pile up acetaldehyde; press normal metabolism for the two-step relay, acetaldehyde buildup for the flush mechanism, chronic drinking for how fatty liver arrives, empty stomach for the absorption difference. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Vortex Tube (A tube with no moving parts, fed compressed air, blowing heat above 100 degrees out one end and cold down to -40 out the other - the vortex tube (Ranque-Hilsch) is thermodynamics' closest thing to a magic trick: air jets in tangentially and spins against the wall at on the order of a million rpm toward the hot end, while the core flow is forced to reverse and escapes through the central orifice - that core is the cold stream. How does energy split? Explanations are still argued, but the accepted picture is shear: the fast outer vortex rubs hard against the inner layers, redistributing energy while its tangential speed decays along the tube through adiabatic expansion and acoustic streaming - the shell ends up hotter, the core colder, and within one tube the two ends differ by 50-70 degrees. Its efficiency is humble (a few to a dozen percent isentropic), but it wins on having nothing to wear out, instant start, and air instead of refrigerant: spot-cooling weld torch tips, personal cooling at hot workstations, sample conditioning for gas analyzers, portable cooling down mines. The little valve at the hot end is the only knob: screw it in or out to change the hot-flow backpressure and split the cold fraction anywhere from 20 to 80 percent - temperature difference and cold output trade off across its travel. Drag inlet pressure for swirl speed and ΔT, drag the hot-valve for the split; press cold-hot split to watch the streams part, temperature profile for the radial gradient inside, cold-fraction tuning to see the valve redistribute, versus refrigerator for the efficiency gap. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 卧式管剖视:切向喷嘴(蓝)进气、贴壁红色高速旋涡流向热端、中央蓝色冷流从左端小孔反向流出;热端锥形阀可伸缩;管内粒子按温度着色(红热/蓝冷);两端温度计与 ΔT 表。) ✅ **vortex-tube/**


- [x] Elastocaloric Cooling (Yank a nickel-titanium shape-memory rod hard and it warms by itself; let it snap back and it chills by itself - not an illusion but the elastocaloric effect: stress-induced phase transition. Stretch austenite past a critical strain and it flips to martensite in a flash, dumping latent heat and jumping several degrees; unload it and martensite reverses, soaking the latent heat back up and dropping cold. Chain the four moves - stretch and reject heat to the hot side, relax and absorb heat from the cold side - and you have a refrigerator with no compressor: the working medium is a solid metal rod, with no refrigerant gas at all (nothing to deplete ozone or warm the planet), reversible temperature spans of 10-20 degrees, and prototypes already pumping tens to a hundred watts. Its opponent is its own lifetime: every cycle shears martensite variants back and forth, microcracks and strain localization accumulate, and performance fades over thousands to tens of thousands of cycles - fatigue stabilization (running tens of thousands of cycles up front until the material settles) and new single-crystal and nanocrystalline alloys are pushing that number up. Elastocaloric, magnetocaloric and electrocaloric are solid-state cooling's three brothers; the elastic one has the biggest effect and the simplest drive - a motor stretching a bar - and is the likeliest to reach a fridge or an air conditioner first. Drag applied strain to watch latent heat released and reabsorbed, drag cycle frequency for cooling power; press stretch heats for the temperature jump, relax cools for the chill, cooling cycle for the four-beat heat pump, fatigue stabilization for how performance fades and recovers. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Magnetron (The heart of a microwave oven is a vacuum tube the size of your palm with no grids and no deflection plates - just an electric field, a magnetic field, and an electron cloud that organizes itself into spokes: the magnetron. Structurally a copper flower: an electron-emitting cathode at the center ringed by an even number of resonant cavities, with a magnetic field threaded along the axis. The filament heats the cathode, electrons start outward under the radial field, and the axial field bends them sideways with the Lorentz force - pushed out while curled around, they can only trace cycloids around the cathode: crossed fields (E perpendicular to B) lock straight motion into rotation. The rotating cloud quickly destabilizes into a few spokes that revolve in step with the field; as each spoke sweeps past the cavity gaps it hands energy to the cavities' oscillation, at a frequency set by their dimensions - tuned to 2.45 GHz, with efficiency of 60-70 percent and a kilowatt of microwaves from one tube. The pi mode - adjacent cavities oscillating in opposition - is the workhorse: electrons parked between cavities sit in the decelerating phase and surrender their kinetic energy in full. Water absorbs this band superbly (dipoles cannot keep up with 2.45 billion field reversals a second, writing heat directly into the food), which is part of why the frequency was chosen. Drag anode voltage for cloud and spoke speed, drag field strength for the cycloid radius; press electron spokes to watch the rotating pattern form, pi mode for cavities oscillating in opposition, microwave output for the antenna feeding the waveguide, oven coupling for standing waves and the turntable. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Bullet Cluster (Two galaxy clusters crashed head-on over three hundred million years ago, leaving a snapshot of dark matter caught in the act: 1E 0657-56, nicknamed the Bullet Cluster. The collision ran on three tracks: the galaxies, only a few percent of the mass, passed through like two flocks of birds that never touch; the hot gas, the bulk of ordinary matter when seen in X-rays (pink), slammed together - tenuous but enormous, the two clouds braked like fluids meeting, stranded mid-field with a bow shock riding the front; and the mass mapped by gravitational lensing (blue) sailed on to both sides - most of the weight sits neither in the galaxies nor in the gas, something dark, frictionless, that crossed its counterpart almost untouched. Mass that behaves that way is dark matter: gravity only, colliding with nothing. The picture closes the standard escape hatch that dark matter is an illusion of wrong gravity: if the force law were at fault, the mapped mass should track the light (galaxies) or the gas; instead the mass peaks align with neither - the only consistent reading is invisible stuff that went through first. Nor is the Bullet alone: a dozen colliding systems found since show the same gas-versus-mass separation. Drag collision progress to run the three tracks, drag dark-matter fraction to move the mass peaks; press the crash to watch gas brake while dark matter passes, lensing map to see background galaxies distort, X-ray map for the shock front, peak offset for mass and light out of register. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] Type Ia Supernovae (The universe has one explosion that always shines with nearly the same light: the Type Ia supernova. The script is a white dwarf's self-destruction: a white dwarf holds itself up with electron degeneracy pressure, which does not scale with mass - the heavier the star, the harder the electrons are squeezed, until the Chandrasekhar limit of 1.4 solar masses, where degeneracy can no longer pay. Give it a companion that keeps feeding it (accretion) and the dwarf queues at the limit's door; the moment it crosses, core carbon ignites, fusion in degenerate matter races away with temperature faster than expansion can vent the heat, and a thermonuclear runaway sweeps the whole star in seconds - no neutron star is left behind. The key is that this limit is a constant of physics: every Type Ia carries nearly the same mass at detonation, so nearly the same peak luminosity (about five billion suns), rising to maximum in about twenty days and fading slowly - and brighter events linger longer (the Phillips relation), which lets the light-curve shape self-calibrate intrinsic brightness; intrinsic brightness against observed flux, distance falls out. In 1998 two teams used dozens of fainter-than-expected distant Type Ia's to find the universe accelerating - dark energy entered the stage, and the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics went to the observers. Drag accretion rate to approach the limit, drag redshift z to place supernovae on the Hubble diagram; press approaching the limit for accretion at the gate, detonation for the runaway spreading, light curve for the standard candle's self-calibration, Hubble diagram for the acceleration evidence. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Matter-Antimatter Asymmetry (The Big Bang should have made matter and antimatter in equal measure - in accelerators, energy always boils into particle-antiparticle pairs. Yet antimatter is nearly extinct today: one baryon per billion photons. Had the early universe been exactly symmetric, the annihilation storm would have left nothing but a sea of light - you would not exist. Something, in the first minutes, tipped the balance by a hair. Sakharov listed the three necessary conditions in 1967: baryon number violation (some process edits the matter ledger), C and CP violation (the laws do not treat matter and mirror-antimatter quite alike), and departure from thermal equilibrium (reactions too slow to smooth the imbalance away). All three exist in the Standard Model, all too weakly: the CP violation measured in kaon and B-meson oscillations, where particle and antiparticle decay along slightly different paths, suffices to leave one extra baryon per billion pairs - exactly today's ratio. Expansion did the rest: the universe cooled too fast, annihilation froze out with the surplus matter unable to find partners, and the surviving one-part-in-a-billion stock lasted to become stars, planets and you. The microscopic mechanism is still being dug for: the CP phase in neutrino oscillations, the strong CP problem, whether the electroweak transition was first order - the hottest ground where particle physics meets cosmology. Drag initial asymmetry to set the survivors, drag universe temperature for the annihilation window; press annihilation storm for pairs flashing out of existence, one in a billion for the survivors, CP violation for the mesons' lopsided oscillation, freeze-out for how annihilation stops. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 膨胀的宇宙盒子:正物质(蓝)与反物质(红)粒子成对诞生、相遇湮灭闪光;比例尺显示重子/光子比从 1:1 跌到 10⁻⁹;CP 破坏环节:介子振荡路径偏向物质侧;温度下降后湮灭停止、蓝点幸存聚团。) ✅ **matter-antimatter-asymmetry/**


- [x] The Fish Ladder (A dam is a sheer wall to a migrating fish: a salmon can burst-jump two metres but not twenty, and the fish ladder's idea is to cut one wall into a hundred steps - pools linked by weirs or vertical slots, each drop only 10-25 centimetres, one jump, one rest, then the next. Design bows to the fish's ability ledger: burst speed (salmon over 6 m/s, sustainable for seconds) and sustained speed (1-2 m/s, sustainable indefinitely) are different budgets; slot velocity must stay comfortably under the sustained figure, drops under the jump and oxygen-debt limits, and each pool must hold a slow corner to rest in. Vertical-slot ladders (the Nordic standard) pass flow over full depth and suit mixed communities of swimmers; pool-and-weir (the North American classic) uses plunging water with a loud attraction flow; nature-like rock-ramp ladders trade efficiency for landscape. The most neglected part is the entrance: fish circle below the dam hunting a way in, and if the entrance lacks a strong attraction flow (ladder discharge is often only 1-5 percent of river flow) they never find the door - many failed ladders failed at the signpost, not the stairs. Acceptance is blunt: PIT tags and cameras count the fish, and good ladders pass over 80 percent end to end while poor ones manage under 20. Drag head difference to set the number of steps, drag drop per pool for velocity against fish limits; press ascent to watch shoals leap pool by pool, slot closeup for the velocity field, attraction flow for how the entrance advertises itself, too steep to see fish turned back by overrun velocity. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] Debris Flows (Rain turns a dry gully into a mud tank when four ingredients line up: a steep channel bed (10-30 degrees), plenty of loose solid material (old slides, colluvium), high-intensity rain in a short window, and the water to mix them. Debris flow density reaches 1.8-2.3 tonnes per cubic metre - close to concrete - and its mechanics run on a different ledger: coarse grains colliding generate dispersive stress that floats boulders in the slurry (rocks ride the crest like corks), while clay and silt balloon the slurry's yield strength, so a stopped flow sits in the gully like dough instead of spreading thin like water. Motion comes in surges: one event may carry dozens to hundreds of waves, the head 2-5 metres tall with boulders tumbling along the crest, at 5-15 m/s and an impact force ten-odd times a flood of the same speed - a one-metre block striking a check dam at 8 m/s delivers a hundred tonnes. Defense is three layers: stabilize upstream (pin the slopes, starve the solids), trap midstream (gabion and slot dams catch the coarse, pass the fine, bleeding off energy in stages), drain downstream (a discharge channel hands the residue to the main river without silting); monitoring adds a last alarm with rainfall thresholds and infrasound - the rumble the flow's head makes grinding down the gully. Drag rainfall intensity for the initiation threshold, drag channel slope for head growth; press initiation for rain prying the slope loose, surging head for boulders afloat on the crest, check dam for catch-the-big-pass-the-small, versus flood for what density does to impact. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] Crosswind Landings (Crosswind landing is every pilot's final exam: ten to fifteen knots blowing across the runway, and the aircraft must fly forward without drifting off the centerline. The mainstream method is the crab: point the nose upwind so the plane flies slightly sideways - the nose offset exactly cancels the drift and the track stays straight down the runway; at the last instant before touchdown, rudder straightens the nose while aileron drops the upwind wing - the de-crab - and the main gear kisses down first. A handy approximation: about three degrees of crab per five knots of crosswind component. The alternative is the sideslip: wing held low into the wind with opposite rudder the whole way down - stable, but passengers feel a continuous bank and large angles risk scraping an engine pod, so airlines favor the crab. Limits are an honest ledger: every type has a demonstrated crosswind limit (say 35-40 knots), a maximum shown in certification rather than a structural wall; the real physics is the side load at touchdown - the tires must absorb the entire lateral kinetic energy in an instant - plus how much roll authority the ailerons have left against the wind. Gusts and shear keep changing the correction, so a good pilot trims continuously through the last hundred feet instead of fixing it once. Drag wind speed for crab angle and drift, drag wind angle for the component split; press crab approach to see the sideways flight, sideslip for the paired controls, touchdown instant for side load on one main gear, crosswind limit for correction running out. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] HyperLogLog Cardinality Estimation (Counting distinct visitors out of a billion, the exact way needs a hash set holding a billion IDs - gigabytes of memory; HyperLogLog does the same job in 12 KB with about 2 percent error, and its insight is one sentence: in uniformly random hash values, the number of leading zeros carries cardinality information. The bigger a set, the likelier some hash begins with a long run of zeros - see k leading zeros and the cardinality is probably on the order of 2^k. One observation is too noisy, so LogLog averages over buckets: the first few bits of each hash route the element to one of m buckets (say 16384), and each bucket keeps a single number - the longest leading-zero run it has seen; a harmonic mean then aggregates all buckets, chosen because it tolerates outlier buckets. HyperLogLog patches two edges - linear counting when many buckets are empty (small cardinalities) and a bias-correction table for large ones - cutting the error to about 1.04 over the square root of m while storing no elements at all. In production it is Redis's PFADD/PFCOUNT, Google's PowerDrill, and every database's approximate COUNT(DISTINCT) - all the massive unique-visitor tallies are trading two percent accuracy for twelve kilobytes. Its opposite-number sibling is the Bloom filter: that one answers 'have I seen it', this one answers 'how many'. Drag element count to track the estimate hugging truth, drag bucket count m for the accuracy-memory trade; press hash routing to watch the prefix split, register update for the longest zero-run, harmonic estimate for the aggregation, versus exact for the memory gap. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 元素流(发光方块)经哈希变成二进制串;前缀路由到 m 列桶;每列一个寄存器柱显示最大前导零;调和平均仪表实时输出估计值与真值曲线;内存对比条:哈希集合 GB 级 vs HLL 12 KB。) ✅ **hyperloglog/**


- [x] Two-Phase Commit (One transfer must update two databases - all-or-nothing across machines. How is that 'all' guaranteed? Two-phase commit's answer is a coordinator that owns the decision. Phase one, prepare: the coordinator asks every participant 'can you commit?' and each writes an undo log to disk before answering yes or no - yes is a promise with a safety catch: from that instant it can commit or roll back, but must stay parked until phase two. Phase two, commit: all yes votes and the coordinator broadcasts commit and everyone takes effect; a single no or timeout broadcasts rollback and everyone undoes. The protocol is simple; its infamy lives in the failure modes. The cruelest cut: a participant answers yes, then the coordinator vanishes - the participant holds locks, may not commit alone, may not roll back alone (it cannot know how the others voted), and freezes in the in-doubt state waiting for the coordinator to wake - the blocking that Raft-style consensus and highly available coordinators exist to cure. Second cruelest: the coordinator dies just before writing its commit record - on restart it replays the log and re-sends the decision, which is why 'log before message' is 2PC's lifeline. The bill: at least two round trips, one extra fsync on every participant, latency three times a local commit - and distributed databases from MongoDB 4.0 to TiKV's Percolator variant ship its descendants built in. Drag failure timing to place each crash on the timeline, drag node count for the message bill; press normal commit for the full two acts, participant crash for in-doubt blocking, coordinator crash for log-replay recovery, abort for one no sending everyone back. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 顶部协调者节点+下方参与者节点(数据库图标);阶段一 prepare 消息(绿)逐个飞出、各节点写 undo 日志闪盘图标后回票;阶段二 commit(金)/rollback(红)广播;宕机场景节点变灰、in-doubt 锁图标挂起;消息计数器与状态机面板。) ✅ **two-phase-commit/**


- [x] The Secretary Problem (You hire one secretary from a hundred applicants who arrive one by one; at each interview you must hire on the spot or say goodbye forever, and your whole score is the probability of hiring the single best. Interview everyone and the best may already be gone; decide early and something better may follow. The optimal answer, worked out in the 1960s, is startlingly elegant: observe the first n/e - about 37 percent - hiring none, recording only the best so far; then take the first later candidate who beats everyone seen before. The success probability of this policy is exactly 1/e - about 36.8 percent - and that is not a passing grade but the ceiling no strategy can beat: in a world where information only flows one way, two-thirds of the outcome is not yours to control. The mathematics is dynamic programming: with an observation window r, the probability of winning is P(r) = (r/n) times the sum of 1/k from r to n-1, and maximizing it drives r/n to 1/e as n grows. The same skeleton answers everyday questions - how many apartments to view before renting, how many people to date before settling - under the assumptions of random arrival and caring only about first place; change the goal to 'any acceptable one' and both strategy and odds shift. The 1960 model now lives inside optimal stopping theory, the shared frame of auction bidding and asset selling. Drag candidate count n to move the 37 percent line, drag window r to trace the success curve; press single run to watch one quality sequence and its decision, success curve for the hump of P(r), thousand runs to watch frequency converge on 36.8, omniscient for the gap to perfect hindsight. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] The Hair Dryer (A hair dryer packs a motor, a fan and a 1000-2000 watt coil of nichrome into a shell the size of your hand, and must never set your hair on fire - its circuit is one sentence: heating element and motor in parallel, a switch in each branch. Cool setting powers the fan alone, pushing room-temperature air through; hot setting adds the element, its resistance sized to the power (1200 W is about 40 ohms), and forced convection carries the heat out at 60-100 degrees. The real engineering lives in the safety chain: a bimetal thermostat (tripping near 90-120 degrees) and a one-shot thermal fuse sit in series with the element - block the air inlet with hair, outlet temperature blows past the setpoint within seconds, the bimetal opens and resets as it cools; if it fails, the fuse melts, the dryer is dead but the house is fine. Airflow and heat are conjugate knobs: the same wire with more air runs a cooler nozzle, and with little air the temperature runs away into protection - which is why classic dryers offer two heat settings (a series diode's half wave, or a tapped resistor) rather than stepless temperature. Premium models swap in a brushless motor: hundred-thousand-rpm-class speed, double the airflow, lower noise, with a thermistor closing the loop on the wire for high-flow low-heat drying that is fast and gentle. Drag airflow for the nozzle temperature trade, drag heat setting for the power split; press cool for fan only, hot for glowing wire and warm wind, overheat protection for the tripped thermostat after a blocked inlet, brushless comparison for the high-speed motor's ledger. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 吹风机纵向剖视:进风格栅、电机+风扇、螺旋镍铬丝(通电发红)、云母支架、出风口;空气流粒子由蓝变红;双金属片与熔断器在加热支路上高亮;堵塞演示时风粒子骤减、丝温红闪、温控跳开。) ✅ **hair-dryer/**


- [x] Uninterruptible Power Supplies (When the mains die for half a second, who holds up the server? A UPS answers in three grades. Standby (offline) is the simplest: mains feeds the load directly while the UPS trickle-charges its battery; at a blackout a relay clicks over to the inverter, and battery DC becomes AC again - 4-10 milliseconds of gap, which a PC power supply's capacitors shrug off but precision instruments blink at. Line-interactive adds an AVR tap transformer: sags are corrected by switching taps without leaving bypass mode, and only a true outage triggers the transfer - it treats voltage sag, the grid's more common disease than blackouts. Double-conversion online is the expensive steady one: mains is always rectified to DC and inverted back to AC, so every watt the load sees is remade by the UPS - surges, frequency drift and harmonics never reach through, transfer time is zero by construction, and the price is 5-10 percent lost in the two conversions plus a fan that never sleeps. The battery is the real ledger: one 12 V 7 Ah lead-acid brick stores about 84 watt-hours, good for a dozen-odd minutes on a 300 W PC - a UPS is not built for the long run but for holding until you save your file or the generator catches; in data centers the UPS relays to diesel, one covering minutes, the other hours. Lithium and supercapacitors are replacing lead: lifetime from 3-5 years to 10, a thousand cycles, half the volume. Drag mains voltage to watch each type react, drag load power for runtime; press standby transfer for the relay click and waveform notch, line-interactive for the AVR taps, double conversion for the rectifier-inverter pair, battery runtime for the discharge curve. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] X-ray Baggage Scanners (An airport scanner sees through your bag in seconds with an eye that draws lines: the belt carries luggage under lead curtains, an X-ray tube below fans out a beam, and a detector row directly above receives it - one inch of travel, one line of picture, a fax machine building a full image. What lets the operator sort materials is dual energy: the same detector column samples at two tube voltages (or two scintillator layers), so every pixel carries two attenuation readings - at higher energy photoelectric absorption fades while Compton scattering holds, and the heavier the element, the steeper that ratio shifts; inverting the ratio yields an effective atomic number, and each pixel gets a material tag: organics (water, plastics, explosives) in orange, mixed in green, metals and inorganics in blue. Shape recognition comes on top: explosives and narcotics have signature outlines and densities, and the algorithm overlays red alarm boxes for the operator to zoom, flip and slice through three views. The dose ledger is restrained: one bag pass delivers about 0.1-1 microgray - a banana's natural radioactivity gives you more; the party actually shielded is the operator - lead under the source plus the curtain tunnel hold leakage to background levels. The difference from medical CT is the viewpoint: security is single-view projection (everything superimposed), CT alone rotates and reconstructs in 3D, so overlapping objects are the operator's daily puzzle. Drag belt speed for the line-by-line rhythm, drag tube voltage for penetration versus contrast; press line-scan imaging to watch the fan draw, dual-energy coloring for the orange-green-blue tags, threat overlay for the alarm boxes, lead curtains for rays stopped inside the tunnel. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] 履带行走装置 (What keeps a sixty-tonne tank from drowning where a wheeled truck buries its axles is ground pressure: spread over two endless tracks totalling about 5.2 square meters of contact, the weight works out to roughly 110 kPa - the same order as a walking adult. Each track is a closed loop of pinned shoes; the drive sprocket never rolls on the ground - it works like a winch, reeling the road up from the front, laying it under the wheels and collecting it at the tail, so every wheel on board rolls inside the track and never touches dirt. A front idler with a crank tensioner keeps the sag out, five road wheels pass the weight down through torsion-bar arms, and return rollers stop the top run from whipping. On soft ground area alone is not enough: transverse grousers shear the soil like boat oars - thrust comes from shearing the ground, not gripping it. Steering is the party trick: slow one side and the hull pivots around that track; reverse it and the tank spins on its own center - a zero turning radius no wheeled vehicle can match. Drag track speed to watch the loop wind and the ground slide back, drag steering ratio to swing from wide arcs to a spin on the spot; press straight drive to see the winch lay road, pivot turn for the zero-radius about-face, soft-soil cross-country for grouser shear and sink, sprocket close-up to watch the teeth mesh. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] 铆接连接 (Before welding took over, steel structures were stitched by millions of rivets: heated to 1000-1100 C, slipped red-hot into aligned holes, hammered until the soft shank swelled and filled them, the tail pounded into a closing head - and the step that really tightens the joint uses no tools at all: cooling. The shrinking shank clamps the plates with a preload near 0.6 times yield strength, so plate friction carries the load first; past the friction limit the joint slips a hair and the shanks go into shear, turning from clamps into pins. The designer keeps three failure ledgers at once: shank shear, hole bearing that ovalizes the hole, and a net-section tear along the rivet line - pitch at 3-4 diameters and edge distance at 2 leave margin on all three. Temperature is the hidden variable: Titanic's plates were riveted with iron, some of which went brittle in ice-sea cold and cracked along hole edges. Aviation gave riveting a second stage: aluminum cannot be welded without annealing and distortion, the Boeing 747 carries about 3 million rivets, countersunk heads vanish into dimpled skin, and cold-worked hole edges resist fatigue - crack one, replace one. Drag tensile load to watch friction hand over to slip and shear, drag temperature to turn a ductile tear brittle; press hot riveting to see a red-hot shank tighten as it cools, load path to follow the force, three failure modes to compare the breaks, brittle fracture for the ice-sea link. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] 伸缩缝与膨胀补偿 (Steel's thermal expansion coefficient, α ≈ 11.7×10⁻⁶/°C, looks harmless until you multiply it by length: a 100 m steel beam warming 50 °C grows about 59 mm - with no gap, a summer beam shoves the abutment apart and track can snake into sun-kink buckling. The oldest fix is to leave a slot: comb joints on bridge decks, and the ~1 cm gaps between old short rails - the summer 'clack-clack' is wheels counting those slots. Continuously welded rail flips the logic: rails welded into 1-2 km strings, locked to the sleepers by strong fastenings, so thermal stress stays bottled inside - tension in winter (guard against breakage), compression in summer (guard against buckling), with 'stress dispersion' re-locking when it overshoots. Pipelines take a third road: the bellows expansion joint, a thin-walled tube with U-shaped corrugations, axially so soft it works like a metal spring, swallowing tens of millimetres of travel while still holding line pressure - travel versus pressure are its two ledgers, tuned by corrugation count and wall thickness. Tall buildings cut themselves in two with double-column joints mid-height, each half breathing with temperature on its own. The stiffer the restraint, the less the steel can grow and the harder the force bites: fully restrained, F = E·A·α·ΔT - a 60 kg/m rail gains about 17 kN per °C, nearly 700 kN by +40 °C, one critical temperature away from kinking the track. Drag ΔT to watch bridge, rail, bellows and thermometer breathe together, drag restraint stiffness to turn free growth into bottled-up force; press bridge & rail for comb and rail gaps, seamless rail for stress piling up around the locked rail temperature, bellows joint for corrugations closing one by one, track buckling for the rail twisting into a snake. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] 铃木偶联反应 (Stitching two carbon fragments into one C-C bond is the most valuable trick in synthesis chemistry - half the skeletons of drug molecules are welded this way, and the catalyst doing it most often is the Suzuki coupling, which earned Heck, Negishi and Suzuki the 2010 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. The catalytic cycle is a three-step dance: oxidative addition, where Pd(0) slips into the C-Br bond of an aryl bromide to give Ar-Pd(II)-Br, palladium rising from 0 to +2; transmetalation, where the base first deprotonates and primes the boronic acid, and only then will the aryl transfer from boron over to palladium, giving Ar-Pd(II)-Ar; and reductive elimination, where the two aryls join hands into a biaryl and Pd(0) is regenerated, ready for the next round. The base is the invisible hero: it primes the boronic acid and mops up HBr; starve it and the cycle stalls at transmetalation, yield collapsing on the spot. Its edge over the older Grignard reagent is temperament: Grignards tolerate neither water nor air - dry ether, nitrogen blanket, and one stray droplet kills them on the spot - while Suzuki runs in open air, even in water, leaving nothing but non-toxic boric acid and salts behind. That is why pharma runs it on ten-thousand-tonne lines - sartan blood-pressure drugs and anticancer agents carry bonds it welded - and materials chemists use it to weld the conjugated backbones of OLEDs. Drag base amount to keep the cycle flowing or stall it, drag temperature for the tempo; press catalytic cycle for the full dance, base at work for deprotonation and HBr mopping, vs Grignard to watch one droplet kill a Grignard reagent, industrial scale for the reactor turning out batches. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
- 场景要点: 分子舞台:中央亮球是带空配位的钯催化剂,右侧 Ar–Br 进场被钯插键闪光;下方蓝色碱小球拽走 H 活化苯硼酸,芳基从硼跳到钯、B(OH)₃ 离场,两个芳基牵手发光成联芳烃后离场,钯复位循环,计数器累计 TON;左角是干冰乙醚加氮气的格氏小剧场,水滴闯入即冒火花报废;右下是搅动的工业反应釜。) ✅ **suzuki-coupling/**


- [x] 蒸汽裂解制烯烃 (Ethylene is the staple food of the chemical industry - over 200 million tonnes a year, feeding plastic bags, antifreeze and PVC pipe - and about nine tenths of it comes from steam cracking: naphtha or ethane mixed with dilution steam races through furnace coils at about 850 °C for just 0.1-0.5 seconds. Heat snaps C-C bonds at random and radical hydrogen-transfer relays the cuts, chopping long alkanes into short alkenes like ethylene and propylene. The craft is a triangle of trade-offs: hotter favors alkene yield, but linger and the newborn ethylene cracks again into methane and coke - so high temperature, short residence and rapid quench must all hold at once; the effluent must plunge below 400 °C within milliseconds in a transfer-line exchanger, freezing the composition while the waste heat is recovered as high-pressure steam for turbines. Dilution steam runs its own ledger: it thins the hydrocarbon partial pressure, suppressing coke and lifting selectivity; even so coils foul within weeks and get decoked with steam and air. Feedstock is the big account: ethane yields about 80% ethylene, the frugal US shale-gas route; naphtha only about 30% but co-produces propylene, butadiene and aromatics, the Asia-Europe route - one furnace's feed choice sketches the global petrochemical map. Drag coil temperature to tilt the yield balance, drag residence time to watch secondary cracking; press crack reaction to watch beaded long chains get cut, quench & heat recovery for the millisecond chill and the steam turbine, coking & decoking for fouled walls making a fresh start, feed comparison for the ethane-versus-naphtha yield gap. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] 电石灯 (Before electric light reached the mines, a miner's headlamp burned a stone: calcium carbide, forged in an arc furnace at 2200 °C from lime and coke, which falls apart on contact with water - CaC2 + 2H2O -> C2H2 + Ca(OH)2 - releasing acetylene that burns at the nozzle with a brilliant flame. The lamp is a drip timer: the upper chamber holds water, a knob-metered valve lets it seep drop by drop onto the carbide below, and drip rate is the brightness dial - drip faster and the flame climbs, but the charge burns sooner too. Acetylene is carbon-rich, its flame full of glowing soot particles: far brighter than kerosene, nearly smokeless, and full-spectrum warm rather than blue-leaning like LED, so rock reads in fine layers - miners lit a century of tunnels with it, cavers mapped decades of caves by its light. But it has a temper: above about 2 atm acetylene decomposes explosively, and with copper or silver it forms shock-sensitive acetylides, so the lamp feeds gas at low pressure through a water seal and its gas path never touches copper. The deadliest error is a blown-out flame: steam snuffs the flame while the wet carbide keeps generating, acetylene accumulates past its lower explosive limit, and one spark brings a flash fire - so shut the valve, ventilate, and flush leftover carbide before cleaning the lime sludge. The hottest descendant of this lamp still works today: the oxyacetylene flame at about 3100 °C cutting steel plate. Drag drip rate to ride the flame, drag carbide level to watch the charge run down; press gas generation for the drip-react-burn chain, brightness dial for flame vs drip, cave exploration for the beam sweeping stalactites, misfire hazard for the blown-flame gas build-up. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause

- [x] 胎儿血液循环 (The fetus's lungs do no work - the placenta works the shift - so the fetal heart's biggest job is not pumping but routing blood around the lungs. The umbilical vein brings back blood at about 80% oxygen saturation, and on reaching the right atrium it takes the shortcuts: the ductus venosus bypasses the liver straight into the inferior vena cava; the foramen ovale leaks right-atrial blood into the left atrium to feed the brain and heart first; the ductus arteriosus reroutes the right-ventricular blood that should enter the lungs into the descending aorta, so only about 10% of cardiac output perfuses the lungs. Grabbing oxygen at the placenta is fetal hemoglobin HbF's trick: its dissociation curve sits left of the adult's, P50 near 19 mmHg against about 27, so at the same partial pressure HbF strips oxygen from maternal hemoglobin. Birth is a hard rerouting: the first breath inflates the alveoli, pulmonary vascular resistance collapses, lung flow leaps from a tenth to the whole right-heart output; the oxygen surge makes the ductus smooth muscle constrict and functionally closes it within 24-48 hours, while left atrial pressure overtakes the right and presses the foramen ovale's flap shut like a door. When the rerouting fails you get congenital heart disease: patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) keeps leaking aortic blood into the pulmonary artery, bringing cyanosis and heart failure - preterm infants get ibuprofen to block the prostaglandins holding the duct open, and in older children a closure device is implanted into the duct. Drag lung vascular resistance to watch lung flow collapse and surge, drag arterial O2 saturation to shift the blood color and the curve markers; press fetal loop for the default shortcuts, birth switch to see them flash and close one by one, PDA pathology for the persistent leak, HbF curve for the two S-curves side by side. 3D interactive demo - drag to orbit / scroll to zoom - Space = play/pause
